B.Correct because the expression for WACC is: WACC = w d r d (1 – t) + w p r p + w e r e , where w d = the target proportion of debt in the capital structure when the company raises new funds r d = the before-tax marginal cost of debt t = the company's marginal tax rate w p = the target proportion of preferred stock in the capital structure when the company raises new funds r p = the marginal cost of preferred stock w e = the target proportion of common stock in the capital structure when the company raises new funds r e = the marginal cost of common stock. Note that preferred stock is also referred to as preferred equity, and common stock is also referred to as common equity, or equity. Hence, WACC = [0.7 × 7%(1 – 0.35)] + [0.1 × 10%] + [0.2 × 12%] = 6.585% ≈ 6.6%. C.Incorrect because it fails to account for the tax deductibility of debt, computing the WACC as: [0.7 × 7%] + [0.1 × 10%] + [0.2 × 12%] = 8.3%.

questions.stem: Which of the following market structures has low barriers to entry?
questions.option_c: Monopolistic competition
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a monopoly has very high barriers to entry. B.Incorrect because an oligopoly has high barriers to entry. C.Correct because monopolistic competition has low barriers to entry.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in € millions) about a company: If all purchases were made on credit, cash paid to suppliers (in € millions) for Year 2 is:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because cash paid to suppliers is calculated as cost of sales plus (less) increase (decrease) in inventory less (plus) increase (decrease) in accounts payable. In this case, inventory declined by 20 (165 – 145) and accounts payable declined by 15 (135 – 120) so the calculation becomes 625 – 20 + 15 = 620. B.Incorrect because the decrease in inventory was added to cost of sales rather than subtracted and the decrease in accounts payable was subtracted rather than added. The calculation becomes 625 + 20 – 15 = 630. C.Incorrect because it is cost of sales plus the decrease in accounts payable. The calculation becomes 625 + 15 = 640.

questions.stem: Which of the following accounting actions would increase stockholders’equity in the current period?
questions.option_a: Capitalizing, rather than expensing, a payment
questions.option_b: Increasing the allowance for uncollectible accounts receivable
questions.option_c: Using LIFO rather than FIFO accounting for inventory in an inflationary environment
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the capitalization of payments is an example of how choices affect both the balance sheet and income statement. Capitalizing a payment changes the benefit from only the current period—making it an expense—to a benefit in future periods as an asset. The creation of an asset results in a comparable increase in stockholder’s equity. B.Incorrect because increasing the allowance for uncollectible accounts receivable will increase the uncollectible accounts expense reported for the period. This will contribute to lower net income and a decrease in stockholders’ equity. C.Incorrect because adopting last-in,-first-out accounting for inventory in an inflationary environment assumes newer and costlier purchases of inventory are sold to customers with the result that the remaining inventory reflects the older costs. This will contribute to lower net income from sales and a decrease in stockholders’equity.

questions.stem: All else being equal, if the level of significance applied to a hypothesis test decreases from 0.05 to 0.01, which of the following probabilities will increase?
questions.option_c: Both a Type I error and a Type II error
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because, the probability of a Type I error in testing a hypothesis is known as the level of significance of the test. Hence, by definition, a smaller significance level would result in a lower probability of a Type I error. B.Correct because, all else equal, if we decrease the probability of a Type I error by specifying a smaller significance level (say 0.01 rather than 0.05), we increase the probability of making a Type II error because we will reject the null less frequently, including when it is false. C.Incorrect because the probability of a Type I error in testing a hypothesis is known as the level of significance of the test. Hence, by definition, a smaller significance level would result in a smaller probability of a Type I error. Furthermore, the only way to reduce the probabilities of both types of errors simultaneously is to increase the sample size, n.

questions.stem: An investment pays $1,000 at the end of each year in perpetuity, with the first payment occurring six years from today. If the discount rate is 9% per year, the present value of the investment today is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it is the present value of a six-year ordinary annuity that pays $1,000 each year: $1,00 × [1 – 1/(1 + 0.09) 6 ]/0.09 = $4,485.92 ≈ $4,486. Calculator solution: N = 6; I = 9%; PMT = –1,000; compute PV = 4,485.92. B.Incorrect because it is the present value of the perpetuity that is wrongly discounted back by six, instead of five, years: PV of investment today = (PV of perpetuity in 5 years)/(1 + r) 6 , where PV of perpetuity in 5 years = A/r = $1,000/0.09 = $11,111.11. Thus, PV of investment today = $11,111.11/(1 + 0.09) 6 = $6,625.19 ≈ $6,625. Calculator solution: N = 6; I = 9%; FV = –11,111.11; compute PV = 6,625.19. C.Correct because it is the present value of the perpetuity that starts in six years: PV of investment today = (PV of perpetuity in 5 years)/(1 + r) 5 , where PV of perpetuity in 5 years = A/r = $1,000/0.09 = $11,111.11. Thus, PV of investment today = $11,111.11/(1 + 0.09) 5 = $7,221.46 ≈ $7,221. Calculator solution: N = 5; I = 9%; FV = –11,111.11; compute PV = 7,221.46.

questions.stem: When performing a simple linear regression with an indicator variable as the independent variable, the slope coefficient can be interpreted as the:
questions.option_a: mean of the dependent variable when the indicator variable is equal to one.
questions.option_b: mean of the dependent variable when the indicator variable is equal to zero.
questions.option_c: difference in the means of the dependent variable when the observations are grouped by the value of the indicator variable.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the mean of the dependent variable when the indicator variable is one can be computed as the sum of the intercept and slope coefficients, not the slope coefficient alone. B.Incorrect because this is the interpretation of the intercept, not the slope, coefficient. The interpretation of the intercept is the predicted value of the dependent variable if the indicator variable is zero. C.Correct because, when an indicator variable taking a value of zero or one is used as the independent variable in a simple linear regression, the estimated slope coefficient can be interpreted as the difference in the means if we grouped the observations by the indicator variable.

questions.stem: The correction of a material error for a prior period is handled by:
questions.option_a: adding a note disclosure regarding the error in the current financial statements only.
questions.option_b: restating the financial statements for the prior periods presented in the current financial statements only.
questions.option_c: both adding a note disclosure regarding the error in the current financial statements and restating the financial statements for the prior periods presented in the current financial statements.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the company is also required to restate the financial statements for the prior periods in the current financial statements. B.Incorrect because the company is also required to add a note disclosure regarding the error. C.Correct because another possible adjustment is a correction of an error for a prior period (e.g., in financial statements issued for an earlier year). This cannot be handled by simply adjusting the current period income statement. Correction of an error for a prior period is handled by restating the financial statements (including the balance sheet, statement of owners’ equity, and cash flow statement) for the prior periods presented in the current financial statements. (IAS No. 8, Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors, and FASB ASC Topic 250 - Accounting Changes and Error Corrections) Note disclosures are required regarding the error.

questions.stem: The most appropriate treatment of goodwill is that it be:
questions.option_c: fully expensed at the time of acquisition.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because goodwill is not amortized. B.Correct because goodwill is tested for impairment annually. C.Incorrect because goodwill is capitalized, rather than expensed.

questions.stem: A company purchases goods for £2,000,000 from various suppliers during its first year of operations. The company bears the inventory risk. The company's sale price includes the cost of sales plus a 20% mark-up. All goods purchased have been sold and delivered to customers by fiscal year-end and all orders are nonrefundable. The company should report revenue of:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it only includes the mark-up in revenue. This would be the case if the company would be only acting as an agent. However, the company bears inventory risk and therefore can't be considered only an agent. B.Incorrect because it subtracts the mark-up from the cost of sales. C.Correct because revenue is recognized when the obligation-satisfying transfer is made. The transaction price is what the seller estimates will be received in exchange for transferring the good(s) or service(s) identified in the contract. The transaction price is then allocated to each identified performance obligation. Revenue is recognized when a performance obligation is fulfilled. Revenue = cost of sales + mark-up = £2,000,000 + 20% × £2,000,000 = £2,000,000 + £400,000 = £2,400,000.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about the performance of a portfolio ($ millions): The portfolio’s annual time-weighted rate of return is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. It uses the following formula: B.Incorrect. It is the money-weighted rate of return (MWR). Solve for r in the following formula: To solve, use the cash flow (CF) function of a financial calculator and enter: CF 0 = −2 − 0.2= −2.2, CF 1 = −0.4, CF 2 = 0.2, CF3 = −1, and CF 4 = 4.1. Compute the quarterly IRR and obtain 6.09%. By annualizing we obtain: (1 + 0.0609) 4 − 1 = 27% (rounded). C. Correct. The time-weighted rate of return is calculated by computing the quarterly holding period returns and linking those returns into an annual return as follows: The time-weighted return (TWR) is found as follows: TWR = (1 + 9.09%) × (1 − 7.14%) × (1 + 33.33%) × (1 − 2.38%) − 1 = 32% (rounded)

questions.stem: All else being equal, a company that acquires a patent through external purchase rather than developing it internally is most likely to report:
questions.option_c: higher operating cash outflows.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect becasue costs associated with internally developing intangible assets are usually expensed, while external purchases are capitalized. A company that purchases intangible assets through external purchase will recognize a higher amount of assets than a company that develops intangible assets internally. B.Correct because the cost of acquiring intangible assets (including patents) is classified as investing cash outflows, whereas the costs of developing them internally is classified as operating cash outflows. If a company obtains intangibles through external purchase, it will report higher investing cash outflows than a company that develops intangible assets internally. C.Incorrect because the cost of acquiring intangible assets is classified as investing cash outflows, while the cost of developing them internally is classified as operating cash outflows. Thus, if the company obtains intangible assets through external purchase, it will report lower operating cash outflows than a company that develops the intangibles internally.

questions.stem: Derecognition of a long-lived asset other than by a sale most likely involves:
questions.option_a: recording cash proceeds if an asset is retired or abandoned.
questions.option_b: spinning off a portion of assets from a cash-generating unit of a company.
questions.option_c: removing the carrying amount of the asset given up, adding a fair value for the asset acquired if an asset is exchanged, and reporting any difference in values.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because when an asset is retired or abandoned, the company does not record cash proceeds. Assets are reduced by the carrying amount of the asset at the time of retirement or abandonment, and a loss equal to the asset’s carrying amount is recorded. B.Incorrect because when a spin-off occurs, typically, an entire cash-generating unit of a company with all its assets is spun off. C.Correct because when an asset is exchanged, accounting for the exchange typically involves removing the carrying amount of the asset given up, adding a fair value for the asset acquired, and reporting any difference between the carrying amount and the fair value as a gain or loss.

questions.stem: Inherent risks in an investment are most appropriately evaluated in which step of the financial statement analysis framework?
questions.option_b: Articulate the purpose and context of analysis
questions.option_c: Develop and communicate conclusions/recommendations
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because risks are evaluated and presented after data are collected and processed. B.Incorrect because risks are evaluated and presented after the purpose and context of analysis are articulated. C.Correct because discussion and presentation of inherent risks in an investment is appropriate in the develop and communicate conclusions/recommendations step.

questions.stem: Assuming wages and prices are rigid, which of the following policy combinations most likely increases government spending as a percentage of GDP?
questions.option_a: Easy fiscal policy and easy monetary policy
questions.option_b: Easy fiscal policy and tight monetary policy
questions.option_c: Tight fiscal policy and easy monetary policy
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because if both fiscal and monetary policy are easy, then the joint impact will be highly expansionary—leading to a rise in aggregate demand, lower interest rates (at least if the monetary impact is larger), and growing private and public sectors. This means it is less likely to increase government spending as percentage of GDP. B.Correct because if taxes are cut or government spending rises, the expansionary fiscal policy will lead to a rise in aggregate output. If this is accompanied by a reduction in money supply to offset the fiscal expansion, then interest rates will rise and have a negative effect on private sector demand. We have higher output and higher interest rates, and government spending will be a larger proportion of overall national income. C.Incorrect because if a fiscal contraction is accompanied by expansionary monetary policy and low interest rates, then the private sector will be stimulated and will rise as a share of GDP, while the public sector will shrink.

questions.stem: If the threshold level for the portfolio return is greater than the risk-free rate, the portfolio's safety-first ratio is:
questions.option_c: greater than its Sharpe ratio.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the safety-first ratio is SFRatio = [E(R P ) − R L ]/σ P and if we substitute the risk-free rate, R F , for the critical level R L , the SFRatio becomes the Sharpe ratio, i.e. Sharpe ratio SR = [E(R P ) – R F ]/σP. If R L > R F and other variables remain unchanged, then E(R P ) – R L < E(R P ) – R F , hence SFRatio < SR. B.Incorrect because if R L > R F , then SFRatio < SR and not SFRatio = SR. C.Incorrect because if R L > R F , then SFRatio < SR and not SFRatio = SR.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about three stocks that are part of an equal-weighted index consisting of 16 stocks: If the index is rebalanced, which stock's weight most likely remains unchanged?
questions.option_c: Stock 3
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because Stock 1's weight has changed and will be increased to 1/16, or 6.25%. B. Correct because rebalancing is necessary because the weights of the constituent securities change. The equal weight for all the 16 stocks in the index at rebalancing is 1/16, or 6.25%. Stock 2's end-of-period weight is 6.25%, so its weight has not changed and need not be changed for the index to be rebalanced. C. Incorrect because Stock 3's weight has changed and will be decreased to 1/16, or 6.25%.

questions.stem: Based on put–call–forward parity, a trader can replicate a short forward position with a:
questions.option_a: short put, a long call, and a long bond.
questions.option_b: short put, a short call, and a short bond.
questions.option_c: long put, a short call, and a short bond.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the cost of the fiduciary call must equal the cost of the synthetic protective put, giving us what is referred to as put–call–forward parity, F0(T)/(1 + r)T + p 0 = c 0 + X/(1 + r) T . This implies: –F 0 (T)/(1 + r) T = p 0 – c 0 – X/(1 + r) T . So, a short forward position can be replicated with a long (not short) a put, short (not long) a call, and short (not long) a bond. B.Incorrect because the cost of the fiduciary call must equal the cost of the synthetic pro­tective put, giving us what is referred to as put–call–forward parity, F 0 (T)/(1 + r) T + p 0 = c 0 + X/(1 + r) T . This implies: –F 0 (T)/(1 + r) T = p 0 – c 0 – X/(1 + r) T . So, a short forward position can be replicated with a long (not short) a put, short a call, and short a bond. C.Correct because the cost of the fiduciary call must equal the cost of the synthetic pro­tective put, giving us what is referred to as put–call–forward parity, F 0 (T)/(1 + r) T + p 0 = c 0 + X/(1 + r) T . This implies: –F 0 (T)/(1 + r) T = p 0 – c 0 – X/(1 + r) T . So, a short forward position can be replicated with a long a put, short a call, and short a bond.

questions.stem: Making a minority equity investment in a mature company that plans to expand operations best describes:
questions.option_c: development capital investing.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because growth capital generally refers to minority equity investments, whereby the firm takes a less-than-controlling interest in more mature companies looking for capital to expand or restructure operations, enter new markets, or finance major acquisitions. B.Incorrect because venture capital (VC) entails investing in or providing financing to private companies with high growth potential. Typically these are start-ups or young companies, but venture capital can be injected at various stages, ranging from concept creation for a company to the point of a company’s IPO (initial public offering) launch or its acquisition by another company. Venture capital generally targets start-up or young private companies with high growth potential, not more mature companies. C.Incorrect because leveraged buyouts (LBOs), or highly leveraged transactions, arise when private equity firms establish buyout funds (or LBO funds) to acquire public companies or established private companies, with a significant percentage of the purchase price financed through debt. In an LBO, the entire company is acquired, not a minority interest.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about covered bonds is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Covered bonds expose investors to prepayment risk.
questions.option_b: Covered bonds usually consist of one bond class per cover pool.
questions.option_c: The cover pool is transferred to a bankruptcy-remote special legal entity.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because in contrast to a static pool of mortgage loans that expose investors to prepayment risk as in the case of US mortgage-backed securities, cover pool sponsors must replace any prepaid or non-performing assets (i.e., assets that do not generate the promised cash flows) in the cover pool to ensure sufficient cash flows until the maturity of the covered bond. B.Correct because whereas ABS often use credit tranching to create bond classes with different borrower default exposures, covered bonds usually consist of one bond class per cover pool. C.Incorrect because in the case of ABS, the financial institution that originates loans transfers securitized assets to a bankruptcy-remote special legal entity, but the pool of underlying assets in a covered bond (or “cover pool”) remains on the financial institution’s balance sheet, against which covered bondholders retain a top-priority claim.

questions.stem: A protective put is a derivatives strategy that involves:
questions.option_a: selling a call and buying a put.
questions.option_b: selling an asset and buying a put.
questions.option_c: buying an asset and buying a put.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the strategy of holding the asset and a put is sometimes called a protective put. B.Incorrect because the strategy of holding the asset and a put is sometimes called a protective put. C.Correct because the strategy of holding the asset and a put is sometimes called a protective put.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is least likely to affect an individual’s ability to take risk?
questions.option_c: Expected income
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because time horizon will likely impact an individual’s ability to take risk. B.Correct because personality type is most likely to affect an individual’s willingness to take risk, not the ability to take risk. An individual’s ability to take risk is affected by such factors as time horizon and expected income. C.Incorrect because expected income will likely impact an individual’s ability to take risk.

questions.stem: When markets are operating normally, the portfolio approach to investing most likely:
questions.option_a: affects an investor’s risk more than the investor’s return.
questions.option_b: provides the same level of risk reduction as during times of severe market turmoil.
questions.option_c: increases an investor’s expected return as compared to owning one individual stock.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the portfolio approach provides investors with a way to reduce the risk associated with their wealth without necessarily decreasing their expected rate of return. B.Incorrect because although portfolio diversification generally does reduce risk, it does not necessarily provide the same level of risk reduction during times of severe market turmoil as it does when the economy and markets are operating "normally". C.Incorrect because the expected return of a portfolio should not be higher or lower as compared to holding one randomly selected stock.

questions.stem: The daily settlement of mark-to-market gains and losses in exchange-traded derivatives most likely reduces:
questions.option_c: counterparty credit risk.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the expected value of a derivative differs unexpectedly from that of the underlying, in what is known as basis risk. Basis risk may arise if a derivative instrument references a price or index that is similar to, but does not exactly match, an underlying exposure such as a different market reference rate or an issuer CDS spread versus that of an actual bond. Basis risk is affected by supply and demand dynamics in derivative markets, among other factors. Marking to market reduces counterparty credit risk, not basis risk. B.Incorrect because mark-to-market increases, not reduces, liquidity risk, which arises due to the divergence in the cash flow timing of a derivative versus that of an underlying transaction. The daily settlement of gains and losses in the futures market can give rise to liquidity risk. If an investor or issuer using a futures contract to hedge an underlying transaction is unable to meet a margin call due to a lack of funds, the counterparty’s position is closed out and the investor or issuer must cover any losses on the derivative trade. C.Correct because daily swings in the price of an underlying, among other factors affecting derivative prices, require more frequent exposure monitoring and management. Counterparty credit exposure varies by the derivative type and market in which a derivative is transacted and daily settlement of MTM (mark-to-market) gains and losses, which characterizes exchange-traded derivatives, substantially reduces counterparty credit risk.

questions.stem: Which of the following derivative contracts has a hard commodity underlying?
questions.option_c: Aluminum futures
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because cattle futures are an example of a derivative contract with a soft commodity underlying. Soft commodities are agricultural products, such as cattle and corn. B.Incorrect because soybean options (and futures) are an example of a derivative contract with an agricultural, or soft, commodity underlying. C.Correct because aluminum futures are an example of a metals contract, which is a derivative with a hard commodity underlying.

questions.stem: Using the rating scale from Moody's, the lowest rating for an investment-grade bond is:
questions.option_c: Baa3.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because bonds rated Baa3 or higher by Moody's and BBB– or higher by Standard & Poor's and Fitch are considered investment grade. B.Incorrect because bonds rated Baa3 or higher by Moody's and BBB– or higher by Standard & Poor's and Fitch are considered investment grade. C.Correct because bonds rated Baa3 or higher by Moody's and BBB– or higher by Standard & Poor's and Fitch are considered investment grade.

questions.stem: If a risk-free asset with zero expected return is added to the investable universe of risky assets, the investors’ risk-return trade-off most likely:
questions.option_c: improves.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because an investor’s portfolio improves (not worsens) if a risk-free asset is added to the mix. In other words, a combination of the risk-free asset and a risky asset can result in a better risk–return trade-off than an investment in only one type of asset because the risk-free asset has zero correlation with the risky asset. B.Incorrect because an investor’s portfolio improves (not remains unchanged) if a risk-free asset is added to the mix. In other words, a combination of the risk-free asset and a risky asset can result in a better risk–return trade-off than an investment in only one type of asset because the risk-free asset has zero correlation with the risky asset. C.Correct because we can improve an investor’s portfolio by expanding the opportunity set of risky assets because this allows the investor to choose a superior mix of assets. An investor’s portfolio improves if a risk-free asset is added to the mix. In other words, a combination of the risk-free asset and a risky asset can result in a better risk–return trade-off than an investment in only one type of asset because the risk-free asset has zero correlation with the risky asset. The combination is called the capital allocation line.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following data (in INR millions) for a company located in India: Assuming an enterprise value multiple of 3.2, the company’s market capitalization (in INR millions) is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because it incorrectly subtracts cash and short-term investments instead of adding them. Enterprise Value (EV) = EBITDA × EV multiple = 15 × 3.2 = 48 Market capitalization = Enterprise value – MV of debt – MV of preferred stock – cash and short-term investments = 48 – 10 – 5 – 4.5 = 28.5 B. Incorrect. It ignores cash and short-term investments. Enterprise Value (EV) = EBITDA × EV multiple = 15 × 3.2 = 48 Market capitalization = Enterprise value – MV of debt – MV of preferred stock – cash and short-term investments = 48 – 10 – 5 = 33 C. Correct because Enterprise value (EV) = EBITDA × EV multiple = 15 × 3.2 = 48. Market capitalization = EV – Market value (MV) of debt – MV of preferred stock + Cash and short-term investments = 48 – 10 – 5 + 4.5 = 37.5.

questions.stem: Compared with an otherwise identical option-free bond, when interest rates fall, the price of a callable bond will:
questions.option_c: rise more.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the value of the bond will rise, not fall. B.Correct because when interest rates fall, the price of the embedded call option increases. The price of a callable bond equals the price of an option-free bond minus the price of the embedded call option. The price of the callable bond will not increase as much as an option-free bond because the price of the call option is increasing. As interest rates fall, the bond is more likely to be called, limiting the upside price increase potential. C.Incorrect because the value of the callable bond cannot rise too much before the bond is called.

questions.stem: If a stock purchased with 60% margin declines 25%, the investor's return on equity is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because 85% is the sum of 60% and 25%, the two numbers provided in the stem, and is not a meaningful number or calculation. B.Incorrect because if 40% rather than 60% is incorrectly used to calculate leverage, leverage = 1/0.4 ≈ 2.5, multiplied by the 25% decline ≈ a 63% decline. C.Correct because 60% margin equals leverage of 1/0.6 ≈ 1.67, multiplied by the 25% decline ≈ a 42% decline.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a US Treasury bill: The bill's discount rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because the years/days is inverted: DR ≠ {days/years} × {(FV – PV)/FV}: = {340/360} × {(1,000,000 – 950,000)/1,000,000} = 0.94444 × 0.05 = 0.047222 ≈ 4.72%. B. Correct because the DR = {year/days} × {(FV – PV)/FV} where: PV = present value, or the price of the money market instrument FV = future value paid at maturity, or the face value of the money market instrument Days = number of days between settlement and maturity; Year = number of days in the year; DR = discount rate, stated as an annual percentage rateDR = {360/340} × {(1,000,000 – 950,000)/1,000,000} DR = 1.05882 × 0.05 = 0.052941 ≈ 5.29%. C. Incorrect because the DR is calculated as an add-on rate. AOR ≠ {year/days} × {(FV – PV)/PV} = {360/340} × {(1,000,000 – 950,000)/950,000} = 1.05882 × 0.052632 = 0.055727 ≈ 5.57%.

questions.stem: When a bank invests its excess reserves, which of the following best describes the bank's return objective? To earn a return that exceeds the:
questions.option_b: interest rate the bank pays on its deposits.
questions.option_c: interest rate the bank receives on its loans.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because banks often have excess reserves that are invested in relatively conservative and very short-duration fixed-income investments, with a goal of earning an excess return above interest obligations due to depositors. B.Correct because banks often have excess reserves that are invested in relatively conservative and very short-duration fixed-income investments, with a goal of earning an excess return above interest obligations due to depositors. C.Incorrect because banks often have excess reserves that are invested in relatively conservative and very short-duration fixed-income investments, with a goal of earning an excess return above interest obligations due to depositors.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is least accurate regarding the factors that affect the interest rate risk characteristics of an option-free bond?
questions.option_a: The higher the yield, the greater the bond’s price sensitivity to changes in interest rates.
questions.option_b: The lower the coupon rate, the greater the bond’s price sensitivity to changes in interest rates.
questions.option_c: The longer the bond’s maturity, the greater the bond’s price sensitivity to changes in interest rates.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because option-free bonds have positive convexity. The higher the yield to maturity, the lower the duration (and thus the lower the interest rate risk). B.Incorrect because bonds with higher coupons have higher interest rate risks. C.Incorrect because bonds with longer maturities have higher interest rate risks.

questions.stem: An analyst observes the following information about a bond: If the initial price of the bond is 97.0,the approximate convexity is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because the formula for the approximate duration is used instead of approximate convexity. B. Incorrect because when calculating the approximate convexity, the change in yield term in the denominator is doubled as in the approximate duration calculation. C. Correct because the approximate convexity statistic = ApproxCon = (PV − + PV + − 2 × PV 0 ) / [(ΔYield) 2 × PV 0 ] where: PV − = price if yields decline PV + = price if yields rise PV 0 = initial price ΔYield = change in yield in decimal form. ApproxCon = [(97.5 + 96.8) − (2 × 97)] ÷ (0.0015 2 × 97) = 1,374.5704 ApproxCon = [194.3 − 194] ÷ (0.00000225 × 97) = 1,374.57, rounded to 1,375.

questions.stem: The price of a pay-fixed receive-floating interest rate swap is most likely:
questions.option_a: the fixed rate that results when the market value of the swap is zero at initiation.
questions.option_b: the sum of the fixed-rate payments minus the sum of the floating-rate payments.
questions.option_c: the present value of the floating-rate payments minus the present value of the fixed-rate payments.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the price of the swap is the fixed rate on the swap at the start of the transaction such that the present value of fixed payments is equal to the present value of the floating payments and the market value of the swap is zero. B.Incorrect because these calculations provide the market value of the swap to one of the parties. C.Incorrect because these calculations provide the market value of the swap to one of the parties.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a hedge fund: If the incentive fee is calculated independently of the management fee, total fees for the year are:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because the incentive fee is calculated only on the return in excess of the soft hurdle rate rather than on the entire return. When a soft hurdle rate is used, the incentive fee is calculated on the entire return. In this case, the calculation of the incentive fee is based on the return in excess of the hurdle rate of $6,000,000 ($80,000,000 × (0.125 gross return – 0.05 soft hurdle rate)). The incentive fee calculated in this manner is $1,200,000 ($6,000,0000 return in excess of the hurdle rate x 0.2 incentive fee). The management fee is calculated correctly as $1,800,000 ((80,000,000 beginning-of-year assets × 1.125) x (0.02 management fee)). Therefore, the total fees calculated in this manner are $3,000,000 (management fee of $1,800,000 + incentive fee of $1,200,000). B. Incorrect because the incentive fee has been calculated net of the management fee rather than independent of the management fee. The management fee is correctly calculated as $1,800,000 ($80,000,000 × 1.125 × 0.02). The incentive fee is incorrectly calculated net of the management fee and totals $1,640,000 ([($80,000,000 × 0.125 gross return) – (management fee of $1,800,000)] × (incentive fee of 0.2)). Thus, the total fee becomes $3,440,000 (management fee of $1800,000 + incentive fee of $1,640,000). C. Correct because the incentive fee is calculated independently of the management fee and, since a soft hurdle rate is used, the incentive fee is calculated on the entire return. The partnership agreement usually specifies that the performance fee is earned only after the fund achieves a return known as a hurdle rate. The hurdle rate is a minimum rate of return that the GP must exceed in order to earn the performance fee. GPs typically receive 20% of the total profit of the private equity fund net of any hard hurdle rate, in which case the GP earns fees on annual returns in excess of the hurdle rate, or net of the soft hurdle rate, in which case the fee is calculated on the entire annual gross return as long as the set hurdle is exceeded. The management fee is calculated on end-of-year AUM of $90,000,000 ($80,000,000 beginning-of-year AUM × 1.125) and is $1,800,000 ($90,000,000 end-of-year AUM × 0.02 management fee). The incentive fee is calculated independently of the management fee and on the entire return (soft hurdle rate) and is $2,000,000 (($80,000,000 × 0.125) x (0.2 incentive fee)). Total fees are therefore $3,800,000 (management fee of $1,800,000 + incentive fee of $2,000,000).

questions.stem: An 8-year, 3.5% annual coupon bond is priced at 92.1492, with a yield to maturity of 4.7% and a Macaulay duration of 7.0705. If rates decrease by 75 bps, the percentage price change of the bond is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because yields and bond prices are inversely related, the price change should be positive. Also, Macaulay duration, rather than modified duration, was used in the price change formula: 7.0705 x (–0.0075) = –0.05303 ≈ –5.3%. B.Correct because to determine the percentage price change of a bond for a given change in yield, first convert Macaulay duration (7.0705) to modified duration by dividing Macaulay duration by 1 plus yield per period. Next, multiply annual modified duration by the change in yield. C.Incorrect because the price change is incorrectly calculated by using Macaulay duration, rather than modified duration. –7.0705 x (–0.0075) = –0.05303 ≈ 5.3%.

questions.stem: If a call option is overvalued relative to the binomial model, investors can earn a return above the risk-free rate by selling the call option and simultaneously:
questions.option_b: selling short the underlying and investing the proceeds at the risk-free rate.
questions.option_c: buying the underlying and funding the transaction by borrowing funds at the risk-free rate.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because, as described in the rationale for the correct answer, the investor needs to sell the call option, buy the underlying shares, and fund the transaction by borrowing funds at the risk-free rate. B.Incorrect because, as described in the rationale for the correct answer, the investor needs to sell the call option, buy the underlying shares, and fund the transaction by borrowing funds at the risk-free rate. C.Correct because if the option is trading too high relative to the formula, investors can sell the call, buy h shares of the underlying, and earn a return in excess of the risk-free rate, while funding the transaction by borrowing at the risk-free rate.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about an equally weighted portfolio comprised of 500 assets: Average variance of the returns of the assets = 0.04 Average covariance between the returns of the assets = 0.01 The variance of the portfolio returns is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because for portfolios with a large number of assets, covariance among the assets accounts for almost all of the portfolio's risk. Given equal weights and average variance/covariance, we can rewrite the portfolio variance as: The variance of the portfolio = (0.04/500) + [(500 – 1)/500] × 0.01 = 0.00008 + 0.00998 = 0.01006 ≈ 0.01 (average covariance of returns). B. Incorrect because it is the average variance of the assets of the portfolio, not the average covariance between the assets. For portfolios with a large number of assets, covariance among the assets accounts for almost all of the portfolio's risk. C. Incorrect because it is the sum of the average variance of the assets of the portfolio and the average covariance between the assets. For portfolios with a large number of assets, covariance among the assets accounts for almost all of the portfolio's risk.

questions.stem: Macaulay duration is best described as:
questions.option_a: an average maturity of the bond.
questions.option_b: a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments.
questions.option_c: an estimated price change for a bond given a shift in its benchmark yield curve.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Macaulay duration is a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments. B.Correct because Macaulay duration is a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments. C.Incorrect because Macaulay duration is a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments.

questions.stem: Cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds:
questions.option_a: do not typically invest directly in cryptocurrencies.
questions.option_b: allow investors to trade shares in trusts holding large pools of a cryptocurrency.
questions.option_c: represent agreements to buy or sell a specific quantity of cryptocurrency at a specified price and date.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds such as ETFs, seek to replicate digital asset investment returns. These ETFs typically do not directly invest in cryptocurrencies and gain exposure to the value of cryptocurrencies using cash and cryptocurrency derivatives. B.Incorrect because cryptocurrency coin trusts (not exchange-traded funds) allow investors to trade shares in trusts holding large pools of a cryptocurrency and that trade over the counter (OTC) and behave like closed-end funds. C.Incorrect because cryptocurrency futures contracts (not exchange-traded funds) are agreements to buy or sell a specific quantity of bitcoin or other cryptocurrency at a specified price on a particular future date.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a pension fund's liabilities: If the current interest rate is 4%, the effective duration of the fund's liabilities is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because the change in the yield curve that is used is 0.100 instead of 0.010. Effective duration is calculated as: B. Correct because the effective duration is calculated as: EffDur = [(PV_) – (PV + )]/[2 × (ΔCurve) × (PV 0 )] = (875.1 –763.4) / (2 × 0.0100 × 822.7) ≈ 6.79. C. Incorrect because the denominator of the effective duration equation is not multiplied by 2. Effective duration is calculated as: EffDur = [(PV_) – (PV + )]/[2 × (ΔCurve) × (PV 0 )], resulting in (875.1 – 763.4) / (0.0100 × 822.7) ≈ 13.58.

questions.stem: A stock has a correlation of 0.45 with the market and a standard deviation of returns of 12.35%. If the market has a standard deviation of returns of 8.25%, then the beta of the stock is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because this calculation incorrectly puts the standard deviation of the stock in the denominator, not the numerator. B. Correct because beta is calculated as follows: where β = beta; ρ i,m = correlation between market and stock; σ i = standard deviation of the stock σ m = standard deviation of the market C.Incorrect because this calculation incorrectly calculates beta as the ratio of the standard deviation of the stock to the standard deviation of the market.

questions.stem: Empirical duration:
questions.option_a: assumes that government bond yields and spreads are independent variables.
questions.option_b: is higher than analytical duration for high-yield bonds under market stress scenarios.
questions.option_c: uses statistical methods and historical bond prices to derive the price–yield relationship for bond portfolios.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the approach to estimate duration and convexity statistics using mathematical formulas is often referred to as analytical duration. These estimates of the impact of benchmark yield changes on bond prices implicitly assume that government bond yields and spreads are independent variables that are uncorrelated with one another. Analytical duration, not empirical duration, relies on this assumption. B.Incorrect because the same macroeconomic factors driving government bond yields lower in a market stress scenario will cause high-yield bond credit spreads to widen because of an increase in expected default risk. Since credit spreads and benchmark yields are negatively correlated under this scenario, wider credit spreads will partially or fully offset the decline in government benchmark yields, resulting in lower empirical duration estimates than analytical duration estimates. C.Correct because empirical duration uses statistical methods and historical bond prices to derive the price–yield relationship for specific bonds or bond portfolios.

questions.stem: An investor buys a stock on margin and holds the position for one year. Assuming that the interest on the loan and the dividend are both paid at the end of the year, the price at which the investor sold the stock is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it ignores the margin interest. B.Incorrect because it ignores the dividend amount. C.Correct.

questions.stem: Regarding the partnership structures of private equity funds, which of the following statements is most accurate?
questions.option_a: General partners theoretically bear unlimited liability
questions.option_b: Limited partners are involved with the management of a fund
questions.option_c: Investors are general partners who own fractional interests in a partnership
questions.explanation: A.Correct because in limited partnerships, the fund manager is the general partner (GP) and investors are the limited partners (LP). The GP runs the business and theoretically bears unlimited liability for anything that goes wrong. B.Incorrect because LPs (limited partners) play passive roles and are not involved with the management of the fund. C.Incorrect because many alternative investments, such as hedge and private equity funds, use a partnership structure with a general partner that manages the business and limited partners (investors) who own fractional interests in the partnership. Therefore, investors are limited partners, not general partners.

questions.stem: The no-arbitrage condition is violated at option expiry when the value of an in-the-money:
questions.option_a: put option is below its exercise price.
questions.option_b: put option is below its exercise value.
questions.option_c: call option is below the price of its underlying.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a put option buyer will exercise only if the spot price, ST, is below X at maturity. The exercise price, X, therefore represents the upper bound on the put value. Therefore, the no-arbitrage condition is not violated when the value of put option is below its exercise price. B.Correct because an option buyer will exercise a call or put option at maturity only if it returns a positive payoff—that is: (X − ST) > 0 for a put (referred to as its exercise value). Also, examples of in-the-money (ITM) options include a put option with an underlying spot price below the exercise price. So, the value of an ITM put is equal to its exercise value at expiry. Also, an option which trades below its exercise value violates the no-arbitrage condition. Therefore, the no-arbitrage condition is violated when the value of ITM put option is below its exercise value. C.Incorrect because the call buyer will not pay more for the right to purchase an underlying than the price of that underlying, which is the upper bound. Therefore, the no-arbitrage condition is not violated when the value of a call option is below the price to its underlying.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely an assumption of the CAPM?
questions.option_a: Security prices are not affected by investor trades
questions.option_b: An investor can invest as much as he or she desires in any asset
questions.option_c: Investors are different only with respect to their unique holding periods
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because one of the assumptions of the CAPM is that investors are price takers, which implies that investor trades will not affect prices. B.Incorrect because one of the assumptions of the CAPM is that all investments are infinitely divisible, which means an investor can invest as much as he or she desires in any asset. C.Correct because one of the assumptions of the CAPM is that investors plan for the same single holding period.

questions.stem: An investor planning to retire in 20 years will make a tuition payment equal to 10% of his portfolio's current value in three years. In the investor's IPS, this payment is most likely stated as a:
questions.option_c: unique circumstance.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the return objective could be a required return – that is, the amount the investor needs to earn to meet a particular future goal – such as a certain level of retirement income. The required payment of tuition fees is not a return objective constraint. B.Correct because in the liquidity constraints section the IPS should state what the likely requirements are to withdraw funds from the portfolio. Examples for an individual investor would be outlays for covering healthcare payments or tuition fees. C.Incorrect because the unique circumstances section of the IPS should cover any other aspect of the client's circumstances that is likely to have a material impact on the composition of the portfolio. A client may have considerations derived from his or her religion or ethical values that could constrain investment choices. Whether rooted in religious beliefs or not, a client may have personal objections to certain products or practices, which could lead to the exclusion of certain companies, countries, or types of securities from the investable universe as well as the client's benchmark. Therefore, a large outlay to cover tuition fees is not a unique circumstance.

questions.stem: Which of the following index types has the most significant potential to suffer from survivorship bias?
questions.option_c: Broad equity market
questions.explanation: A.Correct because hedge fund performance reporting is voluntary. Another consequence of the voluntary performance reporting (of hedge funds) is the potential for survivorship bias and, therefore, inaccurate performance representation. This means that hedge funds with poor performance may be less likely to report their performance to the database or may stop reporting to the database, so their returns may be excluded when measuring the return of the index. As a result, the index may not accurately reflect actual hedge fund performance so much as the performance of hedge funds that are performing well. B.Incorrect because performance reporting of fixed income securities is based on the trading activity of dealers, not the voluntary reporting of government agencies. Fixed-income markets are predominantly dealer markets. This means that firms (dealers) are assigned to specific securities and are responsible for creating liquid markets for those securities by purchasing and selling them from their inventory. C.Incorrect because a broad equity index is not based on voluntary reporting and is intended to be representative of the market. A broad equity market index, as its name suggests, represents an entire given equity market and typically includes securities representing more than 90 percent of the selected market.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in $ millions) about a hedge fund: If the incentive fee is 20% and there is a clawback provision, the total incentive fee (in $ millions) for Years 1 and 2 is:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because it calculated the GP's incentive fee based on the profit/loss in Year 2 only. Therefore Total incentive fee = MAX [$0, –$10 million × 20%] = MAX [$0, –$2 million] = $0. B. Correct because the GP would initially accrue a 20% of $25 million profit at the end of the first year, equal to $5 million. Typically, this amount would be held in escrow for the benefit of the GP but not actually paid. But then the GP loses $10 million of the initial $25 million gain, so the aggregate whole-of-fund gain at the end of the second year would be only $15 million; this amount times 20% would result in only an $3 million incentive fee. The general partner would then have to return $2 million of the previously accrued incentive fees to the capital accounts of LP investors because of the clawback provision. C. Incorrect because it calculated the GP's incentive fee based on the profit/loss in Year 1 only. Therefore Total incentive fee = $25 million × 20% = $5 million.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company's common stock: If the required rate of return is 10%, the intrinsic value per share is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Correct because it is the present value of all future dividends. The present value of the perpetual level dividends, three year from now, is: $2.21 / (0.10 – 0) = $22.10. The present value of the perpetual level dividends now is: $22.10 / (1.10)^3 = $16.604. The present of dividends in the first three years is: $2.00 / 1.10 + $2.10 / (1.10) ^ 2 + $2.21 / (1.10) ^ 3 = $1.818 + $1.736 + $1.660 = $5.214 . So, the intrinsic value of the stock is closest to: $16.604 + $5.214 = $21.818 ≈ $21.82. B. Incorrect because it is only the present value of the perpetual level dividends three years from now. $2.21 / (0.10 – 0) = $22.10. C. Incorrect because the present value of the level dividends in perpetuity three years from now has been added to the present value of the dividends in Year 1, Year 2 and Year 3, without discounting it for three years (see calculations in correct answer). $22.100 + $5.214 = $27.314 ≈ $27.31.

questions.stem: If a risk-free asset is available, an investor's optimal portfolio is the point of tangency between the:
questions.option_a: Markowitz efficient frontier and the capital allocation line.
questions.option_b: capital allocation line and the investor's indifference curve.
questions.option_c: Markowitz efficient frontier and the investor's indifference curve.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it describes the optimal risky portfolio rather than the optimal investor portfolio. The optimal investor portfolio lies on the capital allocation line and any portfolio on the capital allocation line lies above the Markowitz efficient frontier (with the only exception being the optimal risky portfolio). Thus, the described portfolio does not describe an investor's optimal portfolio. Overlaying each individual’s indifference curves on the capital allocation line will provide us with the optimal portfolio for that investor. B.Correct because overlaying each individual’s indifference curves on the capital allocation line will provide us with the optimal portfolio for that investor. The optimal portfolio for the investor with this indifference curve is portfolio C on CAL(P), which is tangent to the indifference curve. C.Incorrect because, if a risk-free asset is available, overlaying each individual’s indifference curves on the capital allocation line (and not the Markowitz efficient frontier) will provide us with the optimal portfolio for that investor.

questions.stem: A company borrowed capital by issuing a number of different securities. Which of the following most likely ranks the highest with respect to priority of payments?
questions.option_c: Senior unsecured bond
questions.explanation: A.Correct because third lien debt is secured debt. It has a secured interest in the pledged assets and ranks higher than all other unsecured debts. B.Incorrect because a subordinate loan is an unsecured debt. Among the various creditor classes, these obligations have among the lowest priority of claims and frequently have little or no recovery in the event of default. C.Incorrect because a senior unsecured bond is also an unsecured debt. It ranks highest among all the unsecured debts, but it ranks below secured debts.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company's earnings: According to the Gordon growth model, if an investor's required return is 6%, the justified forward P/E is:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect but is the result when the retention rate is substituted for the payout rate: 0.4/(0.06 – 0.01) = 0.4/0.05 = 8. B. Incorrect because the growth rate is omitted: 0.6/(0.06) = 10. C. Correct because the dividend payout ratio = (1 ‒ earnings retention rate) = (1 – 0.40) = 0.6. The justified forward P/E is: p/(r – g) where p = dividend payout ratio, r = required rate of return and g = sustainable growth rate, therefore P/E = 0.6/ (0.06 – 0.01) = 0.6/0.05 = 12

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a bond: The bond's money duration per 100 of par value is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because it subtracts accrued interest instead of adding it. MoneyDur = AnnModDur × (PV Flat + AI) ≠ AnnModDur × (PV Flat – AI) = 7.534 × (92.084 – 1.458) = 7.534 × 90.626 ≈ 682.7763 ≈ 683. B. Incorrect because it uses flat price instead of full price. MoneyDur = AnnModDur × (PV Flat + AI) ≠ AnnModDur × (PV Flat ) = 7.534 × 92.084 ≈ 693.761 ≈ 694. C. Correct because money duration (MoneyDur) is calculated as the annual modified duration (AnnModDur) times the full price (PV Full ) of the bond including accrued interest. MoneyDur = AnnModDur × PV Full ." Using also the relation PV Full = PV Flat + AI, where PV Flat is the flat price and AI is the accrued interest, MoneyDur = AnnModDur × (PV Flat + AI) = 7.534 × (92.084 + 1.458) = 7.534 × 93.542 ≈ 704.745 ≈ 705.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about the limit order book for a stock: Based only on this information, which of the following orders to purchase 50 shares will be executed immediately at a price of $78.00?
questions.option_c: Both a market order and a limit order at $78.00
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because while a market order will execute, a limit order will also execute. A limit order seeks the best price immediately available, but in no event accept a price higher than a specified limit price when buying or accept a price lower than a specified limit price when selling. As the lowest offer price is $78.00 for 80 shares, the order will be executed immediately even if it is a limit order at $78.00 B. Incorrect because a limit order and a market order will execute. A market order instructs the broker or exchange to obtain the best price immediately available when filling the order. As the lowest offer price is $78.00 for 80 shares, the order will be executed immediately even if it is a market order. C. Correct because a market order instructs the broker or exchange to obtain the best price immediately available when filling the order. A limit order conveys almost the same instruction: obtain the best price immediately available, but in no event accept a price higher than a specified limit price when buying or accept a price lower than a specified limit price when selling. As the lowest offer price $78.00 for 80 shares, the order will be executed immediately if it is either a market order or a limit order at $78.00

questions.stem: An investor buys a call for $10.70 that has a strike price of $450. If the value at expiration for this call is $33.60, the price of the underlying at expiration is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because $416.40 is the value of the underlying assuming that this was a put option instead of a call option. The "payoff to the put buyer" at expiration is p T = Max(0, X – S T ), where X is the exercise price and ST is the price of the underlying at expiration. Given the information in the stem we get $33.60 = Max(0,$450 – S T ) which yields S T = $450 – $33.60 = $416.40. B.Incorrect because $472.90 is the profit from the option position added to the strike price. It is computed as (c T – c 0 ) + X where cT is the value of the option at expiration, c 0 is the purchase price of the option and X is the strike price. Given the information in the stem we get ($33.60 – $10.70) + $450= $472.90. C.Correct because the value or "payoff to the call buyer" at expiration is cT = Max(0,S T – X) where X is the strike price, S T is the price of the underlying at expiration. Given the information in the stem we get $33.60 = Max(0,S T – $450). Hence, ST = $450 + $33.60 = $483.60.

questions.stem: If a test rejects the hypothesis that market prices reflect private information but does not reject the hypothesis that they reflect past market data and public information, then the form of market efficiency is best described as:
questions.option_c: semi-strong.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because markets are weak-form efficient when market prices reflect past market data only. B.Incorrect because markets are strong-form efficient when market prices reflect past market data, public information, and private information. C.Correct because the forms of market efficiency are as follows: If a test rejects the hypothesis that market prices reflect private information but does not reject the hypothesis that they reflect past market data and public information, then there is evidence that the form of market efficiency is semi-strong (because only past market data and public information are reflected in market prices).

questions.stem: Alternative investments most likely have:
questions.option_c: less transparency than traditional investments.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because alternative investments often carry higher fees, including performance and/or incentive fees. B.Incorrect because alternative investments differ from traditional asset classes in that they involve the use of leverage. C.Correct because fund investment structures for alternative investments differ substantially from traditional public equity and fixed-income fund or ETF investments. For example, alternative funds usually involve less frequent transparency on periodic returns and fund positions versus equity or fixed-income funds.

questions.stem: The price of a stock is $100 and the risk-free rate is 5%. If the strike price of a European put option with one year until expiration is $105, the put option is:
questions.option_c: out of the money.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the put option is in, not at the money since the stock price is below the strike price, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer. B.Correct because when the underlying is beyond the exercise price in the appropriate direction (higher for a call, lower for a put), the option is said to be in the money. When the underlying is precisely at the exercise price, the option is said to be at the money. When the underlying has not reached the exercise price (currently lower for a call, higher for a put), the option is said to be out of the money. Here, the put option is in the money since the stock price is below the strike price. C.Incorrect because the put option is in, not at the money since the stock price is below the strike price, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer.

questions.stem: An index is made up of only two stocks. An analyst gathers the following information about those two stocks: Which of the following index weighting methods results in the largest weighting for Stock 2?
questions.option_c: Float-adjusted market-capitalization weighting
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because Stock 2 has a weight of 84.21% under a float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted index. This is greater compared to its weight under a price-weighted index (76.92%). In price weighting, the weight on each constituent security is determined by dividing its price by the sum of all the prices of the constituent securities. B. Incorrect because Stock 2 has a weight of 84.21% under a float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted index. This is greater compared to its weight under a market-capitalization-weighted index (75.91%). In market-capitalization weighting, or value weighting, the weight on each constituent security is determined by dividing its market capitalization by the total market capitalization (the sum of the market capitalization) of all the securities in the index. Market capitalization or value is calculated by multiplying the number of shares outstanding by the market price per share, where shares outstanding is the sum of the shares available to the public and the shares held by controlling shareholders. C. Correct because Stock 2 has a weight of 84.21% under a float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted index. This is greater compared to its weight under a price-weighted index (76.92% = 100 / (30 + 100)) or a market-capitalization-weighted index (75.91% = 690 / (219 + 690)). In float-adjusted market-capitalization weighting, the weight on each constituent security is determined by adjusting its market capitalization for its market float. Typically, market float is the number of shares of the constituent security that are available to the investing public. Float-adjusted market cap = market float × BOP price. BOP weight = float-adjusted market cap / total float-adjusted market cap.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely forecast by using efficiency ratios?
questions.option_c: Selling and distribution expenses
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because cost of sales is typically forecast as a percentage of sales or as a gross margin. Cost of sales (cost of goods sold, or COGS) is typically the single largest cost for companies that make and/or sell products. Because it has a direct link with sales, forecasting this item as a percentage of sales (or as a gross margin) is usually a good approach. B.Correct because working capital forecasts are typically made by using efficiency ratios, discussed in earlier modules, as the forecast object, which are combined with sales and costs forecasts to project accounts receivable, inventories, accounts payable, and other current assets and liabilities. C.Incorrect because selling and distribution expenses are more likely modeled as a percentage of sales. Although SG&A expenses overall are generally less closely linked to revenue than is cost of sales, certain SG&A expenses could be more variable than others. Specifically, selling and distribution expenses often have a large variable component and can be modeled as a percentage of sales, while general corporate costs are more fixed and might be better modeled using a fixed growth rate based on expected wage inflation.

questions.stem: Compared to a US bond, Eurobonds are most likely:
questions.option_c: more regulated.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the Eurobond market was created primarily to bypass the legal, regulatory, and tax constraints imposed on bond issuers and investors, particularly in the United States. B.Incorrect because the Eurobond market was created primarily to bypass the legal, regulatory, and tax constraints imposed on bond issuers and investors, particularly in the United States. C.Incorrect because the Eurobond market was created primarily to bypass the legal, regulatory, and tax constraints imposed on bond issuers and investors, particularly in the United States.

questions.stem: The industry growth style of the crude oil sector is best characterized as:
questions.option_c: defensive mature.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because crude oil together with natural gas and freight transportation are examples of cyclical mature industries given in the reading. B.Incorrect because biotechnology, software and gaming are examples of defensive growth industries given in the reading, not crude oil which is a cyclical mature industry instead. C.Incorrect because utilities, beverages and pharmaceuticals are examples of defensive mature industries given in the reading, not crude oil which is a cyclical mature industry instead.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following cash flows (in $ millions) for a private equity fund: If the terminal value is $180 million, an investor's multiple of invested capital (MOIC) is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because it reduces the liquidity event by the management fees and fund expenses (as opposed to reducing the invested capital by that amount). MOIC = (Realized value of investment + Unrealized value of investment) / Total amount of invested capital (which is paid-in capital less management fees and fund expenses). MOIC ≠ (180 – 12 – 8) / 100 = 1.60x. B. Incorrect because it fails to subtract the management fees from the invested capital in the correct calculation. MOIC = (Realized value of investment + Unrealized value of investment) / Total amount of invested capital (which is paid-in capital less management fees and fund expenses). MOIC ≠ 180 / (100 – 8) = 1.96x. C. Correct because MOIC = (Realized value of investment + Unrealized value of investment) / Total amount of invested capital (which is paid-in capital less management fees and fund expenses). Hence, MOIC = 180 / (100 – 12 – 8) = 2.25x.

questions.stem: An increase in the dividend payout ratio will most likely increase the intrinsic value when using a(n):
questions.option_c: asset-based valuation model.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the increase in earnings affects the multiplier models, but the increase in the dividend payout ratio does not have any effect. B.Correct because an increase in the dividend payout ratio will increase the cash expected to be distributed to shareholders. The dividend discount model is the present value of the cash expected to be distributed to shareholders. Therefore an increase in the dividend payout ratio will increase the intrinsic value in a present value model. C.Incorrect because the increase in the dividend payout ratio does not have an effect on the asset-based valuation model.

questions.stem: By setting minimum standards of competence for investment managers, regulators most likely:
questions.option_b: ensure firms maintain minimum levels of capital.
questions.option_c: ensure all companies report financial results on a common basis.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because regulators help solve these agency problems by setting minimum standards of competence for agents and by defining and enforcing minimum standards of practice. These agents include investment managers. B.Incorrect because although regulators do set minimum levels of capital, it is not to help with agency problems. Instead, minimum levels of capital ensures that the companies will be able to honor their contractual commitments when unexpected market movements and ensure that the owners of financial firms have substantial interest in the decisions that they make. C.Incorrect because setting minimum standards of competence for agents help solve agency problems and do not ensure all companies report financial results on a common basis.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company for its fiscal year: The sustainable growth rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because it assumes that ROE = net profit margin × leverage (omitting asset turnover); or = 8% × 1.2 = 0.096. Substituting into the sustainable growth rate = retention rate × ROE = (1 – 0.10/0.15) × 0.096 = 0.0320 = 3.2%. B. Correct because the sustainable growth rate = retention rate × ROE, where retention rate = (1 – payout ratio), and the payout ratio is the percentage of earnings that the company pays out as dividends to shareholders, or (EPS – DPS) / EPS, and using the DuPont analysis ROE = net profit margin × total asset turnover × leverage. The retention rate = 1 – (0.10 / 0.15) = 1 – 0.667 = 0.3333. ROE = 8% × 1.5 × 1.2 = 0.144. Substituting into the sustainable growth rate formula: 0.3333 × 0.144 = 0.04799 ≈ 4.8%. C. Incorrect because it uses the payout ratio, not retention rate, when calculating the sustainable growth rate (sustainable growth rate = retention rate × ROE). Based on DuPont analysis (ROE = net profit margin × total asset turnover × leverage), ROE = 8% × 1.2 × 1.5, or 0.144; multiplying by the payout ratio = 0.144 × (0.10 / 0.15) = 0.096 = 9.6%.

questions.stem: The book value of a company's equity increases when the company:
questions.option_c: distributes net income as dividends.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the book value of a company’s equity—the difference between its total assets and total liabilities—increases when the company retains its net income. The more net income that is earned (not lost) and retained, the greater the company’s book value of equity. B.Correct because the book value of a company’s equity—the difference between its total assets and total liabilities—increases when the company retains its net income. The more net income that is earned and retained, the greater the company’s book value of equity. C.Incorrect because the book value of a company’s equity—the difference between its total assets and total liabilities—increases when the company retains (not distributes) its net income. The more net income that is earned and retained (not distributed), the greater the company’s book value of equity.

questions.stem: The price of a European put option rises with an increase in the:
questions.option_c: volatility of the underlying.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because for puts, the opposite argument prevails. A longer time to expiration with a higher interest rate lowers the present value of the receipt of the exercise price upon exercise. Thus, the value today of what the put holder might receive at expiration is lower. Therefore, the price of a European put option rises with a decrease, not increase, in the risk-free rate. B.Incorrect because a put option can be viewed as a means of selling the underlying and a put option is logically worth more if the underlying is worth less. Therefore, the price of a European put option rises with a decrease, not increase, in the price of the underlying. C.Correct because with options, volatility of the underlying is universally desirable. The greater the volatility of the underlying, the more an option is worth. In addition, (1) A put option will have a higher payoff the lower the underlying is at expiration. (2) A put option will have a zero payoff if it expires with the underlying above the exercise price. If we could impose greater volatility, we would find that it would have a beneficial effect in (1) because a larger positive payoff would have a greater chance of occurring. In (2), the zero payoff is unaffected. The greater of the option expiring more out-of-the-money is irrelevant. Expiring more out-of-the-money is not worse than expiring less out-of-the-money. Therefore, the price of a European put option rises with an increase in the volatility of the underlying.

questions.stem: Residential mortgage-backed securities issued in the US by government-sponsored enterprises are guaranteed by:
questions.option_c: the full faith and credit of the government.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because RMBS issued by private entities are not guaranteed by a federal agency or GSE and use credit enhancements to reduce risk. B.Correct because for residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS) issued by a GSE (government-sponsored enterprise), such as Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, credit risk is reduced by the guarantee of the GSE itself. C.Incorrect because RMBS issued by a federally related institution, such as Ginnie Mae, are guaranteed by the full faith and credit of the government with respect to timely payment of principal and interest.

questions.stem: The forward price on an underlying asset will increase with an increase in:
questions.option_a: storage costs of the underlying asset.
questions.option_b: interest earned on the underlying asset.
questions.option_c: convenience yield of the underlying asset.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because forward price = F 0 (T) = (S 0 – γ + θ)(1 + r) T = (underlying price – interest earned + storage cost) × (1 + risk free rate)^(time to expiration). Therefore, the forward price will increase with an increase in storage costs of the underlying asset. B.Incorrect because forward price = F 0 (T) = (S 0 – γ + θ)(1 + r) T = (underlying price – interest earned + storage cost) × (1 + risk free rate)^(time to expiration). Therefore, the forward price will increase with a decrease, not increase, in interest earned on the underlying asset. C.Incorrect because forward price = F 0 (T) = (S 0 – (γ – θ))(1 + r) T = (underlying price – convenience yield) × (1 + risk free rate)^(time to expiration). Therefore, the forward price will increase with a decrease, not increase, in convenience yield of the underlying asset.

questions.stem: All else being equal, if futures prices are positively correlated with interest rates, futures contracts are
questions.option_a: less desirable to holders of long positions than are forwards.
questions.option_b: equally desirable to holders of long positions than are forwards.
questions.option_c: more desirable to holders of long positions than are forwards.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because if futures prices are positively correlated with interest rates, futures contracts are more (not less) desirable to holders of long positions than are forwards. B.Incorrect because if futures prices are positively correlated with interest rates, futures contracts are more (not equally) desirable to holders of long positions than are forwards. C.Correct because if futures prices are positively correlated with interest rates, futures contracts are more (not less) desirable to holders of long positions than are forwards.

questions.stem: All else being equal, which of the following are equivalent to cash dividends of equal value in terms of the effect on shareholders wealth?
questions.option_c: Reverse stock splits
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a stock dividend divides the “pie” (the market value of shareholders’ equity) into smaller pieces without affecting the value of the pie or any shareholder’s proportional ownership in the company. Thus, stock dividends are not relevant for valuation. Stock splits and reverse stock splits are similar to stock dividends in that they have no economic effect on the company or shareholders. B.Correct because a share repurchase (or buyback) is a transaction in which a company uses cash to buy back its own shares. Shares that have been repurchased are not considered for dividends, voting, or computing earnings per share. A share repurchase is viewed as equivalent to the payment of cash dividends of equal value in terms of the effect on shareholders’ wealth, all other things being equal. C.Incorrect because a reverse stock split involves a reduction in the number of shares outstanding with a corresponding increase in share price. A stock dividend divides the “pie” (the market value of shareholders’ equity) into smaller pieces without affecting the value of the pie or any shareholder’s proportional ownership in the company. Thus, stock dividends are not relevant for valuation. Stock splits and reverse stock splits are similar to stock dividends in that they have no economic effect on the company or shareholders.

questions.stem: The use of a three-stage dividend discount model is most appropriate for a company that is entering the early stages of its:
questions.option_c: ransition phase.
