Correct because bond yields-to-maturity are annualized (and compounded) and yield measures in the money market are annualized (but not compounded). C. Incorrect because bond yields-to-maturity are annualized and compounded. Yield measures in the money market are annualized but not compounded. Instead, the rate of return on a money market instrument is stated on a simple interest basis.

questions.stem: A 6% 25-year bond with semiannual payments has a market price of $850.00. The yield to maturity of this bond is closest to :
questions.explanation: A. Incorrect because this is the YTM found when reversing the price and face value. B. Correct. The yield to maturity is the discount rate that equates the price of the bond ($850.00) with its cash flows (49 semiannual cash flows of $30 and a 50th cash flow of $1,030), or $850 = $30/(1+YTM/2) 1 + $30/(1+YTM/2) 2 +...+ $1030/(1+YTM/2) 50 Using a financial calculator to find the yield to maturity gives 7.32%. C. Incorrect because this is the YTM found when setting a calculator for 2 payments per year but inputting only 25 payments, rather than 50.

questions.stem: Which of the following contracts is an example of a contingent claim? A(n):
questions.option_c: commodity forward
questions.explanation: A. Correct because there are two general classes of derivatives. Some provide the ability to lock in a price at which one might buy or sell the underlying. Because they force the two parties to transact in the future at a previously agreed-on price, these instruments are called forward commitments . The various types of forward commitments are called forward contracts, futures contracts, and swaps. Another class of derivatives provides the right but not the obligation to buy or sell the underlying at a pre-determined price. Because the choice of buying or selling versus doing nothing depends on a particular random outcome, these derivatives are called contingent claims . The primary contingent claim is called an option . Therefore, a currency option is an example of a contingent claim. B. Incorrect because swaps are forward commitments and not contingent claims. C. Incorrect because forward contracts are forward commitments and not contingent claims. Derivative Instrument and Derivative Market Features

questions.stem: An index provider launches a new index that will include value stocks in a specific country. This index will most likely be a:
questions.option_c: fundamentally weighted index.
questions.explanation: A. Correct because style indexes represent a group of securities classified according to market capitalization, value, and growth or a combination of these characteristics. Therefore, the new index will most likely be a style index with a value classification. B. Incorrect because large-capitalization indexes represent and track the largest securities in terms of market capitalization. They do not represent the category of value stocks. C. Incorrect because fundamentally weighted indexes use measures such as book value, cash flow, revenues, earnings, dividends, and number of employees to weight the constituent securities. Securities of different styles and sectors could be included in the same fundamentally weighted index. Therefore, fundamentally weighted indexes do not represent the category of value stocks.

questions.stem: According to the Standards, which of the following information requires disclosure? Information 1: A member's brother inherits a significant ownership of a stock that is part of the member's research coverage universe. The member has no beneficial ownership in her brother's investments. Information 2: A member, a portfolio manager at an investment firm, does unpaid volunteer work during holiday weekends at a charity. Information 3: Firm enters into an agreement with a mutual fund to receive commissions for recommending the fund to the firm's clients.
questions.option_c: Information 3
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to Standard VI(A), Avoid or Disclose Conflicts, members and candidates must disclose any materially beneficial ownership interest in a security or other investment that the member or candidate is recommending. The member has no beneficial ownership in her brother's investments. Therefore, Information 1 is not required to be disclosed. B.Incorrect because according to Standard VI(A), Avoid or Disclose Conflicts, situations that must be reported to employers include conflicts that would interfere with rendering unbiased investment advice and conflicts that would cause a member or candidate to act not in the employer ’ s best interest. In this case, the member does unpaid volunteer work at a charity during holiday weekends which is her personal time. It does not have conflicts of interest to her employers. Therefore, Information 2 is not required to be disclosed. C.Correct because according to Standard VI(A), Avoid or Disclose Conflicts, disclosures must be made to clients regarding conflicts that may arise in fee arrangements, subadvisory agreements, or other situations involving nonstandard fee structures. Equally important is the disclosure of arrangements in which the firm benefits directly from investment recommendations. Therefore, Information 3 is required to be disclosed, because the firm benefits directly from its recommendation to invest in a certain mutual fund.

questions.stem: According to the Standard relating to suitability, a member should update a client's Investment Policy Statement at least:
questions.option_c: annually.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to Standard III (C), Suitability, updating the IPS should be repeated at least annually (not quarterly). B.Incorrect because according to Standard III (C), Suitability, updating the IPS should be repeated at least annually (not semiannually) C.Correct because according to Standard III (C), Suitability, updating the IPS should be repeated at least annually and also prior to material changes to any specific investment recommendations or decisions on behalf of the client.

questions.stem: Michael Pak has recently retired from the investment business. A CFA Institute member for 20 years, Pak has decided not to pay his CFA Institute dues or file the annual Professional Conduct Statement. Applying to join the investment committee of a charitable organization, Pak writes: “I was a CFA Institute member for 20 years.” Has Pak most likely violated the Standards?
questions.option_b: Yes, the Standard relating to conduct as participants in CFA Institute programs
questions.option_c: Yes, the Standard relating to reference to CFA Institute, the CFA designation, and the CFA Program
questions.explanation: A.Correct because once accepted as a CFA Institute member, the member must satisfy the following requirements to maintain his or her status: lremit annually to CFA Institute a completed Professional Conduct Statement, which renews the commitment to abide by the requirements of the Code and Standards and the CFA Institute Professional Conduct Program, and pay applicable CFA Institute membership dues on an annual basis. If a CFA Institute member fails to meet any of these requirements, the individual is no longer considered an active member. Until membership is reactivated, individuals must not present themselves to others as active members. They may state, however, that they were CFA Institute members in the past or refer to the years when their membership was active. Therefore, Pak has not violated Standard VII (B), Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA Designation, and the CFA Program, by stating: “I was a CFA Institute member for 20 years.” Pak has also not violated Standard VII(A), Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs, which prohibits any conduct that undermines the public's confidence that the CFA charter represents a level of achievement based on merit and ethical conduct. Pak has not engaged in any conduct that undermines the public's confidence about the CFA charter. B.Incorrect because Standard VII(A), Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs, covers the conduct of CFA Institute members and candidates involved with the CFA Program and prohibits any conduct that undermines the public's confidence that the CFA charter represents a level of achievement based on merit and ethical conduct. Pak has not engaged in any conduct that undermines the public's confidence about the CFA charter. Therefore, Pak has not violated Standard VII (A). C.Incorrect because according to Standard VII (B), Reference to CFA Institute, the CFA Designation, and the CFA Program, members may state that they were CFA Institute members in the past or refer to the years when their membership was active. Therefore, Pak has not violated Standard VII (B).

questions.stem: Which of the following is consistent with the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to referral fees? Statement 1: "Investment professionals should provide to their clients notification of approved referral fee programs." Statement 2: "Members should provide their employer at least annual updates on the amount and nature of compensation received."
questions.option_c: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2
questions.explanation: A.Correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard VI (C), Referral Fees, employers should have investment professionals provide to the clients notification of approved referral fee programs. B.Incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard VI (C), Referral Fees, employers should have investment professionals provide the employer regular (at least quarterly) updates on the amount and nature of compensation received. So, the frequency of the updates should be at least quarterly, not at least annually. C.Incorrect because only Statement 1 is correct.

questions.stem: Ritu Jain, CFA, is preparing to leave her firm and join a new employer. Prior to leaving the firm, Jain calls all her clients informing them of her decision to leave. When asked by the clients, Jain states lack of confidence in the firm's leadership as the reason for her departure and also mentions that more employees are likely to leave soon. Jain has violated the Standard(s) relating:
questions.option_c: both to loyalty and to preservation of confidentiality.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because Standard IV(A), Loyalty states that CFA Institute members and candidates must act for the benefit of their employer and not otherwise cause harm to their employer and Jain violates her duty of loyalty to her employer by making disparaging and harmful statements about the firm to its clients. Jain can call her clients to inform of her decision but cannot make disparaging statements about her employer. Also according to Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality, members and candidates preserve the confidentiality of information communicated to them by their clients, prospective clients, and former clients. No client related information is being disclosed and information pertaining to an employer is not covered by this Standard. Hence only the Standard relating to preservation of confidentiality has been violated. B.Incorrect because according to Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality, members and candidates preserve the confidentiality of information communicated to them by their clients, prospective clients, and former clients. No client related information is being disclosed and information pertaining to an employer is not covered by this Standard. This Standard is not violated. C.Incorrect because according to Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality, members and candidates preserve the confidentiality of information communicated to them by their clients, prospective clients, and former clients. No client related information is being disclosed and information pertaining to an employer is not covered by this Standard. This Standard is not violated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a requirement of Standard II, Integrity of Capital Markets? Members and candidates:
questions.option_a: must promote the integrity and viability of the global capital markets for the ultimate benefit of society.
questions.option_b: must not engage in practices that distort prices or artificially inflate trading volume with the intent to mislead market participants.
questions.option_c: who possess material nonpublic information that could affect the value of an investment must not act or cause others to act on the information.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the Code of Ethics of CFA Institute states that members and candidates for the CFA designation must promote the integrity and viability of global capital markets for the ultimate benefit of society. This is not a requirement under Standard II, Integrity of Capital Markets, and so is the correct answer. B.Incorrect because Standard II(B), Market Manipulation, states that members and candidates must not engage in practices that distort prices or artificially inflate trading volume with the intent to mislead market participants. C.Incorrect because Standard II(A), Material Nonpublic Information, states that members and candidates who possess material nonpublic information that could affect the value of an investment must not act or cause others to act on the information.

questions.stem: Benefits of compliance with the GIPS standards least likely include:
questions.option_c: eliminating in-depth due diligence for investors.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because compliance with GIPS standards may strengthen internal controls. B.Incorrect because compliance with GIPS standards enables a firm to participate in competitive bids against other compliant firms around the world. C.Correct compliance with the GIPS standards does not eliminate the need for in-depth due diligence on the part of the investor.

questions.stem: Abe Seneca, CFA, supervises a team of analysts who create index funds for institutional investors. When Seneca makes sales demonstrations without his colleagues to potential clients simulating the fund’s performance, the scenarios he prepares show outcomes based on assumptions reflecting upside bias and positive risk assessments. Gail Tremblay, CFA, an analyst in Seneca’s group, observes that the actual performance of these index funds is less than indicated in the scenario outcomes shown in the sales meetings. Seneca least likely violated which of the following Standards.
questions.option_c: Responsibilities of Supervisors
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Seneca understates risks and only includes positive assumptions in his sales presentations in order to achieve higher simulated performance. This is a violation of Standard IV(A), Loyalty, because he is causing reputational risk to his employer by misleading potential investors on the performance they might achieve with the index funds. Standard IV(A) requires members and candidates to protect the interests of their firm by refraining from any conduct that would injure the firm. B.Incorrect because Seneca understates risks and only includes positive assumptions in his sales presentations in order to achieve higher simulated performance. This is a violation of Standard III(D), Performance Presentation, because the sales demonstrations he conducts do not provide a fair and accurate representation of performance that the clients are likely to experience. C.Correct because Standard IV(C), Responsibilities of Supervisors, has not been violated as Seneca is not responsible for the supervision of any employees when he makes sales demonstrations to clients because he prepared the material himself.

questions.stem: Maria Bendez, CFA, is a well-known analyst. She sends her recommendations to all of her firm clients. However, Bendez does not disseminate her recommendations to the public even though she believes that her recommendations could affect security prices. A client calls her and says: “Maria, thank you! Every time you send me your recommendations, I think you provide me with an advantage over other market participants.” Has Bendez most likely violated the Standards? Maria Bendez, CFA, is a well-known analyst. She sends her recommendations to all of her firm clients. However, Bendez does not disseminate her recommendations to the public even though she believes that her recommendations could affect security prices. A client calls her and says: “Maria, thank you! Every time you send me your recommendations, I think you provide me with an advantage over other market participants.” Has Bendez most likely violated the Standards?
questions.option_b: Yes, the Standard relating to material nonpublic information
questions.option_c: Yes, the Standard relating to material nonpublic information and the Standard relating to fair dealing
questions.explanation: A.Correct because according to Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, when a particularly well-known or respected analyst issues a report or makes changes to his or her recommendation, that information alone may have an effect on the market and thus may be considered material. However, the analyst is not a company insider and thus does not have access to inside information. Simply because the public in general would find the conclusions material does not require that the analyst make his or her work public. Investors who are not clients of the analyst can either do the work themselves or become clients of the analyst to gain access to the analyst's expertise. In this case, Maria simply shares her recommendation with all of her firm clients, and there is no evidence that she uses inside information in her reports. Thus, she did not violate Standard II (A). Bendez also did not violate Standard III (B), Fair Dealing, which states that Members and Candidates must deal fairly and objectively with all clients when (among other things) making investment recommendations. Each member or candidate is obligated to ensure that information is disseminated in such a manner that all clients have a fair opportunity to act on every recommendation. In this case, Bendez did not violate Standard III (B) because she sends her recommendation to all of her clients. B.Incorrect because Bendez has not violated Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, as described in the rationale for the correct answer. C.Incorrect because Bendez has not violated Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, or Standard III (B), Fair Dealing, as described in the rationale for the correct answer.

questions.stem: According to the Standard relating to preservation of confidentiality, a member is required to maintain confidentiality of information communicated to her：
questions.option_c: both by her former clients and by her prospective clients.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality requires that members and candidates preserve the confidentiality of information communicated to them by their clients, prospective clients, and former clients. B.Incorrect because Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality requires that members and candidates preserve the confidentiality of information communicated to them by their clients, prospective clients, and former clients. C.Correct because Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality requires that members and candidates preserve the confidentiality of information communicated to them by their clients, prospective clients, and former clients.

questions.stem: A firm manages $500 million in large-cap equity portfolios. Of this, non-fee-paying portfolios amount to $50 million, and fee-paying non-discretionary portfolios total $75 million. To be compliant with the GIPS standards, the firm must present the value of its large-cap composite as:
questions.option_c: $450 million.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because according to the GIPS standards, a composite must include all actual, fee-paying, discretionary portfolios managed in accordance with the same investment mandate, objective, or strategy. Therefore, to be compliant with the GIPS standards, the firm must present its large-cap composite value as US$375 million, as the firm should exclude US$50 million of non-fee-paying portfolios and US$75 million of fee-paying non-discretionary portfolios. B.Incorrect because the GIPS standards requires firms to include all actual, fee-paying, discretionary portfolios managed in accordance with the same investment mandate. Therefore, large-cap composite value of US$425 million is incorrect because it excludes only fee-paying non-discretionary portfolios from the total portfolio value of US$500 million. As described in the response rationale for the correct answer, the firm must present its large-cap composite value as US$375 million, not as US$425 million. C.Incorrect because the GIPS standards requires firms to include all actual, fee-paying, discretionary portfolios managed in accordance with the same investment mandate. Therefore, the large-cap composite value of US$450 million is incorrect because it excludes only non-fee-paying portfolios from the total portfolio value of US$500 million. As described in the response rationale for the correct answer, the firm must present its large-cap composite value as US$375 million, not as US$ 450 million.

questions.stem: Toni Lynn, CFA, is a research analyst. Lynn relies on her colleagues to determine whether the third-party research she uses is sound. Lynn also uses content from personal blogs and social media websites for her research after concluding it is sound. Has Lynn most likely violated the Standard relating to diligence and reasonable basis?
questions.option_b: Yes, by using content from personal blogs and social media websites for her research
questions.option_c: Yes, by relying on her colleagues to determine whether the third-party research is sound
questions.explanation: A.Correct because according to Standard V(A), Diligence and Reasonable Basis, a member or candidate may rely on others in his or her firm to determine whether secondary or third-party research is sound and use the information in good faith unless the member or candidate has reason to question its validity or the processes and procedures used by those responsible for the research. Also, according to Standard V(A), Diligence and Reasonable basis, the sources of the information and data will influence the level of the review a member or candidate must undertake. Information and data taken from internet sources, such as personal blogs, independent research aggregation websites, or social media websites, likely require a greater level of review than information from more established research organizations. Because relying on her colleagues to check third-party research is permitted; and Standard V(A) does not prohibit using personal blogs and social media websites for her research, Lynn has not violated Standard V(A). B.Incorrect because Lynn most likely has not violated Standard V(A), Diligence and Reasonable Basis, as described in the response rationale of the correct answer. C.Incorrect because Lynn most likely has not violated Standard V(A), Diligence and Reasonable Basis, as described in the response rationale of the correct answer.

questions.stem: Jolene Campbell, CFA, a well-known analyst, is working on a report about XLK Autos (XLK). XLK is developing a fuel-efficient car about which no public information is yet available. Campbell uses financial data and information gathered from automobile experts not connected to XLK about the commercial viability of XLK's project. She then issues a “buy” recommendation on the stock. Campbell sends her report exclusively to her firm's clients even though she expects her report to impact XLK's stock price. Has Campbell most likely violated the Standard relating to material nonpublic information?
questions.option_b: Yes, because she uses information that is not yet public
questions.option_c: Yes, because she fails to make her recommendation public
questions.explanation: A.Correct because according to Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, when a particularly well-known or respected analyst issues a report or makes changes to his or her recommendation, that information alone may have an effect on the market and thus may be considered material. However, simply because the public in general would find the conclusions material does not require that Campbell make her work public. Campbell is not a company insider and does not have access to inside information. Further, according to Standard II (A), the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. For example, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material. In this case, information gathered from automobile experts not connected to XLK about the commercial viability of XLK's project is not material. Therefore, Campbell has not violated Standard II (A) either by using information that is not yet public or by failing to make her recommendation public. B.Incorrect because Campbell has not violated Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, by using information that is not yet public, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer. C.Incorrect because Campbell has not violated Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, by failing to make her recommendation public, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer.

questions.stem: According to the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to additional compensation arrangements, a member should make an immediate written report specifying the proposed compensation arrangements:
questions.option_b: only to her supervisor and to her firm's compliance officer.
questions.option_c: to her supervisor, to her firm's compliance officer, and to her clients.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(B), Additional Compensation Arrangements, members should make an immediate written report to their supervisor and compliance officer specifying any compensation they propose to receive for services. B.Correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(B), Additional Compensation Arrangements, members and candidates should make an immediate written report to their supervisor and compliance officer specifying any compensation they propose to receive for services. C.Incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(B), Additional Compensation Arrangements, members and candidates should make an immediate written report to their supervisor and compliance officer -- and not their clients -- specifying any compensation they propose to receive for services.

questions.stem: Megan Chandra, CFA, allocates an oversubscribed IPO suitable for all the accounts she manages. Chandra does not allocate the IPO her mother’s standard fee-paying account or her husband’s non-fee-paying account. Has Chandra violated the Standards?
questions.option_b: Yes, by not allocating the IPO allocation to her mother’s account
questions.option_c: Yes, by not allocating the IPO allocation to both her husband’s and her mother’s accounts
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Chandra violated the Standards by failing to allocate the IPO to her mother's account, as described in the response rationale of the correct answer. B.Correct because according to Standard VI(B), priority of transactions, family accounts that are client accounts should be treated like any other firm account and should neither be given special treatment nor be disadvantaged because of the family relationship. Therefore, by forgoing allocation to her mother’s fee-paying account, her mother, a client, has been disadvantaged. Chandra acted in accordance with the Standards by forgoing allocations to her husband's non-fee-paying account because according to Standard VI(B), priority of transactions, members or candidates may undertake transactions in accounts for which they are a beneficial owner only after their clients and employers have had adequate opportunity to act on a recommendation. Personal transactions include those made for the member’s or candidate’s own account, for family (including spouse, children, and other immediate family members) accounts. C.Incorrect because Chandra complied with the Standards by not allocating the IPO to her husband's account, as described in the response rationale of the correct answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a recommended procedure for compliance with the Standard relating to misrepresentation? Firms should:
questions.option_a: avoid verifying information from third-party firms for timely trade executions.
questions.option_b: specifically designate which employees are authorized to speak on behalf of the firm.
questions.option_c: periodically review employee correspondence that contains representations of individual qualifications.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because when providing information to clients from a third party, members and candidates share a responsibility for the accuracy of the marketing and distribution materials that pertain to the third party’s capabilities, services, and products. Misrepresentation by third parties can damage the member’s or candidate’s reputation, the reputation of the firm, and the integrity of the capital markets. Members and candidates should encourage their employers to develop procedures for verifying information of third-party firms. So, the recommendation is to verify information, but not to avoid verifying it. B.Incorrect because firms can also help prevent misrepresentation by specifically designating which employees are authorized to speak on behalf of the firm. C.Incorrect because firms can assist member and candidate compliance by periodically reviewing employee correspondence and documents that contain representations of individual or firm qualifications.

questions.stem: A portfolio manager is hired by an executive manager of a trust. The duty of loyalty is owed to the:
questions.option_c: beneficiaries of the trust.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to Standard III (A), Loyalty, Prudence, and Care, when the manager is responsible for the portfolios of pension plans or trusts, however, the client is not the person or entity who hires the manager but, rather, the beneficiaries of the plan or trust. The duty of loyalty is owed to the ultimate beneficiaries. B.Incorrect because according to Standard III (A), Loyalty, Prudence, and Care, when the manager is responsible for the portfolios of pension plans or trusts, however, the client is not the person or entity who hires the manager but, rather, the beneficiaries of the plan or trust. The duty of loyalty is owed to the ultimate beneficiaries. C.Correct because according to Standard III (A), Loyalty, Prudence, and Care, when the manager is responsible for the portfolios of pension plans or trusts, however, the client is not the person or entity who hires the manager but, rather, the beneficiaries of the plan or trust. The duty of loyalty is owed to the ultimate beneficiaries.

questions.stem: According to the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to record retention, who is most likely responsible for maintaining the records that support investment actions?
questions.option_c: The chief compliance officer
questions.explanation: A.Correct, because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with CFA Institute Standard V(C), Record Retention, the responsibility to maintain records that support investment action generally lies with the firm, rather than individuals. B.Incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard V(C), Record Retention, neither research analysts nor the chief compliance officer is responsible for maintaining records that support investment actions. Members and candidates must, however, archive research notes and documents that support their investment-related communications, all of which belong to the firm. Archiving will assist firms in complying with this requirement for preservation of internal or external records. C.Incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard V(C), Record Retention, neither research analysts nor the chief compliance officer is responsible for maintaining records that support investment actions. Members and candidates must, however, archive research notes and documents that support their investment-related communications, all of which belong to the firm. Archiving will assist firms in complying with this requirement for preservation of internal or external records.

questions.stem: To be compliant with the GIPS standards, after a firm presents five years of performance history, it must build up to a minimum of:
questions.option_c: 15 years of compliant performance presentation.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer, after a firm presents a minimum of five years of GIPS-compliant performances, the firm must present an additional year of performance each year, building up to a minimum of 10 years of GIPS-compliant performance, not 7 years of compliant performance. B.Correct because the GIPS standards state: A ﬁrm is required to initially present, at a minimum, ﬁve years of annual investment performance that is compliant with the GIPS standards. If the composite or pooled fund has been in existence less than ﬁve years, the ﬁrm must present performance since the composite or pooled fund inception date. Prospectively, the ﬁrm must present an additional year of performance each year, building up to a minimum of 10 years of GIPS-compliant performance. C.Incorrect because, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer, after a firm presents a minimum of five years of GIPS-compliant performances, the firm must present an additional year of performance each year, building up to a minimum of 10 years of GIPS-compliant performance, not 15 years of compliant performance.

questions.stem: Meghna Shah, CFA, manages a small-cap fund. Applying mosaic theory, Shah concludes that AK Tech (AKT) is overpriced and sells the fund's significant holding in AKT for a profit. Shah is aware that her transaction could impact AKT's price because the position is large enough to require disclosure to stock exchanges. A blog tracking stock exchange news reports Shah's transaction, which leads to 8% decline in AKT's price, causing losses to other investors. Has Shah violated the Standards?
questions.option_b: Yes, the Standard relating to market manipulation
questions.option_c: Yes, the Standard relating to material nonpublic information
questions.explanation: A.Correct because Standard II(B), Market Manipulation, is not intended to preclude transactions undertaken on legitimate trading strategies based on perceived market inefficiencies. The intent of the action is critical to determining whether it is a violation of this standard. Shah sold her fund's stake in AKT. She is not required to sell small quantities of AKT as long as her transaction does not disadvantage investors in her fund. That AKT declined 8% after a blog reported her transaction cannot be held against her. Therefore, Shah has not violated Standard II(B). Also, according to Standard II(A), Material Nonpublic Information, the analyst may use significant conclusions derived from the analysis of public and nonmaterial nonpublic information as the basis for investment recommendations and decisions even if those conclusions would have been material inside information had they been communicated directly to the analyst by a company. Under the “mosaic theory,” financial analysts are free to act on this collection, or mosaic, of information without risking violation. Therefore, Shah has also not violated Standard II(A) by applying mosaic theory to sell AKT. B.Incorrect because Shah did not violate Standard II(B), Market Manipulation, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer. C.Incorrect because Shah did not violate Standard II(A), Material Nonpublic Information, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer.

questions.stem: Praful Chandarana, CFA, is starting a new business to offer investment consulting services to pension fund trustees in response to a new regulation that requires all pension fund Investment Policy Statements (IPS) to be reviewed and approved by an independent CFA charterholder. Prior to starting the new business, he meets with the pension fund regulator to clarify if the CFA charterholder undertaking the IPS review should be a licensed financial advisor by the capital markets regulator. The capital markets regulator requires and grants licenses to those giving investment advice to clients. The pension regulator states that they do not require the CFA charterholder to hold a financial advisor’s license, despite financial-related advice being given to the pension funds during any IPS review. Chandarana therefore starts his new business to undertake IPS reviews without obtaining a financial advisor’s license from the capital markets regulator. Subsequently, when clients of his former employer contact him he informs them of his new company and the services he offers. Does Chandarana most likely violate the Code and Standards?
questions.option_b: Yes, the Standard relating to loyalty
questions.option_c: Yes, the Standard relating to knowledge of the law
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Chandarana failed to obtain a financial advisor’s license. The CFA Code of Ethics requires Chandarana to uphold the rules governing capital markets. Standard I(A), Knowledge of the Law, states that when rules or regulations are in conflict, members must comply with the more strict law, in this case the requirement for financial advisors to be licensed. B.Incorrect because Chandarana is not restricted from speaking with clients of his old employer by Standard IV(A), Loyalty. Chandarana did not contact the old employer’s clients; they contacted him. He did not use the old employer’s contact list. In addition, he is able to inform the clients of his new business after he has left the service of his old employer. C.Correct because the CFA Code of Ethics requires Chandarana to uphold the rules governing financial advisors. However, he failed to do so in the absence of obtaining a financial advisor’s license. Standard I(A), Knowledge of the Law, states that when rules or regulations are in conflict, members must comply with the more strict law, in this case the requirement for financial advisors to be licensed.

questions.stem: Arshani Madan, CFA, develops a product that selects mutual funds based on historical data. Madan tests her methodology and produces simulated performance results. The promotional material for the product does not indicate that the results are simulated. Madan has violated the Standards relating:
questions.option_b: only to communication with clients and prospective clients.
questions.option_c: both to performance presentation and communication with clients and prospective clients.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Madan has violated both Standard III(D), Performance Presentation, and Standard V(B), Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, as described in the response rationale to the correct answer. B.Incorrect because Madan has violated both Standard III(D), Performance Presentation, and Standard V(B), Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, as described in the response rationale to the correct answer. C.Correct because Standard III(D), Performance Presentation, requires members and candidates to provide credible performance information to clients and prospective clients and to avoid misstating performance or misleading clients and prospective clients about the investment performance of members or candidates or their firms. This standard encourages full disclosure of investment performance data to clients and prospective clients. By not disclosing that the results related to the product were simulated Madan has violated Standard III(D). Also, according to Standard V(B), Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, members must disclose to clients and prospective clients the basic format and general principles of the investment processes they use to analyze investments, select securities, and construct portfolios and must promptly disclose any changes that might materially affect those processes. By not disclosing the use of simulated results, Madan has also violated Standard V(B).

questions.stem: With respect to issuer-paid research, members are not required to:
questions.option_a: strictly limit the type of compensation they accept from the covered company.
questions.option_b: fully disclose the nature of compensation received from the covered company.
questions.option_c: accept compensation related only to investment performance of the covered company.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to Standard I (B), independent analysts must also strictly limit the type of compensation that they accept for conducting issuer-paid research. Otherwise, the content and conclusions of the reports could reasonably be expected to be determined or affected by compensation from the sponsoring companies. Compensation that might influence the research report could be direct, such as payment based on the conclusions of the report, or indirect, such as stock warrants or other equity instruments that could increase in value on the basis of positive coverage in the report. In such instances, the independent analyst has an incentive to avoid including negative information or making negative conclusions. B.Incorrect because analysts must engage in thorough, independent, and unbiased analysis and must fully disclose potential conflicts of interest, including the nature of their compensation. Otherwise, analysts risk misleading investors. Thus, members must disclose the general nature of compensation (for example flat fee, performance-based, issuance of equity, etc.) but are not required to disclose the amount of compensation. C.Correct because according to Standard I (B), Independence and Objectivity, independent analysts must also strictly limit the type of compensation that they accept for conducting issuer-paid research. Otherwise, the content and conclusions of the reports could reasonably be expected to be determined or affected by compensation from the sponsoring companies. Compensation that might influence the research report could be direct, such as payment based on the conclusions of the report, or indirect, such as stock warrants or other equity instruments that could increase in value on the basis of positive coverage in the report. In such instances, the independent analyst has an incentive to avoid including negative information or making negative conclusions.

questions.stem: Kush Shah, CFA, is the chief investment officer of an investment firm. Shah discovers during a routine review of the firm's trading system that the firm erroneously bought shares of IY Steel (IYS) for several clients. Shah immediately sells IY shares and realises significant profits for the clients. Later, Shah outsources a portion of the clients' portfolios to an external manager. Shah does not notify the firm's clients about the external manager because the fund's stock selection process remains unchanged. Shah has violated the Standards because he failed to notify the clients:
questions.option_a: only about the erroneous purchase of IY shares.
questions.option_b: only about outsourcing a portion of the clients' portfolios to an external manager.
questions.option_c: about the erroneous purchase of IY shares and about outsourcing a portion of the clients' portfolios to an external manager.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Shah violated the Standard by failing to notify clients both about the erroneous purchase of IY shares and about outsourcing a portion of the clients' portfolios to an external manager, as described in the response rationale to the correct answer. B.Incorrect because Shah violated the Standard by failing to notify clients both about the erroneous purchase of IY shares and about outsourcing a portion of the clients' portfolios to an external manager, as described in the response rationale to the correct answer. C.Correct because according to Standard V(B) relating to Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients, the member or candidate must keep clients and other interested parties informed on an ongoing basis about changes to the investment processes, specially newly identified significant risks and limitations. Thus, the outsourcing to the external manager should be notified to clients. Also Shah, violated V(B) by not disclosing the error in the trading system. Clients should have been informed about the error and the corrective actions the firm was undertaking on their behalf. Hence, both actions constitute a violation of the Standards.

questions.stem: According to the Standard relating to conduct as participants in CFA Institute programs, CFA candidates are permitted to: A.disclose broad topical areas not tested on the exam. B.discuss curriculum material in study groups in preparation for the exam. C.disclose information on formulas tested in the exam after taking the exam.
questions.option_a: disclose broad topical areas not tested on the exam.
questions.option_b: discuss curriculum material in study groups in preparation for the exam.
questions.option_c: disclose information on formulas tested in the exam after taking the exam.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to Standard VII(A), Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs, examples of information that cannot be disclosed by candidates sitting for an exam include broad topical areas and formulas tested or not tested on the exam. B.Correct because Standard VII(A), Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs, does not prohibit candidates from discussing nonconfidential information or curriculum material with others or in study groups in preparation for the exam. C.Incorrect because according to Standard VII(A), Conduct as Participants in CFA Institute Programs, all aspects of the exam, including questions, broad topical areas, and formulas, tested or not tested, are considered confidential until such time as CFA Institute elects to release them publicly.

questions.stem: The Standard relating to misconduct addresses:
questions.option_a: only all conduct that reflects poorly on members' professional integrity.
questions.option_b: only all actions violating trust in members' professional and private lives.
questions.option_c: both all conduct that reflects poorly on members' professional integrity and all actions violating trust in members' professional and private lives.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because Standard I (D), Misconduct, addresses all conduct that reflects poorly on the professional integrity, good reputation, or competence of members and candidates. B.Incorrect because Standard I (D), Misconduct, is primarily aimed at conduct and actions related to a member’s or candidate’s professional life. C.Incorrect because Standard I (D), Misconduct, addresses all conduct that reflects poorly on the professional integrity, good reputation, or competence of members and candidates; the Standard doesn't address all actions in members' private lives.

questions.stem: A firm claiming compliance with the GIPS standards:
questions.option_a: can claim compliance on specific composites.
questions.option_b: is responsible for maintaining that compliance.
questions.option_c: must be verified by an independent third party.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because according to GIPS standards, compliance is a firm-wide process that cannot be achieved on a single product or composite. Further, verification is performed with respect to an entire firm, not on specific composites. Therefore, a firm that claims compliance with the GIPS standards cannot select those composites it is compliant with but must comply on a firm-wide basis. B.Correct because according to GIPS standards, firms that claim compliance with the GIPS standards are responsible for their claim of compliance and for maintaining that compliance. C.Incorrect because according to GIPS standards, once a firm claims compliance with the Standards, they may voluntarily hire an independent third party to perform a verification in order to increase confidence in the firm's claim of compliance. Therefore, a firm that claims compliance with the GIPS standards is not required to perform a verification of its claim of compliance by using an independent third party, but may do so voluntarily.

questions.stem: A company has a fixed $1,100 capital budget and has the opportunity to invest in the four independent projects listed in the table: The combination of projects that provides the best choice is:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. $1,100 investment for an NPV = $200 versus a $1,000 investment for an NPV = $200. B.Incorrect. $1,100 investment for an NPV = $200 versus a $1,000 investment for an NPV = $200. C.Correct. The company should choose the combination of projects that maximizes net present value (NPV) subject to the budget constraint of $1,100.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in $ millions) about a company's current fiscal year: The interest coverage ratio is:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the interest coverage ratio is EBIT ÷ interest payments. EBIT is earnings before interest and taxes. Thus, EBIT = 20 + 2 + 6 = 28. Interest coverage = 28 ÷ 2 = 14. B.Incorrect because the interest coverage ratio is miscalculated as (net income + depreciation + taxes) ÷ interest payments = (20 + 4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 15. C.Incorrect because the interest coverage ratio is miscalculated as EBITDA ÷ interest payments = (20 + 2 + 4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 16.

questions.stem: If trading partners are to benefit from allowing the free movement of factors of production among their members, the trading partners most likely need to form a:
questions.option_c: common market.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. A customs union allows for the flow of goods and services among members and has a common trade policy against non-members. A customs union does not allow the free movement of factors of production among its members. B.Incorrect. A free trade area eliminates barriers against the flow of goods and services among its members, but each country has its own policies with respect to non-members. A free trade area does not allow the free movement of factors of production among its members. C.Correct. A common market allows the free movement of all factors of production among its members. It is a higher level of economic integration than what is available from either a free trade area or a customs union.

questions.stem: With respect to debt securities measured at fair value through other comprehensive income:
questions.option_a: both interest income and unrealized gains and losses are recognized in other comprehensive income.
questions.option_b: interest income is recognized in other comprehensive income while unrealized gains and losses are not recognized.
questions.option_c: interest income is recognized in profit and loss while unrealized gains and losses are recognized in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because, in the case of securities classified as Measured at Fair Value through Other Comprehensive Income (IFRS), or equivalently as Available-for-Sale debt securities (US GAAP), interest income is recognized in profit and loss while unrealized gains and losses are recognized in other comprehensive income. B.Incorrect because, in the case of securities classified as Measured at Fair Value through Other Comprehensive Income (IFRS), or equivalently as Available-for-Sale debt securities (US GAAP), interest income is recognized in profit and loss while unrealized gains and losses are recognized in other comprehensive income. C.Correct because, in the case of securities classified as Measured at Fair Value through Other Comprehensive Income (IFRS), or equivalently as Available-for-Sale debt securities (US GAAP), the income statement shows only the interest income (which is then reflected in retained earnings on the ending balance sheet). The unrealized gain does not appear on the income statement; instead, it would appear on a Statement of Comprehensive Income as Other Comprehensive Income.

questions.stem: For a non-colluding oligopoly with a price leader, the optimal market price is determined by the:
questions.option_c: market's marginal revenue and marginal cost.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because in the case of the dominant firm, with the other firms following the price leader, the optimal price is determined at the output level (of the dominate firm) where MR = MC. The profit-maximizing price is then determined by the output position of the segment of the demand function faced by the dominant firm. Therefore, the optimal price is determined by the dominant firm's portion of the total demand curve (rather than the aggregate or total market demand curve). B.Incorrect because in the case of the dominant firm, with the other firms following the price leader, the optimal price is determined at the output level (of the dominate firm) where MR = MC. The profit-maximizing price is then determined by the output position of the segment of the demand function faced by the dominant firm. Therefore, the optimal price is determined by the dominant firm's portion of the total demand curve (rather than the aggregate or total market demand curve). C.Incorrect because, in an oligopolistic market, the equilibrium price comes from the demand curve, whereas the output level comes from the relationship between marginal revenue and marginal cost. Further, in the case of the dominant firm, with the other firms following the price leader, the optimal price is determined at the output level where MR = MC. The profit-maximizing price is then determined by the output position of the segment of the demand function faced by the dominant firm.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in€thousands) about an electronics manufacturing company: Changes to the allowance for inventory obsolescence have already been reflected in cost of sales. The days of inventory on hand (based on average inventory and 365-day year) for Year 2 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because IFRS state that inventories shall be measured (and carried on the balance sheet) at the lower of cost and net realizable value; Inventory turnover ratio = Cost of sales ÷ Average inventory and Days of inventory on hand = Number of days in period / Inventory turnover ratio. Accordingly, Inventory turnover ratio = 1,000 / [(125 + 120) / 2] ≈ 8.163; and Days of inventory on hand = Number of days in period / Inventory turnover ratio = 365 / 8.163 = 44.7 ≈ 45. B.Incorrect because inventories in both years were measured at cost instead of the lower of cost and net realizable value. Hence, Inventory turnover ratio = 1,000 / [(150 + 120) / 2] = 1,000 / 135 ≈ 7.407; and Days of inventory on hand = 365 / 7.407 = 49.3 ≈ 49. C.Incorrect because inventories in both years were measured at net realizable value instead of the lower of cost and net realizable value. Hence, Inventory turnover ratio = 1,000 / [(125 + 160) / 2] = 1,000 / 142.5 ≈ 7.018; and Days of inventory on hand = 365 / 7.018 = 52.0 ≈ 52.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following probability distribution of a company's earnings: The standard deviation of the company's earnings is closest to:
questions.option_c: $375 million.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the expected value is calculated as E(X) = P(X 1 )X 1 + P(X 2 )X 2 + … + P(X n )X n = 0.25×100 + 0.70×300 + 0.05×600 = 25 + 210 + 30 = 265 and the variance is calculated as σ 2 (X) = E{[X − E(X)] 2 } = 0.25×(100 – 265) 2 + 0.70×(300 – 265) 2 + 0.05×(600 – 265) 2 = 6,806.25 + 857.50 + 5,611.25 = 13,275 and the standard deviation is the positive square root of variance, i.e. 13,2751/2 ≈ $115.22 ≈ $115 million. B.Incorrect because the candidate incorrectly calculates the expected value as the unweighted mean, i.e. E(X) ≠ (100 + 300 + 600)/3 ≈ 333.33. Then the variance is calculated as σ 2 (X) = E{[X − E(X)] 2 } = 0.25×(100 – 333.33) 2 + 0.70×(300 – 333.33) 2 + 0.05×(600 – 333.33) 2 ≈ 13,610.72 + 777.62 + 3,555.64 = 17,943.98 and the standard deviation is the positive square root of variance, i.e. 17,943.981/2 ≈ $133.96 ≈ $134 million. C.Incorrect because the candidate omits the probabilities in the calculation of variance. The candidate calculates the expected value correctly as E(X) = P(X 1 )X 1 + P(X 2 )X 2 + … + P(X n )X n = 0.25×100 + 0.70×300 + 0.05×600 = 25 + 210 + 30 = 265. The candidate then incorrectly calculates the variance as σ 2 (X) = E{[X − E(X)] 2 } ≠ (100 – 265) 2 + (300 – 265) 2 + (600 – 265) 2 = 27,225 + 1,225 + 112,225 = 140,675 and the standard deviation is the positive square root of variance, i.e. 140,6751/2 ≈ $375.07 ≈ $375 million.

questions.stem: Both monetary and fiscal policies can most likely be used by a government to:
questions.option_b: affect the level of interest rates.
questions.option_c: influence the level of economic activity.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. Only fiscal policy can be used to redistribute income and wealth. B.Incorrect. Only monetary policy can be used to affect the level of interest rates. C.Correct. Both monetary and fiscal policies are used to regulate economic activity over time.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is most accurate? Fintech applications:
questions.option_a: can perform tasks at levels surpassing human capabilities.
questions.option_b: eliminate the need for humans in providing investment advice to retail investors.
questions.option_c: use models that outperform traditional statistical models in revealing linear relationships.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because fintech has since advanced into decision-making applications based on complex machine-learning logic, where computer programs are able to 'learn' how to complete tasks over time. In some applications, advanced computer systems are performing tasks at levels far surpassing human capabilities. B.Incorrect because robo-advisers or automated personal wealth management services provide investment services to a larger number of retail investors at lower cost than traditional adviser models can provide. However, as the complexity and size of an investor's portfolio grows, robo-advisers may not be able to sufficiently address the particular preferences and needs of the investor. In the case of extremely affluent investors who may own a greater number of asset types—including alternative investments (e.g., venture capital, private equity, hedge funds, and real estate)—in addition to global stocks and bonds and have greater demands for customization, the need for a team of human advisers, each with particular areas of investment or wealth-management expertise, is likely to endure. C.Incorrect because for extremely large datasets, techniques involving artificial intelligence (AI)—computer systems capable of performing tasks that previously required human intelligence—may be better suited to identify complex, non-linear relationships than traditional quantitative methods and statistical analysis. Therefore, fintech (AI) models are not necessarily better than traditional models in identifying linear relationships.

questions.stem: When estimating a target capital structure, the equity weight associated with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.6 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because this number represents the debt weight, not equity weight. A simple way of transforming a debt-to-equity ratio (D/E) into a weight— that is, D/(D + E)—is to divide D/E by 1 + D/E. In this case the debt weight is 0.6/1.6 = 37.5% B.Incorrect because this number (incorrectly)assumes that a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.6 corresponds to 60% debt. C.Correct because a simple way of transforming a debt-to-equity ratio (D/E) into a weight that is, D/(D + E)is to divide D/E by 1 + D/E. In this case, Debt weight = 0.6/1.6 = 37.5%. If the weight of debt is 37.5%, the weight of equity will be (1-37.5%) = 62.5%.

questions.stem: A company is forecasting 10% organic growth in revenues. The company believes sales volume will grow by 6.4%. The forecasted price/mix impact for the company is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because organic revenue growth is a combination of volume growth and price/mix impact; 1 + organic growth % = (1 + volume growth %) × (1 + price/mix %); 1 + 10% = (1 + 6.4%) × (1 + price/mix %) 1.0338 = 1 + price/mix % price/mix % = 0.0338 ≈ 3.4%. B.Incorrect because it computes price/mix % as (1 + organic growth %) × (1 + volume growth %) – 1; = (1 +10%) × (1 + 6.4%) – 1; = 1.1704 – 1 = 0.1704 ≈ 17.0%. C.Incorrect because it computes price/mix % as organic growth / volume growth – 1; 10% / 6.4% – 1 = 1.5625 – 1 = 0.5625 ≈ 56.3%.

questions.stem: An account has a stated annual interest rate of 3.6% with monthly compounding. The number of years it will take for an initial investment in the account to double is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because with more than one compounding period per year, the future value formula can be expressed as FV N = PV[1 + (r s /m)] mN where rs is the stated annual interest rate, m is the number of compounding periods per year, and N stands for the number of years. Moreover, we can identify r s = 0.036 and m = 12, and for the initial investment to double we must have FV N /PV = 2. Hence, the number of years, N, must satisfy 2 = [1 + (0.036/12)] 12N , which can be solved as N = ln(2)/[12 × ln(1.003)] = 19.2830 ≈ 19.3 years. B.Incorrect because it neglects the monthly compounding and assumes that 3.6% compounds annually. In this case N must satisfy 2 = 1.036 N , or N = ln(2)/ln(1.036) = 19.5986 ≈ 19.6 years. C.Incorrect because it ignores the monthly compounding and uses the rule of 72. To quickly approximate the number of periods, practitioners sometimes use an ad hoc rule called the Rule of 72: Divide 72 by the stated interest rate to get the approximate number of years it would take to double an investment at the interest rate. With an interest rate of 3.6% the rule of thumb gives: 72/3.6 = 20 years. However, the Rule of 72 is only an approximation.

questions.stem: When a company's payables turnover ratio is lower compared to its peers, the company is most likely:
questions.option_b: taking advantage of lenient supplier terms.
questions.option_c: receiving payments from customers faster than its peers.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a payables turnover ratio that is high (low days payable) relative to the industry could indicate that the company is not making full use of available credit facilities; alternatively, it could result from a company taking advantage of early payment discounts. Thus, a lower payable turnover ratio could mean the company has higher days payable and most likely is not taking advantage of early payment discounts. B.Correct because an excessively low turnover ratio (high days payable) could indicate trouble making payments on time, or alternatively, exploitation of lenient supplier terms. C.Incorrect because receiving payments from customers faster than the industry norm impacts the receivables turnover rather than the payables turnover. The number of DSO represents the elapsed time between a sale and cash collection, reflecting how fast the company collects cash from customers to whom it offers credit.

questions.stem: In hypothesis testing, which of the following is stated in terms of population parameters?
questions.option_c: Both the null hypothesis and the alternative hypothesis
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the null and alternative hypotheses are stated in terms of population parameters, and we use sample statistics to test these hypotheses. B.Incorrect because the null and alternative hypotheses are stated in terms of population parameters, and we use sample statistics to test these hypotheses. C.Correct because the null and alternative hypotheses are stated in terms of population parameters, and we use sample statistics to test these hypotheses.

questions.stem: Consider the following 20 items listed in ascending order: The median value of the items is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. It is the value of the 10th item and also the value of the mode, which is the value that appears the most. B.Correct. The median is the value of the middle item of a set of items that has been sorted into ascending or descending order. In an even-numbered sample, we define the median as the mean of the values of items occupying the n/2 and (n + 2)/2 positions (the two middle items). The n/2 item is the 10th item and the (n + 2)/2 item is the 11th item. The value of the 10th item is 3; the value of the 11th item is 5. The mean of 3 and 5 is 4. C.Incorrect. It is the value of the 11th item.

questions.stem: In ESG factor analysis, a company's ownership of stranded assets is most likely considered a(n):
questions.option_c: governance risk.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because environmental factors that are generally considered material in investment analysis include the existence of carbon assets. Stranded assets are carbon-intensive assets at risk of no longer being economically viable because of changes in regulation or investor sentiment. B.Incorrect because stranded assets are an environmental risk, not a social risk. Social factors considered in ESG implementation generally pertain to the management of the human capital of a business. C.Incorrect because the existence of "stranded assets" is more likely related to environmental risk, not a governance risk. Corporate governance can be defined as the system of internal controls and procedures by which individual companies are managed.

questions.stem: Using market levels as signals to measure the likelihood of a geopolitical risk best describes:
questions.option_c: geopolitical risk translation into investment action.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because a signpost is an indicator, market level, data piece, or event that signals a risk is becoming more or less likely. B.Incorrect because scenario analysis is the process of evaluating portfolio outcomes across potential circumstances or states of the world. C.Incorrect because a final step in incorporating geopolitical risk into portfolio management process thus requires that geopolitical risk analysis be translated into investment action as appropriate for investor goals, risk tolerance, and time horizon. This is talking about asset allocation strategy and portfolio management, rather than selecting market levels as indicators.

questions.stem: A rising inventory-sales ratio most likely indicates the economy is undergoing a:
questions.option_c: contraction.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because in a recovery the ratio begins to fall as sales recovery outpaces production. B.Correct because in a slowdown the inventory-sales ratio increases, signaling a weakening economy. C.Incorrect because in a contraction the ratio begins to fall back to normal.

questions.stem: Compared with its net income, a mature company’s operating cash flow is most likely:
questions.option_c: higher.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. For a mature company, net income includes non-cash expenses (depreciation and amortization), so it is expected and desirable for operating cash flow exceeds net income. If operating cash flows were lower than net income, this would be an indication of poor earnings quality. B.Incorrect. For a mature company, net income includes non-cash expenses (depreciation and amortization), so it is expected and desirable for operating cash flow to exceed net income, not for them to be equal. C.Correct. For a mature company, because net income includes non-cash expenses (depreciation and amortization), operating cash flow typically exceeds net income.

questions.stem: A firm reports sales of €50,000 for a year ended 31 December. Its accounts receivable balances were €6,000 on 1 January of the year and €7,500 on 31 December. The company’s cash collections from sales for the year is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. It is sales less the end receivables: €50,000 – €7,500 = €42,000. B.Correct. Cash collections from sales equals beginning receivables plus sales less ending receivables: €6,000 + €50,000 – €7,500 = €48,500 C.Incorrect. It is sales plus the change in receivables: €50,000 + (€7,500 – €6,000) = €51,500.

questions.stem: Which of the following most likely enforces financial reporting requirements?
questions.option_c: Both regulatory authorities and standard-setting bodies
questions.explanation: A.Correct because regulatory authorities require publicly traded issuers to prepare financial reports in accordance with specified accounting standards and other securities laws and regulations. Although technically not a regulatory authority, IOSCO regulates a significant portion of the world’s financial capital markets. To ensure consistent application of international financial standards (such as the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s standards and IFRS), it is important to have uniform regulation and enforcement across national boundaries. B.Incorrect because regulatory authorities require publicly traded issuers to prepare financial reports in accordance with specified accounting standards and other securities laws and regulations. C.Incorrect because regulatory authorities require publicly traded issuers to prepare financial reports in accordance with specified accounting standards and other securities laws and regulations.

questions.stem: The following is an excerpt from the note to the financial statements on intangible assets for a company: Intangible Assets (€ millions) As of end of Year 2, licenses with a net book value of €2,530 million have been pledged as security against borrowings. The percentage of intangible assets pledged as security against borrowings in Year 2 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. In incorrectly uses cost information instead of book value to calculate the percentage, giving €2,530/€25,459 = 9.9%. B.Correct. The percentage of intangible assets pledged as security against borrowings in Year 2 is closest to 15.0% (€2,530/€16,874 = 15.0%). C.Incorrect. It incorrectly uses the book value for only licenses when calculating the percentage, giving €2,530/€16,594 = 15.3%.

questions.stem: If differences between accounting profit and taxable income are recoverable, deferred tax assets are created when:
questions.option_a: accounting profit is less than taxable income.
questions.option_b: accounting profit is greater than taxable income.
questions.option_c: income taxes payable is less than income tax expense.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because deferred tax assets arise when an excess amount is paid for income taxes (taxable income higher than accounting profit) and the company expects to recover the difference during the course of future operations. B.Incorrect because it has the relationship reversed. Deferred tax assets arise when an excess amount is paid for income taxes (taxable income higher than accounting profit) and the company expects to recover the difference during the course of future operations. C.Incorrect because it has the relationship reversed; when income taxes payable exceed income tax expense, that creates a deferred tax asset. Deferred tax assets arise when an excess amount is paid for income taxes (taxable income higher than accounting profit) and the company expects to recover the difference during the course of future operations.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding inventory valuation is most accurate?
questions.option_a: IFRS defines market value as net realizable value less a normal profit margin.
questions.option_b: Both IFRS and US GAAP allow the reversal of write-downs back to the original cost.
questions.option_c: Both IFRS and US GAAP allow agricultural inventories to be valued at net realizable value.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. IFRS defines net realizable value as selling price less costs to get it ready to sell and to make the sale. B.Incorrect. US GAAP does not allow reversal of a write-down generally. C.Correct. Both IFRS and US GAAP allow agricultural inventories to be valued at net realizable value.

questions.stem: Assume the percentage increases in each of the following listed items: The predicted change in the nominal US spot exchange rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the change in the real exchange rate is not included: [(1 + 1.5%)/(1 + 2%)] -1 = -0.5%. B.Correct. Change in the nominal exchange rate: = (1+%ΔReal Exchange rate(USD/EUR)) × [(1+%ΔUS price level)/(1+%ΔEurozone price level)]-1 = (1+5%) × [(1+1.5%)/(1+2%)] – 1 = 4.5% C.Incorrect because the change in the price levels are inverted: (1 + 5%) × [(1 + 2%)/(1 + 1.5%)] – 1 = 5.5%.

questions.stem: Based on each company’s debt-to-capital and financial leverage ratios, which company is the most solvent?
questions.option_c: Company C
questions.explanation: A.Correct. Company A is the most solvent based on the calculation of the debt-to-capital and financial leverage ratios because each of the two ratios has the lowest value relative to the ratios of Companies B and C. Company A’s debt-to-capital ratio = Total Debt/(Total Debt + Total Shareholders’ Equity) = $12,796/($12,796 + $32,000) = $12,796/$44,796 = 0.29 Company A’s financial leverage ratio = Average Total Assets/Average Shareholders’ Equity = $42,979/$30,295 = 1.42 B.Incorrect because Company B has a higher debt-to-capital ratio relative to Company A and has the highest financial leverage ratio of the three companies. Both of Company B’s ratios imply weaker solvency relative to Company A, and to Company A and C in the case of the financial leverage ratio. Company B’s debt-to-capital ratio = Total Debt/(Total Debt + Total Shareholders’ Equity) = $44,030/($44,030 + $82,000) = $44,030/$126,030 = 0.35 Company B’s financial leverage ratio = Average Total Assets/Average Shareholder’s Equity = $201,536/$80,970 = 2.49 C.Incorrect because Company C has the highest debt-to-capital ratio of the three companies, and a higher financial leverage ratio relative to Company A. Both of Company C’s ratios imply weaker solvency relative to Company A and to Company A and B in the case of the debt-to-capital ratio. Company C’s debt-to-capital ratio = Total Debt/(Total Debt + Total Shareholders’ Equity) = $8,115/($8,115 + $6,000) = $8,115/$14,115 = 0.57 Company C’s financial leverage ratio = Average Total Assets/Average Shareholder’s Equity =$13,970/$5,741 = 2.43

questions.stem: An investor is considering three investments: Investment 1 makes 20 annual payments of $50,000, starting one year from today. Investment 2 makes 25 annual payments of $45,000, starting today. Investment 3 makes annual payments of $40,000 indefinitely, starting one year from today. If the investor's discount rate is 10% per year, which investment has the highest present value?
questions.option_c: Investment 3
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Investment 2 has the highest present value. Investment 1 is an ordinary annuity with a present value calculated as PV = A[(1 – 1/(1 + r) N )/r], where A is the annual payment, N is the number of payments, and r is the discount rate. Therefore, PV = $50,000 × [(1 – 1/(1.1) 20 )/0.1] = $425,678. Calculator solution (END mode): I/Y = 10%; PMT = 50,000; N = 20; solve for PV = 425,678. A candidate could choose this if Investment 2 is mistaken for an ordinary annuity such that PV of Investment 2 = 408,467. Calculator solution (END mode): I/Y = 10%; PMT = 45,000; N = 25; solve for PV = 408,467. B.Correct because Investment 2 has the highest present value. Investment 2 is an annuity due with a present value calculated as PV = A[(1 – 1/(1 + r) N )/r] × (1 + r), where A is the annual payment, N is the number of payments, and r is the discount rate. Therefore, PV = $45,000 × [(1 – 1/(1.1) 25 )/0.1] × (1.1) = $449,313. Calculator solution (BGN mode): I/Y = 10%; PMT = 45,000; N = 25; solve for PV = 449,313. C.Incorrect because Investment 2 has the highest present value. Investment 3 is a perpetuity with a present value calculated as PV = A/r, where A is the annual payment and r is the discount rate. Therefore, PV = $40,000/0.1 = $400,000.

questions.stem: Under US GAAP, which of the following should be reported separately from continuing operations on the income statement?
questions.option_b: Gain or loss from sale of an asset
questions.option_c: Results of discontinued operations
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because IFRS require that items of income or expense that are material and/or relevant to the understanding of the entity’s financial performance should be disclosed separately. Unusual or infrequent items are likely to meet these criteria. Under US GAAP, material items that are unusual or infrequent, and that are both as of reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2015, are shown as part of a company’s continuing operations but are presented separately. For example, restructuring charges, such as costs to close plants and employee termination costs, are considered part of a company’s ordinary activities. B.Incorrect because IFRS require that items of income or expense that are material and/or relevant to the understanding of the entity’s financial performance should be disclosed separately. Unusual or infrequent items are likely to meet these criteria. Under US GAAP, material items that are unusual or infrequent, and that are both as of reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2015, are shown as part of a company’s continuing operations but are presented separately. For example, gains and losses arising when a company sells an asset or part of a business, for more or less than its carrying value, are also disclosed separately on the income statement. These sales are considered ordinary business activities. C.Correct because both IFRS and US GAAP specify that the results of discontinued operations should be reported separately from continuing operations. When a company disposes of or establishes a plan to dispose of one of its component operations and will have no further involvement in the operation, the income statement reports separately the effect of this disposal as a “discontinued” operation under both IFRS and US GAAP.

questions.stem: A company receives a subscription payment for a publication to be delivered next fiscal year. Ignoring income taxes, the company would recognize in the current fiscal year an increase in:
questions.option_c: liabilities and revenue.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because no revenue is recognized in the P&L as the publication is to be delivered in the next fiscal year.
