B.Correct because there are situations when a company receives cash in advance and actually delivers the product or service later, perhaps over a period of time. In this case, the company would record a liability for unearned revenue when the cash is initially received, and revenue would be recognized as being earned over time as products and services are delivered. An example would be a subscription payment received for a publication that is to be delivered periodically over time. Therefore, the liability for unearned revenue would be recognized, but no revenue recognized in the P&L as the payment was for delivery in future accounting periods. The cash received would be recognized as the asset. C.Incorrect because no revenue is recognized in the P&L as the publication is to be delivered in the next fiscal year.

questions.stem: An analyst examines the following quarterly returns for a client's portfolio: If the target return is 5% per quarter, the target downside deviation is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the target semideviation = Sum(for all X i <= B) [(X i – B) 2 /(n – 1)] 1/2 . The calculations are as follows: Target semideviation = [142/(8 – 1)] 1/2 = 4.504% or 4.50%. B.Incorrect because the target semideviation is calculated using the wrong formula (not dividing by n – 1): Sum(for all X i <= B) [(X i – B) 2 )] 1/2 . The calculations are as follows: Incorrect target semideviation = (142) 1/2 = 11.916% or 11.92%. C.Incorrect because the target semideviation is calculated using the wrong formula (not taking the square root): Sum(for all X i <= B) (X i – B) 2 /(n – 1).The calculations are as follows: Incorrect target semideviation = 142/(8 – 1) = 20.286% or 20.29%.

questions.stem: A central bank most likely:
questions.option_a: will not lend money to banks facing shortages.
questions.option_b: is a monopoly supplier of a country's currency.
questions.option_c: does not manage a country's foreign currency reserves.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because most central banks act as a lender of last resort to banks. Because the central bank effectively has the capacity to print money, it is in the position to be able to supply the funds to banks that are facing a damaging shortage. B.Correct because generally, a central bank is the monopoly supplier of the currency. C.Incorrect because most central banks will also be responsible for managing their country’s foreign currency reserves.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about prediction intervals is most accurate? All else being equal:
questions.option_a: the width of the prediction interval does not depend on the standard error of the estimate.
questions.option_b: a smaller variation of the independent variable will result in a narrower prediction interval.
questions.option_c: a larger sample size in the regression estimation will result in a smaller standard error of the forecast.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the better the fit of the regression model, the smaller the standard error of the estimate (s e ) and, therefore, the smaller standard error of the forecast. Moreover, once we have this estimate of the standard error of the forecast, determining a prediction interval around the predicted value of the dependent variable (Ŷ f ) is very similar to estimating a confidence interval around an estimated parameter. The prediction interval is Ŷ f ± t critical for α/2 s f . Thus, a smaller standard error of the estimate will result in a narrower prediction interval. B.Incorrect because the standard error of the forecast is s f = s e (1 + 1/n + (X f –X) 2 /Σ i=1 n (X i –X) 2 ) 0.5 The standard error of the forecast depends on the variation of the independent variable [ Σ i=1 n (X i – X) 2 ] From the equation of the standard error of the forecast, the smaller variation of the independent variable will increase the standard error of the forecast, and thus will result in a wider prediction interval. C.Correct because the larger the sample size (n) in the regression estimation, the smaller the standard error of the forecast. This is evident from the equation for the standard error of the forecast, which is s f = s e (1 + 1/n + (X f –X) 2 /Σ i=1 n (X i –X) 2 ) 0.5

questions.stem: In capital investment decisions, project sequencing is most likely a type of:
questions.option_c: fundamental option.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because project sequencing is a type of timing option. Delaying an investment and basing the decision on hopefully improved information that you might have in, say, a year could help improve the NPV of the projects selected. Project sequencing options allow the company to defer the decision to invest in a future investment until the outcome of some or all of a current investment is known. B.Incorrect because project sequencing is a type of timing option, not a type of flexibility option. Once an investment is made, operational flexibilities besides abandonment or expansion may be available. Management may be able to exercise a price-setting option, which is a flexibility option to benefit from excess demand. There are also production flexibility options which offer the operational flexibility to alter production when demand varies from what is forecast. C.Incorrect because project sequencing is a type of timing option, not a type of fundamental option. A fundamental option exists in cases where the whole investment is essentially an option. The payoffs from the investment are contingent on an underlying asset, just like most financial options.

questions.stem: The arithmetic and geometric mean are calculated for the same data. If there is variability in the data, compared with the arithmetic mean, the geometric mean will most likely be:
questions.option_c: greater.
questions.explanation: A.Correct. The geometric mean is always less than or equal to the arithmetic mean. The only time the two means will be equal is when there is no variability in the observations. B.Incorrect. The geometric mean is typically less than the arithmetic mean. C.Incorrect. The geometric mean is typically less than the arithmetic mean.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in € millions) about a company's land reported under the revaluation model: As a result of the second revaluation, the company recognizes in Year 2:
questions.option_a: a €5 million loss on the income statement.
questions.option_b: a €5 million loss in other comprehensive income.
questions.option_c: neither a loss on the income statement nor a loss in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it assumes that the second revaluation impacts the income statement rather than the revaluation surplus account. If a revaluation initially increases the carrying amount of the asset class, the increase in the carrying amount of the asset class bypasses the income statement and goes directly to equity under the heading of revaluation surplus. Any subsequent decrease in the asset's value first decreases the revaluation surplus and then goes to income. B.Correct because if a revaluation initially increases the carrying amount of the asset class, the increase in the carrying amount of the asset class bypasses the income statement and goes directly to equity under the heading of revaluation surplus. Any subsequent decrease in the asset's value first decreases the revaluation surplus and then goes to income. Under IFRS, other comprehensive income includes certain changes in the value of long-lived assets that are measured using the revaluation model rather than the cost model. After initial revaluation, the revaluation surplus is thus 17 – 12 = 5. The second revaluation decreases the revaluation surplus by 5. C.Incorrect because it compares the result of the second revaluation to the initial cost, thus resulting in neither a loss on the income statements nor a decrease in the revaluation surplus account. If a revaluation initially increases the carrying amount of the asset class, the increase in the carrying amount of the asset class bypasses the income statement and goes directly to equity under the heading of revaluation surplus. Any subsequent decrease in the asset's value first decreases the revaluation surplus and then goes to income.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about kurtosis is most accurate?
questions.option_a: A fat-tailed distribution is referred to as platykurtic.
questions.option_b: All distributions with kurtosis above zero are fat-tailed.
questions.option_c: The calculation for kurtosis involves finding the average of deviations from the mean raised to the fourth power.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a distribution that has fatter tails than the normal distribution is referred to as leptokurtic, not platykurtic. B.Incorrect because a fat-tailed distribution has a kurtosis of above 3. So not all distributions with kurtosis above 0 are fat-tailed. C.Correct because the calculation for kurtosis involves finding the average of deviations from the mean raised to the fourth power and then standardizing that average by dividing by the standard deviation raised to the fourth power.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary source of liquidity?
questions.option_c: Short-term investment portfolio ​
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because primary sources of liquidity represent the most readily accessible resources available to the company. These can be cash held or near-cash securities and include free cash flow, which is the firm’s after-tax operating cash flow less planned short- and long-term investments. B.Correct because the main difference between primary and secondary sources of liquidity is that using a primary source is not likely to affect the normal operations of the company, whereas using a secondary source might result in a change in the company’s financial and operating positions. Secondary sources used by companies include negotiating debt contracts, such as relieving pressures from high interest payments or principal repayments, waiving debt covenants or suspending dividends. C.Incorrect because primary sources of liquidity represent the most readily accessible resources available to the company. These can be cash held or near-cash securities and include short-term funds, which can include items such as trade credit, bank lines of credit, and short-term investment portfolios of the firm.

questions.stem: An analyst calculates the following metrics about a sample of paired observations of a dependent variable Y and an independent variable X: Based on the sample, the slope coefficient of the simple linear regression of Y to X is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it used the variance of Y, and not the variance of X, in the denominator, and calculates the slope = 12 / 1. It is also closest to the inverse of the correct answer, 9/12 = 0.75. B.Incorrect because it is the sample correlation between X and Y, and not the slope of the linear regression. The sample correlation, r, is the ratio of the covariance to the product of the standard deviations, and thus equals 12 / ((9 0.5 )(15 0.5 )) = 12 / 11.62 = 1.0328 ≈ 1.03. C.Correct because the slope of a linear regression is the ratio of the covariance between Y and X to the variance of X, thus slope = 12/9 ≈ 1.33.

questions.stem: A company's ability to support debt most likely improves with a(n):
questions.option_c: decrease in interest coverage.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because in general, companies with higher liquidity and profitability have a greater ability to support greater use of debt in their capital structures. Increased liquidity and higher interest coverage strengthens the ability to support debt. B.Incorrect because higher leverage weakens the ability to support debt. In general, companies with higher liquidity and profitability have a greater ability to support greater use of debt in their capital structures. C.Incorrect because lower interest coverage weakens the ability to support debt. The larger the interest coverage ratio, the larger the financial cushion and the greater the company's ability to service its debt obligations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an assumption in Modigliani and Miller’s capital structure framework?
questions.option_a: Investors can lend and borrow at the risk free rate
questions.option_b: Interest expense is deductible from income for tax purposes
questions.option_c: Investors have heterogeneous expectations about future corporate earnings
questions.explanation: A.Correct because given their assumptions, Modigliani and Miller proved that changing the capital structure does not affect firm value, in part because individual investors can create any capital structure they prefer for the company by borrowing and lending in their own accounts in addition to holding shares in the company. This 'homemade' leverage argument relies on the MM assumption that investors can lend and borrow at the risk-free rate. B.Incorrect because the assumption is that investors can borrow and lend at the risk free rate. In their theoretical framework, MM assumed that all investors have homogeneous expectations about expected future corporate earnings and the riskiness of those earnings. Their assumptions, including a world of perfect capital markets—in which there are no taxes, no transaction costs, and no bankruptcy costs, and all investors have equal (“symmetric”) information. C.Incorrect because the assumption is that investors have homogeneous and not heterogeneous expectations about future earnings. In their theoretical framework, MM assumed that all investors have homogeneous expectations about expected future corporate earnings and the riskiness of those earnings. Their assumptions, including a world of perfect capital markets—in which there are no taxes, no transaction costs, and no bankruptcy costs, and all investors have equal (“symmetric'”) information.

questions.stem: Which of the following sampling methods involves selecting every kth member from a population until a desired sample size is obtained?
questions.option_c: Convenience sampling
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because in this method, the population is divided into clusters, each of which is essentially a mini-representation of the entire populations Then certain clusters are chosen as a whole using simple random sampling. B.Correct because with systematic sampling, we select every kth member until we have a sample of the desired size. The sample that results from this procedure should be approximately random. C.Incorrect because in this method, an element is selected from the population based on whether or not it is accessible to a researcher or on how easy it is for a researcher to access the element. Because the samples are selected conveniently, they are not necessarily representative of the entire population, and hence the level of the sampling accuracy could be limited.

questions.stem: A company's interest payments are fully tax deductible. When tax rates increase, the company's cost of debt:
questions.option_c: increases.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the marginal cost of debt financing is the cost of debt after considering the allowable deduction for interest on debt. Based on the country’s tax law the marginal cost of debt is r d (1 – t). Therefore, if tax rates increase the after-tax cost of debt will decrease. B.Incorrect because when interest is deductible, the marginal cost of debt is equal to r d (1 – t). If tax rates increase, the cost of debt will decrease, not remain the same. C.Incorrect because the cost of debt would decrease, not increase. The marginal cost of debt financing is the cost of debt after considering the allowable deduction for interest on debt based on the country’s tax law. The marginal cost of debt is r d (1 – t).

questions.stem: A corporate takeover in which shareholders are persuaded to vote for a group seeking a controlling position on the board of directors best describes a:
questions.option_c: hostile takeover.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because managerial teams can also be displaced through a tender offer, which involves shareholders selling their interests directly to the group seeking to gain control. A tender offer does not involve a vote. B.Correct because in a proxy contest, shareholders are persuaded to vote for a group seeking a controlling position on a company's board of directors. C.Incorrect because a hostile takeover is an attempt by one entity to acquire a company without the consent of the company's management. A hostile takeover does not involve a vote.

questions.stem: Which of the following most likely provides an opportunity for a company's management to issue low-quality financial reports?
questions.option_c: Incentive compensation based on earnings
questions.explanation: A.Correct because, typically, three conditions exist when low-quality financial reports are issued: opportunity, motivation, and rationalization. Opportunity can be the result of internal conditions, such as poor internal controls or an ineffective board of directors. B.Incorrect because this represents a motivation, not an opportunity, for issuing low-quality financial reports. Career concerns and incentive compensation may motivate accounting choices. For example, managers might be concerned that working for a company that performs poorly will limit their future career opportunities or that they will not receive a bonus based on exceeding a particular earnings target. In both cases, management might be motivated to make accounting choices to increase earnings. Concern about future career opportunities is an example of motivation for issuing low-quality financial reports rather than an opportunity for doing so. C.Incorrect because this represents a motivation, not an opportunity, for issuing low-quality financial reports. Career concerns and incentive compensation may motivate accounting choices. For example, managers might be concerned that working for a company that performs poorly will limit their future career opportunities or that they will not receive a bonus based on exceeding a particular earnings target. In both cases, management might be motivated to make accounting choices to increase earnings. Incentive compensation based on exceeding a particular earnings target is an example of motivation for issuing low-quality financial reports rather than an opportunity for doing so.

questions.stem: Quantitative easing addresses the monetary policy challenges most likely caused by:
questions.option_c: inflationary demand shocks or supply shocks.
questions.explanation: A.Correct. In a deflationary environment, reducing rates below zero may become ineffective and result in a liquidity trap. The next step to deter deflation is quantitative easing. B.Incorrect. Bond market vigilantes act on long-term rates when they determine that the central bank lacks credibility or is ineffective in its policy implementation. C.Incorrect. Demand shocks and supply shocks that cause increases in inflation would not be addressed by quantitative easing. Such an action would exacerbate inflation.

questions.stem: The NZD/EUR (amount of NZD per 1 EUR) spot rate is 1.5453. If the 3-month forward discount is 24 points, the 3-month forward rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because if the forward rate is less than the spot rate, the points (forward rate minus spot rate) are negative and the base currency is said to be trading at a forward discount. To convert quoted forward points into a forward rate, one would divide the number of points by 10,000 (to scale down to the fourth decimal place, the last decimal place in the spot quote) and then add the result to the spot exchange rate quote. Therefore, scaling down the forward points by dividing by 10,000 gives a forward discount of 24/10,000 = 0.0024. Since it is a discount, subtracting it from the spot rate results in a three-month forward rate of 1.5453 – 0.0024 = 1.54290. B.Incorrect because it adds, rather than subtracts, the forward discount; 1.5453 + 0.0024 = 1.54770. C.Incorrect because it multiplies the spot rate by (1 + the forward discount) rather than adding it; 1.5453 × (1 + 0.0024) ≈ 1.54901.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in £ thousands) about equipment owned by a company: The equipment is considered impaired under:
questions.option_c: both IFRS and US GAAP.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the equipment is impaired under IFRS. Under IAS 36, an impairment loss is measured as the excess of carrying amount over the recoverable amount of the asset. The recoverable amount of an asset is defined as ‘the higher of its fair value less costs to sell and its value in use.' Value in use is a discounted measure of expected future cash flows. In this case, the carrying amount is £36; and the recoverable amount is £32, which is higher of fair value less costs to sell (34-4=30) and its value in use (32); Therefore, the impairment loss is £4 (36 – 32). B.Incorrect because the equipment is not impaired under US GAAP. Under US GAAP, assessing recoverability is separate from measuring the impairment loss. An asset's carrying amount is considered not recoverable when it exceeds the undiscounted expected future cash flows. If the asset's carrying amount is considered not recoverable, the impairment loss is measured as the difference between the asset's fair value and carrying amount. In this case, the carrying amount (36) does NOT exceed the undiscounted expected future cash flows (38), so the carrying amount is considered recoverable, so the equipment is not considered impaired. C.Incorrect because the equipment is considered impaired under IFRS and not impaired under US GAAP, as explained above.

questions.stem: For a company paying preferred dividends, the components needed to compute basic EPS are net income: A.and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding. B.preferred dividends, and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding. C.preferred dividends, additional shares issued if preferred is converted, and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding.
questions.option_a: and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding.
questions.option_b: preferred dividends, and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding.
questions.option_c: preferred dividends, additional shares issued if preferred is converted, and the weighted average number of common shares outstanding.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because preferred dividends must be subtracted from net income before dividing by the weighted average number of shares outstanding. B.Correct. Basic EPS is calculated by subtracting preferred dividends from net income and then dividing the result by the weighted average number of shares outstanding. C.Incorrect because basic EPS is not adjusted for additional ordinary shares issued, an adjustment which uses the if-converted method for potentially dilutive securities. This method is applicable when determining diluted EPS.

questions.stem: A company's cash contribution to its defined contribution pension plan is recorded on the company's statement of cash flows as a(n):
questions.option_c: financing cash outflow.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because under a defined-contribution plan, a company contributes an agreed-upon (defined) amount into the plan. The agreed-upon amount is the pension expense. The amount the company contributes to the plan is treated as an operating cash outflow. B.Incorrect because the amount the company contributes to the plan is treated as an operating cash outflow, not an investing cash outflow. C.Incorrect because the amount the company contributes to the plan is treated as an operating cash outflow, not a financing cash outflow.

questions.stem: Assume that a central bank has decided to lower interest rates in the economy. To carry out this policy, the central bank will most likely:
questions.option_c: increase required reserve requirements.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. If the central bank sells securities, reserves fall and interest rates are likely to increase. B.Correct. In implementing monetary policy, central banks have three primary tools available to them: open market operations (which including purchasing securities), setting the official policy rate, and reserve requirements. When the central bank purchases securities, it increases the reserves held by private sector banks. These increased reserves lead to a reduction in interest rates on money market securities and, ultimately, to a reduction in other interest rates in the economy. C.Incorrect. An increased reserve requirement reduces the money supply (as banks can lend out less) and leads to higher interest rates.

questions.stem: Part of the conflict between shareholders and debtholders is that shareholders prefer:
questions.option_c: greater financial leverage than debtholders.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because debtholders with a fixed claim tend to be risk averse and prefer that the corporation take actions to ensure sufficient cash flow to meet its debt obligations. B.Incorrect because debtholders tend to prefer that a company raise more equity and limit shareholder distributions. Shareholders, however, tend to prefer greater leverage and shareholder distributions rather than dilutive equity issuance. C.Correct because shareholders, however, tend to prefer greater leverage and shareholder distributions rather than dilutive equity issuance.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company's capital sources: If the marginal tax rate is 20% and interest expense is tax deductible, the company's WACC is:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because taking the sources of capital to be common stock, preferred stock, and debt and allowing for the fact that in some jurisdictions, interest expense may be tax deductible, the expression for WACC is: WACC = w d r d (1 – t) + w p r p + w e r e , where w d = the target proportion of debt in the capital structure when the company raises new funds; r d = the before-tax marginal cost of debt; t = the company’s marginal tax rate; w p = the target proportion of preferred stock in the capital structure when the company raises new funds [which is equal to 0 in our case]; r p = the marginal cost of preferred stock; w e = the target proportion of common stock in the capital structure when the company raises new funds; r e = the marginal cost of common stock. Thus, WACC = 0.25 × 4% × (1 – 20%) + 0.75 × 12% = 9.80%. B.Incorrect because it ignores that interest expense is tax deductible and calculates the WACC as w d r d + w e r e = 0.25 × 4% + 0.75 × 12% = 10.00%. C.Incorrect because, instead of multiplying, it divides the cost of debt by (1 – t), thus calculating the WACC as w d r d /(1 – t) + w e r e = 0.25 × 4%/(1 – 20%) + 0.75 × 12% = 10.25%.

questions.stem: An analysis used to forecast earnings that shows the changes in key financial quantities that result from alternative sets of economic events best describes which of the following techniques?
questions.option_c: Scenario analysis
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. Simulation is a computer-generated sensitivity or scenario analysis based on probability models for the factors that drive outcomes. B.Incorrect. Sensitivity analysis, also known as “what if” analysis, shows the range of possible outcomes as specific assumptions are changed. C.Correct. Scenario analysis shows the changes in key financial quantities that result from given economic events, such as the loss of customers or a catastrophic event.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely a feature of sole proprietorships?
questions.option_c: Taxation of business profits as personal income
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because key features of sole proprietorships include operational simplicity and flexibility. B.Incorrect because key features of sole proprietorships include no legal identity. C.Correct because key features of sole proprietorships include profits from business taxed as personal income.

questions.stem: With respect to the cash flow statement, under US GAAP, interest paid is reported as a(n):
questions.option_c: operating activity.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because under US GAAP, interest paid is not reported as an investing activity. B.Incorrect because under US GAAP, interest paid is not reported as a financing activity. C.Correct because under US GAAP, interest paid is reported as an operating activity.

questions.stem: An expansionary fiscal policy is least likely to include an increase in:
questions.option_c: government expenditures.
questions.explanation: A.Correct. An expansionary fiscal policy means that the government increases its purchases of goods and services and/or cuts tax rates to increase aggregate demand. Furthermore, an increase in the budget deficit would be associated with an expansionary fiscal policy. B.Incorrect. A rise in the budget deficit would be associated with an expansionary fiscal policy. C.Incorrect. An expansionary fiscal policy means that government increases its purchases of goods and services and/or cuts tax rates to increase aggregate demand.

questions.stem: Tiered pricing is best described as:
questions.option_a: charging different prices at different times.
questions.option_b: charging different prices to different buyers.
questions.option_c: combining a low price on a piece of equipment with high-margin pricing on repeat-purchase consumables.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because dynamic pricing charges different prices at different times. B.Correct because tiered pricing charges different prices to different buyers, most commonly based on volume purchased. C.Incorrect because razors-and-blades pricing combines a low price on a piece of equipment and high-margin pricing on repeat-purchase consumables.

questions.stem: The Herfindahl–Hirschman index (HHI) is more responsive than the concentration ratio to:
questions.option_c: mergers among the existing companies in the market.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, HHI, is widely used by competition regulators; however, just like the concentration ratio, the HHI does not take the possibility of entry into account, nor does it consider the elasticity of demand. B.Incorrect because the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, HHI, is widely used by competition regulators; however, just like the concentration ratio, the HHI does not take the possibility of entry into account, nor does it consider the elasticity of demand. C.Correct because a disadvantage of the concentration ratio is that it tends to be unaffected by mergers among the top market incumbents. The HHI is able to measure the impact of a merger as illustrated in the following example: consider a market of eight producers, where the largest producer has 35 percent of the market, the second largest has 25 percent, the third has 20 percent, the fourth has 10 percent, and the remaining four have 2.5 percent each. If we computed the concentration ratio of the top three producers, it would be 35 + 25 + 20= 80 percent, while the concentration ratio of the top four producers would be 35 + 25 + 20 + 10 = 90 percent. If the two largest companies merged, the new concentration ratio for the top three producers would be 60 (the sum of the market shares of the merged companies) + 20 +10 = 90 percent, and the concentration ratio for the four top producers would be 92.5 percent. Therefore, this merger affects the concentration ratio very mildly, even though it creates a substantial entity that controls 60 percent of the market. By comparison, the HHI for the top three companies would be 0.352 + 0.252 + 0.202 = 0.225 before the merger, while after the merger, it would be 0.602 + 0.202 + 0.102 = 0.410, which is substantially higher.

questions.stem: In jackknife resampling:
questions.option_a: the results are similar for every resample.
questions.option_b: the required number of repetitions is the same as in bootstrap resampling.
questions.option_c: each subsequent resample has one less observation than the previous resample.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because jackknife is another resampling technique for statistical inference of population parameters. Unlike bootstrap, which repeatedly draws samples with replacement, jackknife samples are selected by taking the original observed data sample and leaving out one observation at a time from the set (and not replacing it). According to its computation procedure, we can conclude that jackknife produces similar results for every run. B.Incorrect because for a sample of size n, jackknife usually requires n repetitions, whereas with bootstrap, we are left to determine how many repetitions are appropriate, i.e., the number of repetitions required is not necessarily the same as for bootstrapping. C.Incorrect because jackknife samples are selected by taking the original observed data sample and leaving out one observation at a time from the set (and not replacing it), i.e., each resample size is one less than the original data sample, not the previous resample.

questions.stem: Under US GAAP, which of the following is least likely a disclosure concerning inventory?
questions.option_a: The amount of the reversal of any write-down of inventories
questions.option_b: The amount of inventories recognized as an expense during the period
questions.option_c: The carrying amounts of inventories carried at fair value less costs to sell
questions.explanation: A.Correct. US GAAP does not permit the reversal of prior year write-downs; therefore, there are no disclosures related to reversals. B.Incorrect. Under both US GAAP and IFRS, disclosure is required about the amount of inventories expensed during the period (cost of goods sold). C.Incorrect. Both US GAAP and IFRS require disclosures of any inventories carried at fair value less costs to sell (NRV).

questions.stem: A country seeking nationalism but willing to cooperate with other countries is best classified as:
questions.option_c: hegemonic.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because autarky describes countries seeking political self-sufficiency with little or no external trade or finance. Autarky describes a country seeking both anti-globalization and non-cooperation. B.Correct because bilateralism describes a country seeking both nationalism and cooperation. Bilateralism is the conduct of political, economic, financial, or cultural cooperation between two countries. C.Incorrect because hegemony describes a country seeking both globalization and non-cooperation. A hegemonic system can provide valuable benefits both to hegemonic countries themselves and to the international system. For the country itself, economic and political dominance may provide important influence on global affairs.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a portfolio: If the equity weighting is 70%, the fixed-income weighting is 30% and the portfolio is rebalanced annually, the portfolio's annual geometric mean return is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the first step is to calculate the portfolio’s annual returns as a weighted mean of the equity and fixed-income returns with 70% equity and 30% fixed-income weighting. Year 1: (0.7 ×0.072) + (0.3×0.021) = 0.0567 = 5.67% Year 2: (0.7 ×0.096) + (0.3 ×–0.046) = 0.0534 = 5.34% Year 3: (0.7 ×–0.142) + (0.3 ×0.047) = –0.0853 = –8.53% Next, the portfolio’s geometric mean annual return is calculated as: [(1 + 0.0567) ×(1 + 0.0534) ×(1 – 0.0853)]^(1/3) – 1 = [1.01818]^(1/3) – 1 = 0.00602 » 0.60%. B.Incorrect because it reflects the incorrect decision to calculate the arithmetic mean return of the portfolio in the second step. Annual portfolio returns: Year 1: (0.7 ×0.072) + (0.3×0.021) = 0.0567 = 5.67% Year 2: (0.7 ×0.096) + (0.3 ×–0.046) = 0.0534 = 5.34% Year 3: (0.7 ×–0.142) + (0.3 ×0.047) = –0.0853 = –8.53% Next, the portfolio’s arithmetic mean annual return is calculated as: (0.0567 + 0.0534 – 0.0853)/3 = 0.00827 » 0.83%. C.Incorrect because it reflects the error of not applying the cubed root when the three annual returns are linked geometrically in the second step. Annual portfolio returns: Year 1: (0.7 ×0.072) + (0.3×0.021) = 0.0567 = 5.67% Year 2: (0.7 ×0.096) + (0.3 ×–0.046) = 0.0534 = 5.34% Year 3: (0.7 ×–0.142) + (0.3 ×0.047) = –0.0853 = –8.53% Next, the portfolio’s cumulative return is calculated as: [(1 + 0.0567) × (1 + 0.0534) ×(1 – 0.0853)] – 1 = 1.01818 – 1 = 0.01818 » 1.82%.

questions.stem: Firms operating under a monopolistic competition market structure most likely:
questions.option_b: benefit from high barriers to entry.
questions.option_c: sell products that are close substitutes for those offered by other firms.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because under monopolistic competition, there are a large number of potential buyers and sellers. B.Incorrect because under monopolistic competition, entry into and exit from the market are possible with fairly low costs. Furthermore, barriers to entry in a monopolistic competition market structure are low. C.Correct because under monopolistic competition, the products offered by each seller are close substitutes for the products offered by other firms, and each firm tries to make its product look different.

questions.stem: Hedge funds are most likely characterized by:
questions.option_b: a high correlation of returns with investment-grade bonds.
questions.option_c: performance relative to a traditional portfolio that may be hard to gauge.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because hedge funds are also subject to much lighter regulatory, compliance, and transparency requirements. With more flexibility in portfolio construction, hedge funds enjoy leeway to invest in situations in which time may be needed to generate an expected return. B.Incorrect because hedge fund performance has a very low correlation with that of traditional asset classes, such as investment bonds and currencies/cash. (However, hedge funds have a fairly high correlation with equities.) C.Correct because hedge fund portfolios approach return generation differently from traditional portfolios. The most significant difference is that hedge funds seek to limit market exposure and returns from beta and primarily focus on generating idiosyncratic returns by identifying sources of unique return, or alpha. Due to this different approach to return generation, hedge fund performance relative to a traditional portfolio may be hard to gauge.

questions.stem: The price of a forward contract most likely:
questions.option_a: decreases as the price of the underlying goes up.
questions.option_b: is constant and set as part of the contract specifications.
questions.option_c: increases as market risk increases.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. The price of a forward contract is not affected by market conditions. It is set as part of the contract specifications. B.Correct. The price of a forward contract remains constant throughout the life of the contract. It is set as part of the contract specifications. C.Incorrect. The price of a forward contract is not affected by market conditions. It is set as part of the contract specifications.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely a distinction between futures and forward contracts? Futures contracts are:
questions.option_c: more attractive than forwards for long positions when futures prices are negatively correlated to interest rates.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because futures contracts differ from forward contracts in that they have standard terms, are traded on a futures exchange, and are more heavily regulated, whereas forward contracts are typically private, customized transactions. Therefore, it is more likely that forwards would be customizable than future contracts. B.Correct because futures contracts differ from forward contracts in that they have standard terms, are traded on a futures exchange, and are more heavily regulated, whereas forward contracts are typically private, customized transactions. C.Incorrect because a negative correlation between futures prices and interest rates leads to the opposite interpretation, with forwards being more desirable than futures to the long position. The more desirable contract will tend to have the higher price.

questions.stem: Which of the following yield curves is a sequence of breakeven reinvestment rates?
questions.option_c: Forward curve
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the spot curve is used to derive two other important yield curves: the par curve and the forward curve. A par curve involves bond yields for hypothetical benchmark securities priced at par. B.Incorrect because yields-to-maturity on a series of default-risk-free zero-coupon bonds, are known as spot rates. The spot curve is used to derive two other important yield curves: the par curve and the forward curve. A par curve involves bond yields for hypothetical benchmark securities priced at par, while the forward curve involves rates for interest periods starting in the future. C.Correct because spot rates can also be used to calculate implied forward rates (also known as forward yields), which are breakeven reinvestment rates. They link the return on an investment in a shorter-term zero-coupon bond to the return on an investment in a longer-term zero-coupon bond.

questions.stem: The sensitivity of a 30-year fixed-rate bond to a 50 basis points increase in the benchmark rate at the 25-30 years maturity segment is best measured by:
questions.option_c: modified duration.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because key rate duration provides further insight into a bond’s sensitivity to changes in the benchmark yield curve. A key rate duration (or partial duration) is a measure of a bond’s sensitivity to a change in the benchmark yield curve at a specific maturity segment. B.Incorrect because effective duration is a curve duration statistic in that it measures interest rate risk in terms of a parallel shift in the benchmark yield curve (ΔCurve). C.Incorrect because modified duration provides an estimate of the percentage price change for a bond given a change in its yield-to-maturity.

questions.stem: In using matrix pricing to estimate the required yield spread on a new corporate bond issue, the benchmark rate used is most likely to be the:
questions.option_a: coupon rate on a government bond with a similar time to maturity.
questions.option_b: yield to maturity on a government bond with a similar time to maturity.
questions.option_c: yield to maturity on a corporate bond with similar credit risk and time to maturity.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the benchmark rate is measured relative to the yield to maturity and not the coupon rate. B.Correct because matrix pricing also is used in underwriting new bonds to get an estimate of the required yield spread over the benchmark rate, or the difference in yield-to-maturity between the bond and that of a government benchmark bond with the same or a similar time-to-maturity. C.Incorrect because the benchmark rate is measured relative to the yield to maturity of a government bond, not a similar corporate bond.

questions.stem: Which type of preference shares can be exchanged into a predetermined number of common shares?
questions.option_c: Participating preference shares
questions.explanation: A.Correct because convertible preference shares entitle shareholders to convert their shares into a specified number of common shares. B.Incorrect because dividends on cumulative preference shares accrue so that if the company decides not to pay a dividend in one or more periods, the unpaid dividends accrue and must be paid in full before dividends on common shares can be paid. C.Incorrect because participating preference shares entitle the shareholders to receive the standard preferred dividend plus the opportunity to receive an additional dividend if the company’s profits exceed a pre-specified level.

questions.stem: Privately held convertible debt is most likely used by companies in which of the following life cycle stages?
questions.option_c: Maturity
questions.explanation: A.Correct because privately held convertible debt is relied on in the seed or start-up stages of the corporate life cycle. B.Incorrect because privately held convertible debt is relied on in the seed or start-up stages of the corporate life cycle, not in the growth stage. C.Incorrect because privately held convertible debt is relied on in the seed or start-up stages of the corporate life cycle, not in the maturity stage.

questions.stem: Which of the following industries would most likely be included in the 'mature and cyclical' quadrant of an industry growth style box?
questions.option_c: Freight transportation
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because, according to the exhibit, the semiconductor industry is in the "Cyclical" and "Growth," not mature, quadrant. B.Incorrect because, according to the exhibit, the pharmaceutical industry is in the "Mature" and "Defensive," not cyclical, quadrant. C.Correct because the pattern of historical growth of an industry can be used to characterize it based on the magnitude of its growth rate and sensitivity to the business cycle. One approach to characterizing an industry’s growth rate is a style box, in which the freight transportation industry appears in the "Mature" and "Cyclical" quadrant.

questions.stem: Pooled investment vehicles that frequently trade at a significant discount to net asset value are most likely:
questions.option_c: exchange-traded funds.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because closed-end funds generally trade at a discount to their net asset values. The discount reflects the expenses of running the fund and sometimes investor concerns about the quality of the management. B.Incorrect because open-ended funds issue new shares and redeem existing shares on demand, usually on a daily basis. The price at which a fund redeems and sells the fund's shares is based on the net asset value of the fund's portfolio. C.Incorrect because the prices at which ETFs trade rarely differ much from net asset values. The market price and net asset values of ETFs tend to converge.

questions.stem: In an equally weighted portfolio, the diversification ratio is best described as a measure of the:
questions.option_a: relative level of risk between any two individual assets.
questions.option_b: amount of risk an asset contributes to the portfolio's risk.
questions.option_c: risk reduction benefit of investing in the portfolio versus a security from the portfolio.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the diversification ratio compares volatility between a portfolio and a single asset, not between two single assets. A simple measure of the value of diversification is calculated as the ratio of the standard deviation of the equally weighted portfolio to the standard deviation of the randomly selected security. B.Incorrect because the diversification ratio compares the risk of an overall portfolio relative to a single security; it does not measure the amount of risk an asset contributes to the portfolio's risk. C.Correct because the level of risk reduction from the portfolio approach to investing, relative to the risk of investing in a single security, can be measured by the diversification ratio. A simple measure of the value of diversification is calculated as the ratio of the standard deviation of the equally weighted portfolio to the standard deviation of the randomly selected security. This ratio may be referred to as the diversification ratio. The diversification ratio of the portfolio's standard deviation to the individual asset's standard deviation measures the risk reduction benefits of a simple portfolio construction method, equal weighting.

questions.stem: Consider the following set of valuation multiples for three firms among seven in a particular industry sector: Based the P/E and P/CF ratios,which company appears overvalued?
questions.option_c: Company C
questions.explanation: A.Correct. Company A has the highest P/E multiple and the highest P/CF multiple. Given the law of one price, similar companies should trade at similar P/E and P/CF levels. Thus, Company A is the company that appears overvalued relative to its peers. B.Incorrect because Company B has the lowest P/E and P/CF multiples; therefore, it does not appear overvalued relative to its peers. C.Incorrect because Company C has lower P/E and P/CF multiples than Company A and has P/E and P/CF multiples that are below the industry P/E and P/CF averages. Therefore, Company C does not appear to be overvalued relative to its peers.

questions.stem: The variance of returns of a security and the market portfolio are 0.25 and 0.09, respectively. If the covariance of security returns and market returns is 0.06, the security’s beta is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. It is computed as (0.06/0.25) = 0.24. B.Incorrect. It is computed as the correlation between the returns on the security and the market portfolio as [0.06/(0.5 × 0.3)] = 0.4. C.Correct. The security's beta, β, is the covariance of security returns and market returns divided by the variance of returns of the market portfolio, as follows. β = Cov(R i ,R m )/σ 2 m = 0.06/0.09 = 0.67

questions.stem: Which of the following is an assumption of the CAPM?
questions.option_b: Investors plan for multiple holding periods.
questions.option_c: Large investors can influence security prices.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the CAPM assumes that markets are frictionless, including no transaction costs and no taxes. B.Incorrect because the CAPM assumes that investors plan for the same single holding period. The CAPM is a single-period model, and all investor decisions are made on the basis of that one period. C.Incorrect because an assumption of the CAPM is that investors are price takers. The CAPM assumes that there are many investors and that no investor is large enough to influence prices. Thus, investors are price takers, and we assume that security prices are unaffected by investor trades.

questions.stem: Short sellers most likely:
questions.option_a: pay a short rebate to security lenders.
questions.option_b: receive cash collateral from security lenders.
questions.option_c: make payments-in-lieu of dividends to security lenders.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because security lenders will pay a short rebate rate to short sellers. Short sellers deposit collateral to security lenders, who invest the collateral in short-term securities, and rebate the interest to the short sellers at rates called short rebate rates. B.Incorrect because short seller will deposit cash collateral to security lenders. To secure the security loans, lenders require that the short seller leave the proceeds of the short sale on deposit with them as cash collateral for the stock loan. C.Correct because the short sellers will pay the long sellers [security lenders] all dividends or interest that they otherwise would have received had they not lent their securities. These payments are called payments-in-lieu of dividends (or of interest).

questions.stem: With regard to their investment in pension plans, employees with defined contribution plans accept:
questions.option_c: both inflation and investment risks.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the key to a defined contribution plan is that the employee accepts the investment and inflation risk, not only inflation risk. B.Incorrect because the key to a defined contribution plan is that the employee accepts the investment and inflation risk, not only investment risk. C.Correct because the key to a [defined contribution plan is that the employee accepts the investment and inflation risk and is responsible for ensuring that there are enough assets in the plan to meet their needs upon retirement.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information to evaluate the effect of dividends and leverage on future growth: If return on assets is the same for each scenario, the sustainable growth rate is:
questions.option_c: the same under both Scenario 1 and Scenario 2.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because scenario 2's sustainable growth rate 1.5 × ROA is higher than Scenario 1's sustainable growth rate 1.2 × ROA. B.Correct because sustainable growth rate g = b × ROE, where b = retention rate = (1 – Dividend payout ratio), and ROE = ROA × Financial leverage. Thus g = (1 – Dividend payout ratio) × ROA × Financial leverage. Since ROA is unchanged between Scenario 1 and 2: g scenario 1 = (1 – 0.6) × ROA × 3.0 = 1.2 × ROA; and g scenario 2 = (1 – 0.4) × ROA × 2.5 = 1.5 × ROA. Accordingly, scenario 2's sustainable growth rate 1.5 × ROA is higher than Scenario 1's sustainable growth rate 1.2 × ROA. C.Incorrect because scenario 2's sustainable growth rate 1.5 × ROA is higher than Scenario 1's sustainable growth rate 1.2 × ROA.

questions.stem: An investor values a company based on the dividend discount model. All else being equal, the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a one-year holding period is most likely:
questions.option_a: lower than the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a five-year holding period.
questions.option_b: equal to the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a five-year holding period.
questions.option_c: higher than the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a five-year holding period.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a one-year holding period will be the same as for a five-year holding period. B.Correct because the general form of the dividend discount model (DDM) applies even in the case in which the investor has a finite investment horizon. For that investor, stock value today depends directly on the dividends the investor expects to receive before the stock is sold and depends indirectly on the expected dividends for periods subsequent to that sale, because those expected future dividends determine the expected selling price. Therefore, the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a one-year holding period will be the same as for a five-year holding period. C.Incorrect because the estimated intrinsic value of the stock for a one-year holding period will be the same as for a five-year holding period.

questions.stem: A credit issuer rating assigned by a rating agency is based on:
questions.option_a: the notching adjustment of a specific bond of the issuer.
questions.option_b: the ranking of a specific bond in the issuer's capital structure.
questions.option_c: the issuer's ability and willingness to service its senior unsecured debt.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because an issue rating is notched from the issuer rating, not the other way round. The rating agencies have adopted a notching process whereby their credit ratings on issues can be moved up or down from the issuer rating, B.Incorrect because an issue rating, not an issuer rating, should consider ranking in the capital structure. Issue ratings refer to specific financial obligations of an issuer and take into consideration such factors as ranking in the capital structure (e.g., secured or subordinated). C.Correct because an issuer credit rating is meant to address an obligor’s overall creditworthiness — its ability and willingness to make timely payments of interest and principal on its debt. The issuer credit rating usually applies to its senior unsecured debt.

questions.stem: A net investment hedge occurs when a derivative is used to:
questions.option_a: offset the fluctuation in the fair value of an asset or liability.
questions.option_b: absorb the variable cash flow of a floating rate asset or liability.
questions.option_c: offset the exchange rate risk of the equity of a foreign operation.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because this describes a fair value hedge, not a net investment hedge. A fair value hedge designation applies when a derivative is deemed to offset the fluctuation in fair value of an asset or liability. B.Incorrect because this describes a cash flow hedge, not a net investment hedge. Derivatives designated as absorbing the variable cash flow of a floating-rate asset or liability such as foreign exchange, interest rates, or commodities are referred to as cash flow hedges. C.Correct because net investment hedges occur when either a foreign currency bond or a derivative such as an FX swap or forward is used to offset the exchange rate risk of the equity of a foreign operation.

questions.stem: The value effect anomaly:
questions.option_b: was identified using time series of data only.
questions.option_c: states that growth stocks have consistently outperformed value stocks.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the value stock anomaly contradicts semi-strong market efficiency because all the information used to categorize stocks in this manner is publicly available. B.Incorrect because the anomalies are placed into categories because based on the research method that identified the anomaly. Time-series anomalies were identified using time series of data. Cross-sectional anomalies were identified based on analyzing a a cross section of companies that differ on some key characteristics. The value effect was found based on cross-sectional analysis. C.Incorrect because the value stock anomaly refers to the studies that have shown that value stocks have consistently outperformed growth stocks over long periods of time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to be an example of a derivative?
questions.option_b: A contract to sell Alphabet Inc.’s shares at a fixed price
questions.option_c: A contract to buy Australian dollars at a predetermined exchange rate
questions.explanation: A.Correct. Although an exchange-traded fund derives its value from the underlying assets it holds, it does not transform the performance of those assets and so is not a derivative. B.Incorrect. A contract to sell Alphabet Inc.’s shares transforms the performance of the underlying shares of Alphabet Inc and is an example of an option derivative. C.Incorrect. A contract to buy Australian dollars transforms the performance of the underlying currency and is an example of a currency derivative.

questions.stem: Accounting standards and reporting requirements that produce meaningful and timely financial disclosures are most critical for achieving which of the following efficiencies associated with a well-functioning financial system?
questions.option_c: Operational
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. Allocational efficiency refers to making resources available where they are most valuable. B.Correct. Accounting standards and reporting requirements that allow meaningful and timely financial disclosures reduce the costs of obtaining fundamental information and thereby allow analysts to form more accurate estimates of fundamental values. They support informationally efficient markets. C.Incorrect. Operational efficiency relates to the costs of arranging trades, which can be reduced via organized exchanges, brokerages, securitization, clearing houses, and so forth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely a primary reason a company would raise capital through the issuance of equity securities?
questions.option_c: Finance the purchase of long-lived assets
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. The primary goal of raising capital is to finance the company’s revenue generating activities in order to increase its net income and maximize the wealth of its shareholders. B.Correct. In general, a company will utilize share buybacks to satisfy stock compensation plans. C.Incorrect. In most cases, the capital that is raised through equity issuance is used to finance the purchase of long-lived assets, capital expansion projects, research and development, the entry into new product or geographic regions, and the acquisition of other companies.

questions.stem: Mass redemptions may force the sale of underlying real estate by managers of:
questions.option_c: both open-end funds and publicly traded REITs.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the REIT is not forced to sell the company’s underlying real estate like open-end funds experiencing mass redemptions. B.Incorrect because the REIT is not forced to sell the company’s underlying real estate like open-end funds experiencing mass redemptions. C.Incorrect because the REIT is not forced to sell the company’s underlying real estate like open-end funds experiencing mass redemptions.

questions.stem: The bonds of Apex Corporations have a par value of $10,000 each and an annual required rate of return of 10%. The bonds make quarterly coupon payments at an annual rate of 6% and have two years remaining until maturity. The current market price of each bond is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct. Using the quarterly coupon payment of $150 [= (0.06 × 10000)/4] over eight quarters and a quarterly required rate of return of 2.5%, we calculate the bond’s price as: P 0 = 150/(1.025) 1 + 150/(1.025) 2 + ... + 150/(1.025) 8 + 10,000/(1.025) 8 = $9,282.99 B.Incorrect because the bond’s price is computed using the annual coupon payment of $600 [= (0.06 × 10,000)] over 2 years and the annual required rate of return of 10%: P 0 = 600/(1.10) 1 + (600 + 10,000)/(1.10) 2 = $9,305.79 C.Incorrect because the bond’s price is computed using a quarterly coupon payment of $250 [= (0.10 × 10000)/4] and a quarterly required rate of return of 1.5%: P 0 = 250/(1.015) 1 + 250/(1.015) 2 + ... + 250/(1.015) 8 + 10000/(1.015) 8 = $10,748.59

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely an example of a Eurobond?
questions.option_a: A Japanese borrower issuing US dollar–denominated bonds in the US market.
questions.option_b: A Canadian borrower issuing British pound–denominated bonds in the UK market.
questions.option_c: An Australian borrower issuing Canadian dollar–denominated bonds in the UK market.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because this is an example of a foreign bond, which is a bond issued by an entity incorporated in a country other than where the bond is issued and in whose currency the bond is denominated. B.Incorrect because this is an example of a foreign bond, which is a bond issued by an entity incorporated in a country other than where the bond is issued and in whose currency the bond is denominated. C.Correct. A Eurobond is an international bond issued outside the jurisdiction of any one country and not denominated in the currency of the country where it is issued.

questions.stem: For a bond investment, loss severity is:
questions.option_b: B.used in the calculation of the expected loss.
questions.option_c: C.the primary focus when assessing the creditworthiness of high-quality issuers.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because loss severity is often expressed as (1 − Recovery rate), where the recovery rate is the percentage of the principal amount recovered in the event of default. B.Correct because Expected loss = Default probability × Loss severity given default. C.Incorrect because loss severity is most relevant for lower-quality debt issuers. Because default risk (default probability) is quite low for most high-quality debt issuers, bond investors tend to focus primarily on assessing this probability and devote less effort to assessing the potential loss severity arising from default.

questions.stem: For a call option, if the underlying asset’s value is less than the option’s exercise price, the option is said to be:
questions.option_c: in the money.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. For an at-the-money call option, the value of the underlying asset is equal to the option’s exercise price, and the option buyer would be indifferent between exercising or not exercising the option. B.Correct. If the underlying asset’s value is less than the option’s exercise price, the call option is not worth exercising and is said to be out of the money. C.Incorrect. For an in-the-money call option, the value of the underlying asset is greater than the option’s exercise price, and the option is worth exercising.

questions.stem: For European options, all else being equal, a higher exercise price results in a higher value for:
questions.option_c: both puts and calls.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the value of a European call option is inversely related to the exercise price whereas the value of a European put option is directly related to the exercise price. Therefore, all else being equal, the higher the exercise price, the higher is the value of European puts and the lower is the value of European calls. B.Incorrect because higher exercise price results in a higher value for puts only (not calls), as explained in the rationale for the correct answer. C.Incorrect because higher exercise price results in a higher value for puts only (not calls), as explained in the rationale for the correct answer.

questions.stem: Consider the following information for a fixed-rate bond: If the bond’s yield to maturity increases to 7.25%, the bond’s estimated market value will be closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because $9,746,818 results from incorrectly using a yield to maturity of 4.5% (the semiannual coupon rate rather than the 6.57% yield to maturity): ΔAnnYield ≠ 7.25% – 4.50% = 2.75% or 0.0275 %ΔPVFull ≈ –AnnModDur × ΔAnnYield ≈ –4.687985 × 0.0275 ≈ –0.1289 or –12.89% $11,189,092 × (1 – 0.1289) = $9,746,599. B.Incorrect because the result incorrectly applies the annual coupon rate in deriving the ΔAnnYield term ΔYield ≠ 9.00% – 7.25% = 1.75% or 0.0175, hence %ΔPVFull ≈ –AnnModDur × ΔAnnYield ≈ –4.687985 × 0.0175 ≈ –0.0820 or –8.20% $11,189,092 × (1 – 0.0820) = $10,271,142. C.Correct because modified duration provides an estimate of the percentage price change for a bond given a change in its yield to maturity: %ΔPVFull ≈ –AnnModDur × ΔAnnYield. Given the bond’s modified duration of 4.687985 and the change in yield of 0.68% (= 7.25% – 6.57%), %ΔPVFull ≈ –4.687985 × 0.0068 ≈ –0.0319 or –3.19%. Given an increase in the yield from 6.57% to 7.25%, the market value of the bond would decline by approximately 3.19%, resulting in an estimated market value of $10,832,160: $11,189,092 × (1 – 0.0319) = $10,832,403 (rounded).

questions.stem: Assume management fees are calculated using end-of-period valuation. The investor’s net return given this fee structure is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. It ignores the fact that the incentive fee is calculated net of management fees. Management fee: 1% of $112 million = $1.12 million. Incentive fee: 10% of $12 million = $1.2 million. Fund value after fees: $112 million – $1.12 million – $1.2 million = $109.68 million Investor return: ($109.68 million / $100 million) - 1 = 9.68% B.Correct. Management fee: 1% of $112 million = $1.12 million Incentive fee: 10% of ($12 million – $ 1.12 million) = $1.088 million Fund value after fees: $112 million – $1.12 million – $1.088 million = $109.792 million Investor return: ($109.792 million/$100 million) – 1 = 9.79% C.Incorrect. It neglects the incentive fee. Management fee: 1% of $112 million = $1.12 million Fund value after fees: $112 million – $1.12 million = $110.88 million Investor return: ($110.88 million/$100 million) – 1 = 10.88%

questions.stem: Under US GAAP, an investment valued using reliable outside broker quotes is most appropriately categorized as a:
questions.option_c: Level 3 asset.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because GAAP accounting rules in the United States created a methodology that involves the categorization of investments into three buckets: Level 1, 2, and 3 asset pricing. Level 1 assets involve situations where an exchange-traded, publicly traded price is available and is mandated to be used for valuation purposes. B.Correct because GAAP accounting rules in the United States created a methodology that involves the categorization of investments into three buckets: Level 1, 2, and 3 asset pricing. Level 1 assets involve situations where an exchange-traded, publicly traded price is available and is mandated to be used for valuation purposes. When such pricing is not available, outside broker quotes, or Level 2 values, may be relied on. C.Incorrect because GAAP accounting rules in the United States created a methodology that involves the categorization of investments into three buckets: Level 1, 2, and 3 asset pricing. Level 1 assets involve situations where an exchange-traded, publicly traded price is available and is mandated to be used for valuation purposes. When such pricing is not available, outside broker quotes, or Level 2 values, may be relied on. As a final recourse, when such broker quotes are deemed either unavailable or unreliable, assets may be computed using only internal models—a process referred to as Level 3 asset pricing.

questions.stem: One source of return for an investor in a fixed-rate corporate bond is most likely the:
questions.option_c: reinvestment of coupon payments.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the bid–offer spread or bid–ask spread, which reflects the prices at which dealers will buy from a customer (bid) and sell to a customer (offer or ask), is very often used as an indicator of liquidity, not a source of return for an investor. The bid-ask spread may provide return for an intermediary such as a bank or broker selling the bond to the investor. B.Incorrect because in contrast to corporate bonds, the source of payment for ABS does not depend on the claims-paying ability of an operating entity but on the cash flows generated by one or more underlying financial assets, such as mortgages or auto loans. Interest on the collateral of the bond may be a source of return from certain ABS, but not from a typical fixed-rate corporate bond. C.Correct because the fixed-rate bond investor has three sources of return: (1) receipt of the promised coupon and principal payments on the scheduled dates, (2) reinvestment of coupon payments, and (3) potential capital gains or losses on the sale of the bond prior to maturity.

questions.stem: Which of the following performance measures is only relevant for well-diversified portfolios?
questions.option_c: M-squared (M2)
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because total risk is relevant for an investor when he or she holds a portfolio that is not fully diversified, which is not a desirable portfolio. In such cases, the Sharpe ratio and M2 are appropriate performance measures. Performance measures relative to beta risk—Treynor ratio and Jensen’s alpha—are relevant when the investor holds a well-diversified portfolio with negligible diversifiable risk. Thus, the Sharpe ratio, which considers total risk, is not an appropriate performance measure for an investor that holds a well-diversified portfolio. B.Correct because total risk is relevant for an investor when he or she holds a portfolio that is not fully diversified, which is not a desirable portfolio. In such cases, the Sharpe ratio and M2 are appropriate performance measures. Performance measures relative to beta risk—Treynor ratio and Jensen’s alpha—are relevant when the investor holds a well-diversified portfolio with negligible diversifiable risk. Thus, Jensen's alpha, which considers only beta risk, is an appropriate performance measure for an investor that holds a well-diversified portfolio. C.Incorrect because total risk is relevant for an investor when he or she holds a portfolio that is not fully diversified, which is not a desirable portfolio. In such cases, the Sharpe ratio and M2 are appropriate performance measures. Performance measures relative to beta risk—Treynor ratio and Jensen’s alpha—are relevant when the investor holds a well-diversified portfolio with negligible diversifiable risk. Thus, M-squared, which considers total risk, is not an appropriate performance measure for an investor that holds a well-diversified portfolio.

questions.stem: Which of the following behavioral biases most likely helps explain the momentum market anomaly?
questions.option_c: Anchoring and adjustment bias
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because status quo bias is an emotional bias in which people choose to do nothing (i.e., maintain the 'status quo') instead of making a change, even when change is warranted. While this could be incorrectly interpreted as maintaining a trend in a price, it does not explain the momentum anomaly. Momentum can be partly explained by availability, hindsight, and loss aversion biases. B.Correct because momentum can be partly explained by availability, hindsight, and loss aversion biases. Studies have identified faulty learning models within traders, in which reasoning is based on their recent experience. Behaviorally, this is availability bias. C.Incorrect because anchoring and adjustment bias refers to relying on an initial piece of information to make subsequent estimates, judgments, and decisions. While the current market price may act as an anchor, it does not explain the observed momentum anomaly. Momentum can be partly explained by availability, hindsight, and loss aversion biases.

questions.stem: A good risk management framework:
questions.option_a: is a top-down process and guidance directing risk management activities.
questions.option_b: seeks to prioritize avoidance of financial loss over defining policies and processes.
questions.option_c: is typically a process that addresses a common set of factors within different organizations.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect. Risk governance is the top-down process and guidance that directs risk management activities to align with and support the overall enterprise. B.Incorrect. A good risk management framework prioritizes the definition of policies and procedures over avoidance of financial loss. C.Correct. Good risk management may not prevent losses but provides a framework that addresses common factors, such as risk governance, risk infrastructure, policies and procedures, risk monitoring, and integration, among others. A risk management framework flows logically from the definition of risk management that was previously given: It is the infrastructure, process, and analytics needed to support effective risk management in an organization. This process should fully integrate the “risk” and “return” aspects of the enterprise into decisions in support of best achieving its goals within its tolerance for risk. Risk management is not a “one-size-fits-all” solution; it is integral to the enterprise’s goals and needs. Despite customization, every risk management framework should address the common factors listed above.

questions.stem: For a coupon bond with a positive yield, compounding more frequently within the year results in a yield-to-maturity that is:
questions.option_c: more positive.
questions.explanation: A.Correct because for a given pair of cash flows, the stated annual rate and the periodicity are inversely related. Thus, increasing the frequency of compounding reduces the annual rate. B.Incorrect because for a given pair of cash flows, the stated annual rate and the periodicity are inversely related. Thus, increasing the frequency of compounding reduces the annual rate. The annual rate does not stay the same. C.Incorrect because for a given pair of cash flows, the stated annual rate and the periodicity are inversely related. Thus, increasing the frequency of compounding reduces, not increases, the annual rate.

questions.stem: Which of the following ESG investment approaches best describes positive screening?
questions.option_a: Systematic consideration of material ESG factors in asset allocation
questions.option_b: Inclusion of sectors or companies in the portfolio based on specific ESG criteria
questions.option_c: Investments made with the intention to generate positive, measurable social and environmental impact
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because this describes ESG integration, not positive screening. ESG integration is defined as the systematic consideration of material ESG factors in asset allocation, security selection, and portfolio construction decisions. B.Correct because positive screening is defined as including sectors or companies based on specific ESG criteria, typically ESG performance relative to industry peers. C.Incorrect because it describes impact investing, not ESG integration. Impact investing is defined as investments made with the intention to generate positive, measurable social and environmental impact alongside a financial return.

questions.stem: A market index has the following information: By the end of Quarter 3, which of the following statements is most accurate?
questions.option_b: The value of the price return index is 998.1.
questions.option_c: The value of the total return index is below 1,000.
questions.explanation: Solution A.Incorrect because by the end of Q3, the total return is 1.26% whereas the price return is (0.2%). Value of price return index, V PRIT = V PRI0 (1 + PR I1 )(1 + PR I2 ) … (1 + PR IT ) Value of total return index, V TRIT = V TRI0 (1 + TR I1 )(1 + TR I2 ) … (1 + TR IT ) B.Correct. The value of the price return index is 998.1. The value calculations for the price return index and the total return index are based on the geometrical link of the respective series of index returns as follows: Value of price return index, V PRIT = V PRI0 (1 + PR I1 )(1 + PR I2 ) … (1 + PR IT ) Value of total return index, V TRIT = V TRI0 (1 + TR I1 )(1 + TR I2 ) … (1 + TR IT ) C.Incorrect because the value of the total return index at the end of Q3 is 1,012.61 which is above 1,000. Value of price return index, V PRIT = V PRI0 (1 + PR I1 )(1 + PR I2 ) … (1 + PR IT ) Value of total return index, V TRIT = V TRI0 (1 + TR I1 )(1 + TR I2 ) … (1 + TR IT )

questions.stem: An asset-backed securitization with a waterfall structure is most likely structured with which type of credit enhancement?
questions.option_c: Special-purpose entity (SPE)
questions.explanation: A.Correct. Asset-backed securitizations can be structured with subordinated bond classes. They function as credit protection for the more senior bond classes; that is, losses are realized by the subordinated bond classes before any losses are realized by the senior bond classes. This type of protection is also commonly referred to as a waterfall structure because of the cascading flow of payments between bond classes in the event of default. B.Incorrect. The creation of bond classes that possess different expected maturities is referred to as time tranching. C.Incorrect. An SPE is a bankruptcy remote legal entity that holds the collateral and is considered not an enhancement but, rather, a prerequisite for establishing securitizations.

questions.stem: If a bank wants the ability to retire debt prior to maturity in order to take advantage of lower borrowing rates, it most likely issues a:
questions.option_c: convertible bond.
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because putable bonds give bondholders the ability to sell the bond at predetermined price to issuers. B.Correct. Callable bonds give issuers the ability to retire debt prior to maturity. The most compelling reason for them to do so is to take advantage of lower borrowing rates. C.Incorrect because convertible bonds give bondholders the ability to convert the bond to a predetermined number of shares of the company.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a clawback provision? A provision that:
questions.option_a: protects clients from paying twice for the same performance.
