questions.stem: An analyst purchases the following derivatives with the same maturity date and underlying: If the profit on the call option is zero at maturity,the price of the forward at maturity is:
questions.option_a: less than the price of the underlying

B.Incorrect because this does not consider the option premium.For the buyer of a call option with an exercise price of F0(T)[we have the following expression for the profit of the call option]:Π=max[0,S T –F 0 (T)]–c0.If the profit on the call option is zero,then S T –F 0 (T)=$3 and F 0 (T)<>S T . C.Incorrect because for the buyer of a call option with an exercise price of F 0 (T)[we have the following expression for the profit of the call option]:Π=max[0,S T –F 0 (T)]–c0.If the profit on the call option is zero,then S T –F 0 (T)=$3 and F 0 (T)=S T –$3[not S T +$3].The forward price is therefore less than,not greater than,the price of the underlying by the amount of the option premium.

questions.stem: In contrast to risk tolerance,risk budgeting focuses more on:
questions.option_c: what is and is not acceptable risk
questions.explanation: A.Correct because whereas risk tolerance focuses on the appetite for risk and what is and is not acceptable,risk budgeting has a more specific focus on how that risk is taken. B.Incorrect because whereas risk tolerance focuses on the appetite for risk and what is and is not acceptable,risk budgeting has a more specific focus on how that risk is taken. questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a hedge fund: If the incentive fee is calculated independently of the management fee,total fees for the year are:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the incentive fee is calculated only on the return in excess of the soft hurdle rate rather than on the entire return.When a soft hurdle rate is used,the incentive fee is calculated on the entire return. In this case,the calculation of the incentive fee is based on the return in excess of the hurdle rate of$6,000,000($80,000,000×(0.125 gross return–0.05 soft hurdle rate)).The incentive fee calculated in this manner is$1,200,000($6,000,0000 return in excess of the hurdle rate x 0.2 incentive fee).The management fee is calculated correctly as$1,800,000((80,000,000 beginning-of-year assets×1.125)x(0.02 management fee)).Therefore,the total fees calculated in this manner are$3,000,000(management fee of$1,800,000+incentive fee of$1,200,000). B.Incorrect because the incentive fee has been calculated net of the management fee rather than independent of the management fee.The management fee is correctly calculated as$1,800,000($80,000,000×1.125×0.02).The incentive fee is incorrectly calculated net of the management fee and totals$1,640,000([($80,000,000×0.125 gross return)–(management fee of$1,800,000)]×(incentive fee of 0.2)).Thus,the total fee becomes$3,440,000(management fee of$1800,000+incentive fee of$1,640,000). C.Correct because the incentive fee is calculated independently of the management fee and,since a soft hurdle rate is used,the incentive fee is calculated on the entire return.The partnership agreement usually specifies that the performance fee is earned only after the fund achieves a return known as a hurdle rate.The hurdle rate is a minimum rate of return that the GP must exceed in order to earn the performance fee.GPs typically receive 20%of the total profit of the private equity fund net of any hard hurdle rate,in which case the GP earns fees on annual returns in excess of the hurdle rate,or net of the soft hurdle rate,in which case the fee is calculated on the entire annual gross return as long as the set hurdle is exceeded. The management fee is calculated on end-of-year AUM of$90,000,000($80,000,000 beginning-of-year AUM×1.125)and is$1,800,000($90,000,000 end-of-year AUM×0.02 management fee).The incentive fee is calculated independently of the management fee and on the entire return(soft hurdle rate)and is$2,000,000(($80,000,000×0.125)x(0.2 incentive fee)).Total fees are therefore$3,800,000(management fee of$1,800,000+incentive fee of$2,000,000).

questions.stem: An investor gathers the following information: The expected return of a portfolio on the capital market line with a standard deviation of returns of 15%is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it forgets to add the risk-free rate in the correct calculation;E(R p )=[(E(R m )–R f )/σ m ]×σ p =[(12%–4%)/20%]×15%=0.4×15%=6%.This is also the closest answer if a candidate attempts to use the CAPM with the standard deviation of the asset in place of its beta;E(R p )=R f +σ p ×[E(R m )–R f ]=4%+0.15×[12%–4%]=4%+0.15×8%=5.2%. B.Incorrect because it is the expected return of a portfolio on the capital market line with equal weights(rather than 25%/75%weights)in the risk-free asset and the market portfolio;E(R p )=(0.5×12%)+(0.5×4%)=8%.8%is also equal to the market risk premium,E(R m )–R f =12%–4%=8%,and it is the difference between the market's standard deviation and expected return,σ m –E(R m )=20%–12%=8%. C.Correct because,according to capital market theory,all portfolios(p)on the capital market line(CML)have an expected return equal to E(R p )=R f +[(E(Rm)–R f )/σ m ]×σp.Hence,for a portfolio withσp=15%,we have E(R p )=4%+[(12%–4%)/20%]×15%=4%+(0.4×15%)=4%+6%=10%.Alternatively,it can be deduced from the standard deviation of the CML portfolio that it consists of 75%invested in the market portfolio and 25%invested in the risk-free asset.Specifically,σp=(1–w 1 )σm,where w1 denotes the portfolio weight in the risk-free asset and(1–w 1 )the portfolio weight in the market,and therefore(1–w 1 )=σp/σm=15%/20%=0.75.The expected return on the portfolio is therefore:E(R p )=(0.75×12%)+(0.25×4%)=10%.

questions.stem: In which section of an IPS is the rebalancing policy most likely found?
questions.option_c: Evaluation and Review
questions.explanation: A.Correct because Appendices details(A)Strategic Asset Allocation(B)Rebalancing Policy.Many investors specify a strategic asset allocation(SAA),also known as the policy portfolio,which is the baseline allocation of portfolio assets to asset classes in view of the investor’s investment objectives. B.Incorrect because Investment Guidelines provides information about how policy should be executed(e.g.,on the permissible use of leverage and derivatives)and on specific types of assets excluded from investment,if any.It is Appendices that details(A)Strategic Asset Allocation(B)Rebalancing Policy. C.Incorrect because Evaluation and Review provides guidance on obtaining feedback on investment results.It is Appendices that details(A)Strategic Asset Allocation(B)Rebalancing Policy.

questions.stem: The value of a swap contract at initiation is most likely equal to:
questions.option_c: the present value of the fixed payments on the swap
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the value(not the price)of the swap is typically zero at initiation and the fixed swap price is typically determined such that the value of the swap will be zero at initiation. B.Incorrect because the value(not the price)of the swap is typically zero at initiation and the fixed swap price is typically determined such that the value of the swap will be zero at initiation.Therefore,the price of the swap should be set at a level so that the value of a swap is zero instead of equal to the value of the swap at initiation. C.Incorrect because the principal of replication articulates that the valuation of a swap is the present value of all the net cash flow payments from the swap,not simply the present value of the fixed payments of the swap or the present value of the underlying at the end of the contract.

questions.stem: All else being equal,which of the following conditions most likely results in wider credit spreads?
questions.option_c: A period of heavy new issue supply
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because spreads are tightest at or near the top of the credit cycle. B.Incorrect because a strengthening economy will cause credit spreads to narrow. C.Correct because in periods of heavy new issue supply,credit spreads will widen if there is insufficient demand.In periods of high demand for bonds,spreads will move tighter.

questions.stem: Regarding the partnership structures of private equity funds,which of the following statements is most accurate?
questions.option_a: General partners theoretically bear unlimited liability
questions.option_b: Limited partners are involved with the management of a fund
questions.option_c: Investors are general partners who own fractional interests in a partnership
questions.explanation: A.Correct because in limited partnerships,the fund manager is the general partner(GP)and investors are the limited partners(LP).The GP runs the business and theoretically bears unlimited liability for anything that goes wrong. B.Incorrect because LPs[limited partners]play passive roles and are not involved with the management of the fund. C.Incorrect because many alternative investments,such as hedge and private equity funds,use a partnership structure with a general partner that manages the business and limited partners(investors)who own fractional interests in the partnership.Therefore,investors are limited partners,not general partners.

questions.stem: If yields decrease by 0.75%,the convexity adjustment for a bond with an annual convexity of 400 is:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the“second order”effect,is the convexity adjustment.The convexity adjustment is the annual convexity statistic,AnnConvexity,times one-half,multiplied by the change in the yield-to-maturity squared. Convexity adjustment=(0.5×AnnConvexity×ΔYield 2 ) =(0.5×400×0.0075 2 )=0.01125. B.Incorrect because the 0.5 is missing in the formula: Convexity adjustment≠(400×0.0075 2 )=0.02250 C.Incorrect because the change in yield is not squared: Convexity adjustment≠(0.5×400×0.0075)=1.50000.

questions.stem: Which of the following cognitive errors is best classified as a processing error?
questions.option_c: Anchoring and adjustment bias
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it is a belief perseverance bias,and not a processing error.The belief perseverance biases discussed are conservatism,confirmation,representativeness,illusion of control,and hindsight. B.Incorrect because it is a belief perseverance bias,and not a processing error.The belief perseverance biases discussed are conservatism,confirmation,representativeness,illusion of control,and hindsight. C.Correct because the processing errors discussed are anchoring and adjustment,mental accounting,framing,and availability.Anchoring and adjustment bias refers to relying on an initial piece of information to make subsequent estimates,judgments,and decisions.

questions.stem: Based on put–call–forward parity,a trader can replicate a short forward position with a:
questions.option_a: short put,a long call,and a long bond
questions.option_b: short put,a short call,and a short bond
questions.option_c: long put,a short call,and a short bond
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the cost of the fiduciary call must equal the cost of the synthetic pro­tective put,giving us what is referred to as put–call–forward parity,F 0 (T)/(1+r) T +p 0 =c 0 +X/(1+r) T .This implies:–F 0 (T)/(1+r) T =p 0 –c 0 –X/(1+r) T .So,a short forward position can be replicated with a long(not short)a put,short(not long)a call,and short(not long)a bond. B.Incorrect because the cost of the fiduciary call must equal the cost of the synthetic pro­tective put,giving us what is referred to as put–call–forward parity,F0(T)/(1+r) T +p0=c0+X/(1+r) T .This implies:–F 0 (T)/(1+r) T =p 0 –c 0 –X/(1+r) T .So,a short forward position can be replicated with a long(not short)a put,short a call,and short a bond. C.Correct because the cost of the fiduciary call must equal the cost of the synthetic pro­tective put,giving us what is referred to as put–call–forward parity,F 0 (T)/(1+r) T +p 0 =c 0 +X/(1+r) T .This implies:–F 0 (T)/(1+r) T =p 0 –c 0 –X/(1+r) T .So,a short forward position can be replicated with a long a put,short a call,and short a bond.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a bond: The price value of a basis point is:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because only the increase in yield side is used to calculate PVBP. PVBP≠(PV–PV + ) ≠(96–95.92)=0.08. B.Correct because the price value of a basis point(or PVBP)is an estimate of the change in the full bond price given a 1 bp change in the yield-to-maturity. PVBP=(PV – –PV + )/2 =(96.1–95.92)/2=0.09. C.Incorrect because the'divide by 2'is missing in the formula. ≠(96.1–95.92)=0.18.

questions.stem: An investor sells a European put option with the following characteristics: If the price of the underlying at expiration is€1,230,the profit for the seller is:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it represents the put price p0 less the difference between the exercise price X and the price of the underlying S T at expiration:40–(1,230–1,200)=10.This would be the profit to the seller of a call option,Π=–Max(0,S T –X)+c0,with the same exercise price and the same selling price.By contrast,to the put seller,the profit isΠ=–Max(0,X–S T )+p 0 .Therefore,Π=–Max(0,1200–1230)+40=40. B.Incorrect because it represents the payoff to the call buyer c T =Max(0,S T –X),where S T is the price of the underlying at expiration and X is the exercise price.Therefore,c T =Max(0,1,230-1,200)=30.By contrast,to the put seller,the profit isΠ=–Max(0,X–S T )+p 0 ,where p 0 is the put price.Therefore,Π=–Max(0,1200–1230)+40=40. C.Correct because to the put seller,the profit isΠ=–Max(0,X–S T )+p 0 ,where X is the exercise price,S T is the price of the underlying at expiration,and p0 is the put price.Therefore,Π=–Max(0,1200–1230)+40=40.

questions.stem: Companies that are candidates for a leveraged buyout most likely:
questions.option_b: generate a high level of cash flow
questions.option_c: are experiencing a rapid deterioration in operations
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a company requiring start-up capital would likely seek venture capital.Venture capital investments provide'seed'or start-up capital whereas,a leveraged buyout(LBO)occurs when a group of investors uses a large amount of debt to purchase all of the outstanding common shares of a publicly traded company. B.Correct because a leveraged buyout(LBO)occurs when a group of investors(such as the company’s management or a private equity partnership)uses a large amount of debt to purchase all of the outstanding common shares of a publicly traded company.Companies that are candidates for these types of transactions generally have large amounts of undervalued assets(which can be sold to reduce debt)and generate high levels of cash flows(which are used to make interest and principal payments on the debt). C.Incorrect because a company experiencing rapid deterioration in operations is unlikely to be able to service the debt involved with a leveraged buyout.A company in such a situation may issue a private investment in public equity,or PIPE.This type of investment is generally sought by a public company that is in need of additional capital quickly.For example,a company may require a large investment of new equity funds in a short period of time because it has significant expansion opportunities,is facing high levels of indebtedness,or is experiencing a rapid deterioration in its operations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a well-functioning financial system?
questions.option_c: Prices vary primarily in response to demands for liquidity made by traders
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because well-functioning financial systems are characterized by liquid markets in which the costs of trading—commissions,bid–ask spreads,and order price impacts—are low(operationally efficient markets). B.Correct because well-functioning financial systems are characterized by prices that reflect fundamental values so that prices vary primarily in response to changes in fundamental values and not to demands for liquidity made by uninformed traders(informationally efficient markets). C.Incorrect because well-functioning financial systems are characterized by prices that reflect fundamental values so that prices vary primarily in response to changes in fundamental values and not to demands for liquidity made by uninformed traders(informationally efficient markets).Therefore the prices vary primarily due to fundamentals and not liquidity demands.

questions.stem: Institutional investors typically begin investing in alternative investments via:
questions.option_c: direct investing
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because institutional investors typically begin investing in alternative investments via funds.Then,as they gain experience,they can begin to invest via co-investing and direct investing. B.Correct because institutional investors typically begin investing in alternative investments via funds.Then,as they gain experience,they can begin to invest via co-investing and direct investing.The largest and most sophisticated direct investors(such as some sovereign wealth funds)compete with fund managers for access to the best investment opportunities. C.Incorrect because institutional investors typically begin investing in alternative investments via funds.Then,as they gain experience,they can begin to invest via co-investing and direct investing.

questions.stem: For which of the following industries are economic influences most important?
questions.option_c: Pharmaceuticals
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because economic influences are most important for cyclical sectors such as crude oil,natural gas,freight transportation,semiconductor,fintech,and digital advertising.Utilities is a defensive industry. B.Correct because economic influences are most important for cyclical sectors such as crude oil,natural gas,freight transportation,semiconductor,fintech,and digital advertising. C.Incorrect because economic influences are most important for cyclical sectors such as crude oil,natural gas,freight transportation,semiconductor,fintech,and digital advertising.Pharmaceuticals is a defensive industry.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes changes in the value of a long forward position during its life?
questions.option_a: As interest rates go down,the value of the position goes up
questions.option_b: As the time to maturity goes down,the value of the position goes up
questions.option_c: As the price of the underlying goes up,the value of the position goes up
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because as interest rates go down,the value of the contract goes down. B.Incorrect because as the time to maturity goes down,the value of the contract goes down. C.Correct because given the formula for the value of a forward contract: V t (T)=S t –F 0 (T)(1+r) –(T–t) it follows that the value of the contract goes up as the price of the underlying goes up.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely forecast by using efficiency ratios?
questions.option_c: Selling and distribution expenses
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because cost of sales is typically forecast as a percentage of sales or as a gross margin.Cost of sales(cost of goods sold,or COGS)is typically the single largest cost for companies that make and/or sell products.Because it has a direct link with sales,forecasting this item as a percentage of sales(or as a gross margin)is usually a good approach. B.Correct because working capital forecasts are typically made by using efficiency ratios,discussed in earlier modules,as the forecast object,which are combined with sales and costs forecasts to project accounts receivable,inventories,accounts payable,and other current assets and liabilities. C.Incorrect because selling and distribution expenses are more likely modeled as a percentage of sales.Although SG&A expenses overall are generally less closely linked to revenue than is cost of sales,certain SG&A expenses could be more variable than others.Specifically,selling and distribution expenses often have a large variable component and can be modeled as a percentage of sales,while general corporate costs are more fixed and might be better modeled using a fixed growth rate based on expected wage inflation.

questions.stem: A hedge fund with$98 million of initial capital charges a management fee of 2%and an incentive fee of 20%.The management fee is based on assets under management at year end and the incentive fee is calculated independently from the management fee.The fee structure has a high-water mark provision.The fund value is$112 million at the end of Year 1,$100 million at the end of Year,and$116 million at the end of Year 3.The net-of-fees return earned by the fund in Year 3 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because 11.87%results from calculating the return based on a Year 2 ending capital position(i.e.,Year 3 beginning capital position)of$100 million.Instead,the return should be calculated based on the Year 2 ending capital position of$98 million,which is net of fees($100 million–$2 million). Management fee=Year-end value×Management fee%=$116 million×2%=$2.32 million Incentive fee=(Year-end value–High water mark)×Incentive fee% =($116 million–$106.96 million)×20%=$1.81 million. Total fees=Management fee+Incentive fee=$2.32 million+$1.81 million=$4.13 million Net-of-fees return=(Year-end value–Total fees–Beginning capital position)/Beginning capital position =($116 million–$4.13 million–$100 million)/$100 million=11.87%. B.Incorrect because 12.33%results from calculating the incentive fee using the net capital position at the end of Year 2 instead of the high-water mark value established at the end of Year 1. Management fee=Year-end value×Management fee%=$116 million×2%=$2.32 million Incentive fee=(Year-end value–Year 2 Ending capital position)×Incentive fee% =($116 million–$98 million)×20%=$3.60 million. Total fees=Management fee+Incentive fee=$2.32 million+$3.60 million=$5.92 million Net-of-fees return=(Year-end value–Total fees–Beginning capital position)/Beginning capital position =($116 million–$5.92 million–$98 million)/$98 million=12.33%. C.Correct because the net-of-fees return to the fund in Year 3 is closest to 14.15%,calculated as follows: Year 1: Portfolio gain=Year-end value–Beginning value=$112 million−$98 million=$14 million Management fee=Year-end value×Management fee%=$112 million×2%=$2.24 million Incentive fee=Portfolio gain×Incentive fee%=$14 million×20%=$2.8 million Total fees=Management fee+Incentive fee=$2.24 million+$2.8 million=$5.04 million Ending Capital Position=Year-end value–Total fees =$112 million−$5.04 million=$106.96 million High water mark=Ending capital position=$106.96 million Year 2: No incentive fee is earned as the fund declines in value;the high water mark established in Year 1 is not exceeded. Management fee=Year-end value×Management fee%=$100 million×2%=$2 million Ending Capital Position=Year-end value–Management fee =$100 million−$2 million=$98 million High water mark=Highest ending capital position=$106.96 million Year 3: Net-of-fee returns are affected by the Year 1 high water mark and the Year 2 net capital position(i.e.Year 3 beginning capital position). Management fee=Year-end value×Management fee%=$116 million×2%=$2.32 million Incentive fee=(Year-end value–High water mark)×Incentive fee% =($116 million–$106.96 million)×20%=$1.81 million. Total fees=Management fee+Incentive fee=$2.32 million+$1.81 million=$4.13 million Net-of-fees return=(Year-end value–Total fees–Beginning capital position)/Beginning capital position =($116 million–$4.13 million–$98 million)/$98 million=14.15%.

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions most likely represents a fair value hedge?
questions.option_b: Currency forward to hedge forecasted sales
questions.option_c: Interest rate swap to a fixed rate for floating-rate debt
questions.explanation: A.Correct because it is an example of a fair value hedge.A fair value hedge designation applies when a derivative is deemed to offset the fluctuation in fair value of an asset or liability.For example,a commodities producer might sell its inventory forward in anticipation of lower future prices. B.Incorrect because it is an example of a cash flow hedge.Derivatives designated as absorbing the variable cash flow of a floating-rate asset or liability such as foreign exchange,interest rates,or commodities are referred to as cash flow hedges.For instance,the FX forward to hedge forecasted sales constitutes an example of a cash flow hedge. C.Incorrect because it is an example of a cash flow hedge.Derivatives designated as absorbing the variable cash flow of a floating-rate asset or liability such as foreign exchange,interest rates,or commodities are referred to as cash flow hedges.A swap to a fixed rate for a floating-rate debt liability is another example of a cash flow hedge.

questions.stem: An infrastructure investment financing the construction of a new seaport is most likely classified as a:
questions.option_c: social infrastructure investment
questions.explanation: A.Correct because greenfield investments involve developing new assets and new infrastructure. B.Incorrect because a new infrastructure asset is classified as a greenfield investment,not a brownfield investment.Brownfield investments expand existing facilities and may involve privatization of public assets or a sale leaseback of completed greenfield projects. C.Incorrect because a seaport is classified as economic infrastructure,not social infrastructure.Economic infrastructure investments support economic activity through transportation assets,information and communication technology(ICT)assets,and utility and energy assets:Transportation assets include roads,bridges,tunnels,airports,and seaports.

questions.stem: The redemption value of a US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities(TIPS)issue at maturity is most likely:
questions.option_a: equal to the initial par value
questions.option_b: the greater of the inflation-adjusted principal or initial par value
questions.option_c: above or below the initial par value depending on actual inflation during the term
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because investors receive the greater of inflation-adjusted or par at maturity.TIPS,which have a periodic principal adjustment based on a price index,are an example of a capital-indexed bond.Note that while deflation causes the principal to decline over time,investors usually receive the greater of the inflation-adjusted principal or par at maturity. B.Correct because TIPS,which have a periodic principal adjustment based on a price index,are an example of a capital-indexed bond.Note that while deflation causes the principal to decline over time,investors usually receive the greater of the inflation-adjusted principal or par at maturity. C.Incorrect because investors can never receive below par.TIPS,which have a periodic principal adjustment based on a price index,are an example of a capital-indexed bond.Note that while deflation causes the principal to decline over time,investors usually receive the greater of the inflation-adjusted principal or par at maturity.

questions.stem: Which of the following market anomalies is best described as a cross-sectional anomaly？
questions.option_c: Initial public offerings
questions.explanation: A.Correct because two of the most researched cross-sectional anomalies in financial markets are the size effect and the value effect.The size effect results from the observation that equities of small-cap companies tend to outperform equities of large-cap companies on a risk-adjusted basis. B.Incorrect because the momentum anomaly is best described as a time-series anomaly.Momentum is a short-term price pattern where past price moves continued through time to move in the same direction. C.Incorrect because the Initial Public Offering(IPO)anomaly is best described as an“other”anomaly.

questions.stem: Effective duration is the appropriate interest rate risk measure for callable bonds because it:
questions.option_a: measures the sensitivity of the bond price to a change in the yield to worst
questions.option_b: accounts for the convexity adjustment which can be significant for callable bonds
questions.option_c: can be calculated for bonds that do not have a well-defined internal rate of return
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the duration of a callable bond is not the sensitivity of the bond price to a change in the yield-to-worst(i.e.,the lowest of the yield-to-maturity,yield-to-first-call,yield-to-second-call,and so forth)a callable bond does not have a well-defined internal rate of return(yield-to-maturity).Therefore,yield duration statistics,such as modified and Macaulay durations,do not apply;effective duration is the appropriate duration measure. B.Incorrect because only the primary,or first-order,effect of a shift in the benchmark yield curve is measured by effective duration,the secondary,or second-order,effect is measured by effective convexity.The convexity adjustment is measured by effective convexity and not accounted for in effective duration. C.Correct because a callable bond does not have a well-defined internal rate of return(yield to maturity).Therefore,yield duration statistics,such as modified and Macaulay durations,do not apply;effective duration is the appropriate duration measure.

questions.stem: Posting 55%equity,an investor purchases a stock for€95 per share.Assuming no other activity,if the maintenance margin is 30%,the price below which a margin call first occurs is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it calculates the margin call price as initial price×(1–initial margin),forgetting to divide by(1–maintenance margin):€95×(1–0.55)=€42.75. B.Correct because the margin call price is calculated as initial price×(1–initial margin)/(1–maintenance margin).This equation is the algebraic rearrangement of the process and formula,where maintenance margin=(initial equity per share+margin call price–initial price).For this trade,the margin call price=€95×(1–0.55)/(1–0.30)=€95×0.64285≈€61.07. C.Incorrect because it calculates the margin call price as initial price×initial margin/(1–maintenance margin):€95×0.55/(1–0.3)≈€74.64.

questions.stem: Which of the following reflects the right of limited partners to reclaim part of the general partner's performance fee?
questions.option_c: Clawback provision
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the hurdle rate is a minimum rate of return,typically 8%,that the GP must exceed in order to earn the performance fee.GPs typically receive 20%of the total profit of the private equity fund net of any hard hurdle rate,in which case the GP earns fees on annual returns in excess of the hurdle rate,or net of the soft hurdle rate,in which case the fee is calculated on the entire annual gross return as long as the set hurdle is exceeded. B.Incorrect because the hurdle rate is a minimum rate of return,typically 8%,that the GP must exceed in order to earn the performance fee.GPs typically receive 20%of the total profit of the private equity fund net of any hard hurdle rate,in which case the GP earns fees on annual returns in excess of the hurdle rate,or net of the soft hurdle rate,in which case the fee is calculated on the entire annual gross return as long as the set hurdle is exceeded. C.correct because a clawback provision reflects the right of LPs to reclaim part of the GP’s performance fee.Along either waterfall path,if a GP ever accrues(or actually pays itself)an incentive fee on gains that are not yet fully realized and then subsequently gives back these gains,an investor is typically able to claw back prior incentive fee accruals and payments.Clawback provisions are usually activated when a GP exits successful deals early on but incurs losses on deals later in the fund’s life.

questions.stem: A company increased the dividend paid on its common stock by 3%per year over the past three years.If this growth rate is expected to continue indefinitely,the most appropriate model to estimate the intrinsic value of the stock is the:
questions.option_c: three-stage dividend discount model
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the Gordon growth model assumes perpetual constant growth.Because of its assumption of a constant growth rate,the Gordon growth model is particularly appropriate for valuing the equity of dividend-paying companies that are relatively insensitive to the business cycle and in a mature growth phase.A history of increasing the dividend at a stable growth rate is another practical criterion if the analyst believes that pattern will hold in the future. B.Incorrect because a two-stage model assumes that at some point the company will begin to pay dividends that grow at a constant rate,but prior to that time the company will pay dividends that are growing at a higher rate than can be sustained in the long run.Since the firm has been paying dividends that have been increasing and the pattern is expected to continue,the Gordon growth model is more suitable since it assumes that the dividend growth rate is forever:It is perpetual and never changes. C.Incorrect because a three-stage DDM would be most appropriate for a fairly young company,one that is just entering the growth phase.Since the firm operates in an industry that is relatively insensitive to the business cycle and has been paying a steady stream of increasing dividends,the Gordon growth model is more suitable since it assumes that the dividend growth rate is forever:It is perpetual and never changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about return-generating models is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Factor weights in the market model are derived from theoretical models
questions.option_b: The market model uses macroeconomic,fundamental,and statistical factors
questions.option_c: The single-index model allows the decomposition of total variance into systematic and nonsystematic variances
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because factor weights in return-generating models are usually derived from historical relationships between these factors and the returns.For example,in case of the market model,the intercept,αi,and slope coefficient,βi,can be estimated by using historical security and market returns.These parameter estimates are then used to predict company-specific returns that a security may earn in a future period. B.Incorrect because the most common implementation of a single-index model is the market model,in which the market return is the single factor or single index.Thus,the market model does not use any factor other than the market return. C.Correct because with the introduction of return-generating models,particularly the single-index model,we are able to decompose total variance into systematic and nonsystematic variances.

questions.stem: In the context of strategic asset allocation,adding asset classes with low correlation will most likely improve a portfolio’s risk–return trade-off as long as the stand-alone risk of the added asset class:
questions.option_a: does not exceed its diversification effect
questions.option_c: exceeds its diversification effect
questions.explanation: A.Correct because,in general,adding assets classes with low correlation improves the risk–return trade-off as long as the stand-alone risk of the added asset class does not exceed its diversification effect. B.Incorrect because adding assets classes with low correlation will only improve the risk–return trade-off if the stand-alone risk of the added asset class does not exceed its diversification effect. C.Incorrect because adding assets classes with low correlation will only improve the risk–return trade-off if the stand-alone risk of the added asset class does not exceed its diversification effect.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is least likely to be an example of a Eurobond?
questions.option_a: An Australian company issuing US$-denominated bonds to investors domiciled in Japan
questions.option_b: A UK-based company issuing Japanese yen-denominated bonds to investors domiciled in Japan
questions.option_c: A Japanese company issuing euro-denominated bonds to investors domiciled in the United Kingdom
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because this is an example of a Eurodollar bond. B.Correct because it is an example of a foreign bond,that is,a bond issued by a foreign company in the domestic market of the country in whose currency the bond is denominated. C.Incorrect because this is an example of a euro-denominated Eurobond.

questions.stem: An investor holds a€100 million portfolio.If the portfolio has a one-day 5%value at risk(VaR)of €5 million,the maximum potential loss on a given trading day is:
questions.option_c: greater than €5 million
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because VaR does not tell the maximum loss.The maximum loss is the entire equity of an organization or the entire value of a portfolio. B.Incorrect because VaR does not tell the maximum loss.The maximum loss is the entire equity of an organization or the entire value of a portfolio. C.Correct because value at risk or VaR is a measure of the size of the tail of the distribution of profits on a portfolio or for an entity.VaR does not tell the maximum loss.The maximum loss is the entire equity of an organization or the entire value of a portfolio,which is€100 million in this case.A one-day VaR of€5 million with a 5%probability means that the portfolio can expect to lose at least€5 million on a single trading day 5%of the time.

questions.stem: Consider a call option trading for$2.00 with an exercise price of$38.00.If the price of the underlying at expiration is$42.00,the payoff for the call option seller is:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the call seller’s payoff as:–c T =–Max(0,S T –X)=–Max(0,$42.00–$38.00)=–$4.00. B.Incorrect because the call seller’s profit(not payoff)is calculated as:–Max(0,S T –X)+c 0 =–Max(0,$42.00–$38.00)+$2.00=–$2.00. C.Incorrect because the call buyer’s(not seller’s)payoff is calculated as:Max(0,S T –X)=Max(0,$42.00–$38.00)=$4.00.

questions.stem: Macaulay duration is best described as:
questions.option_a: an average maturity of the bond
questions.option_b: a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments
questions.option_c: an estimated price change for a bond given a shift in its benchmark yield curve
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Macaulay duration is a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments. B.Correct because Macaulay duration is a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments. C.Incorrect because Macaulay duration is a weighted average of the time to receipt of the bond’s promised payments.

questions.stem: When a company has significant intangibles,asset-based valuation is most likely:
questions.option_a: used to determine the value of off the books assets
questions.option_b: less preferred than forward-looking cash flow valuation
questions.option_c: appropriate to calculate a maximum value for the company
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because an asset-based valuation of a company uses estimates of the market or fair value of the company’s assets and liabilities.Thus,asset-based valuations work well for companies that do not have a high proportion of intangible or“off the books”assets. B.Correct because when a company has significant intangibles,the analyst should prefer a forward-looking cash flow valuation. C.Incorrect because asset-based valuation may not consider some intangibles,thus it can give a“floor”value,not a maximum value,for a situation involving a significant amount of intangibles.

questions.stem: Which of the following natural resources has formed part of large institutional portfolios for decades?
questions.option_c: Both farmland and timberland
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because farmland as an investment is a more recent phenomenon,with only a few dedicated funds involved.With population growth,weather,and water management becoming more topical,however,investors may turn to these assets to actively address sustainability. B.Correct because timberland investment involves ownership of raw land and the harvesting of its trees for lumber,thus generating an income stream and the potential for capital gain,and timberland has been included in large institutional portfolios for decades.Farmland as an investment is a more recent phenomenon,with only a few dedicated funds involved.With population growth,weather,and water management becoming more topical,however,investors may turn to these assets to actively address sustainability. C.Incorrect because farmland as an investment is a more recent phenomenon,with only a few dedicated funds involved.With population growth,weather,and water management becoming more topical,however,investors may turn to these assets to actively address sustainability.

questions.stem: The book value of a company's equity increases when the company:
questions.option_c: distributes net income as dividends
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the book value of a company’s equity—the difference between its total assets and total liabilities—increases when the company retains its net income.The more net income that is earned[not lost]and retained,the greater the company’s book value of equity. B.Correct because the book value of a company’s equity—the difference between its total assets and total liabilities—increases when the company retains its net income.The more net income that is earned and retained,the greater the company’s book value of equity. C.Incorrect because the book value of a company’s equity—the difference between its total assets and total liabilities—increases when the co.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely a characteristic of real assets?
questions.option_c: Substantial management costs
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because real assets are characterized by illiquidity,not high liquidity. B.Incorrect because real assets are characterized by heterogeneity,not homogeneity. C.Correct because real assets are characterized by illiquidity,not high liquidity.The heterogeneity of real assets,their illiquidity,and the substantial costs of managing them are all factors that complicate the valuation of real assets.

questions.stem: If a security’s return is plotted to the right of the market portfolio on the security market line,the security has a:
questions.option_a: lower expected return and lower systematic risk than the market portfolio
questions.option_b: higher expected return and higher systematic risk than the market portfolio
questions.option_c: higher expected return and higher unsystematic risk than the market portfolio
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a security with a lower expected return and lower systematic risk would be plotted below and to the left of the market portfolio. B.Correct because the security market line(SML)is a graphical representation of the capital asset pricing model with beta,reflecting systematic risk,on the x-axis and expected return on the y-axis.The linear relationship between expected return and beta(systematic risk)is upward sloping.Therefore,a security that is plotted higher and to the right of the market portfolio exhibits higher expected return due to its exposure to higher systematic risk. C.Incorrect because the SML demonstrates the relationship between a security’s return and systematic risk,not unsystematic risk.

questions.stem: A seasoned equity offering occurs in the:
questions.option_c: alternative investment market
questions.explanation: A.Correct because if the issuer wants to sell additional units of a previously issued security,it makes a seasoned offering(sometimes called a secondary offering).Both types of offerings(IPO and seasoned offering)occur in the primary market where issuers sell their securities to investors. B.Incorrect because if the issuer wants to sell additional units of a previously issued security,it makes a seasoned offering(sometimes called a secondary offering).Both types of offerings(IPO and seasoned offering)occur in the primary market where issuers sell their securities to investors.Later,if investors trade these securities among themselves,they trade in secondary markets. C.Incorrect because practitioners distinguish between traditional investment markets and alternative investment markets.Alternative investments include hedge funds,private equities(including venture capital),commodities,real estate securities and real estate properties,securitized debts,operating leases,machinery,collectibles,and precious gems.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about open-end mutual funds and ETFs is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Investors can buy both open-end mutual funds and ETFs from other investors
questions.option_b: Open-end mutual funds can be priced intraday,while ETFs are priced once a day
questions.option_c: ETFs can be settled at a price different from the NAV,while open-end mutual funds are settled at the NAV
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because mutual fund investors buy the fund shares directly from the fund.An alternative to setting the fund up as an open-end fund would be to create a closed-end fund in which no new investment money is accepted into the fund.New investors invest by buying existing shares,and investors in the fund liquidate by selling their shares to other investors. B.Incorrect because ETFs can be transacted(and are priced)intraday.In contrast,mutual funds typically can be purchased or sold only once a day. C.Correct because mutual fund investors buy the fund shares directly from the fund,and all investments are settled at the net asset value.In practice,the market price of the ETF is likely to be close(but different)to the net asset value of the underlying investments.The mutual fund can be set up as an open-end fund or a closed-end fund.If it is an open-end fund,it will accept new investment money and issue additional shares at a value equal to the net asset value of the fund at the time of investment.

questions.stem: A company just paid an annual dividend of€1.25 per share.If the required annual rate of return is 14%and dividends are expected to grow indefinitely at a constant rate of 8%,the company’s intrinsic value per share is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because€16.88 is derived using the growth rate in the denominator of the formula instead of the difference between the required rate of return and the growth rate:V 0 =€1.35/0.08≈€16.88. B.Incorrect because€20.83 results from usingD 0 (instead of D 1 )as the next period dividend:V 0 =€1.25/0.06≈€20.83. C.Correct because the value of the shares can be estimated using the Gordon growth model:V 0 =D 0 (1+g)/(r-g)=(€1.25×1.08)/(0.14–0.08)=€1.35/0.06=€22.50.

questions.stem: An annual-pay option-free bond has a 3.5%coupon and three years until maturity.If the current price of this bond is 90,the market discount rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it interchanges the years to maturity[3]as the coupon rate,and the coupon rate[3.50]as the number of years until maturity.Using calculator inputs,PMT=3.00 or(3.0%×100);FV=100;N=3.5;PV=–90.00.Solve for I=6.2704≈6.27%. C.Correct because the general formula for calculating a bond price given the market discount rate is: PV=[PMT÷(1+r) 1 ]+[PMT÷(1+r) 2 ]+…+[(PMT+FV)÷(1+r) N ] Where: PV=present value,or the price of the bond PMT=coupon payment per period FV=future value paid at maturity,or the par value of the bond r=market discount rate,or required rate of return per period N=number of evenly spaced periods to maturity. Or,using calculator inputs,PMT=3.50 or(3.5%×100);FV=100;N=3;PV=–90.00(90%×–100,00).Solve for I=7.33378%≈7.33%.

questions.stem: All else being equal,a bond issuer is most likely to be evaluated as more creditworthy than its peers if it has a:
questions.option_a: lower debt/EBITDA and a lower EBITDA/interest expense
questions.option_b: lower debt/EBITDA and a higher EBITDA/interest expense
questions.option_c: higher debt/EBITDA and a lower EBITDA/interest expense
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because lower EBITDA/interest expense indicates that the company might not be able to cover its interest payments.interest payments and thus has a higher probability of default and lower creditworthiness(all else being equal). B.Correct because lower debt/EBITDA shows a lower level of debt compared to adjusted earnings and due to higher EBITDA interest coverage there is less risk that the company will not be able to pay its interest(coupon),leading to a lower probability of default and higher evaluation of creditworthiness(all else being equal). CDebt/EBITDA is a common leverage measure.A higher ratio indicates more leverage and thus higher credit risk.Note that this ratio can be very volatile for companies with high cash flow variability,such as those in cyclical industries and with high operating leverage(fixed costs). Coverage ratios measure an issuer’s ability to meet—to'cover'—its interest payments.The two most common are the EBITDA/interest expense and EBIT/interest expense ratios.The ratio EBITDA/interest expense)is a bit more liberal than the ratio EBIT/interest expense because it does not subtract out the impact of(non-cash)depreciation and amortization expense.A higher ratio indicates higher credit quality. C.Incorrect because higher debt/EBITDA shows that there is higher leverage in comparison to earnings and this increases the probability of default and lowers the evaluation of creditworthiness of the company(all else being equal)whilst a lower EBITDA/interest expense indicates that the company might not be able to cover its interest payments.interest payments and thus has a higher probability of default and lower creditworthiness(all else being equal).

questions.stem: Which of the following sources of private debt financing may provide equity participation to lenders or investors?
questions.option_c: Both venture debt and mezzanine debt
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because both venture debt and mezzanine debt might provide equity participation to lenders or investors. B.Incorrect because both venture debt and mezzanine debt might provide equity participation to lenders or investors. C.Correct because mezzanine debt often comes with additional features,such as warrants or conversion rights.These provide equity participation to lenders/investors,conveying the option to convert their debt into equity or purchasing the equity of the underlying borrower under certain circumstances.Similar to mezzanine debt,venture debt may carry additional features that compensate the investor/lender for the increased risk of default or for the start-up and early-stage companies that lack substantial assets for debt collateral.One such feature could grant the lender rights to purchase equity in the borrowing company under certain circumstances.

questions.stem: A protective put is a derivatives strategy that involves:
questions.option_a: selling a call and buying a put
questions.option_b: selling an asset and buying a put
questions.option_c: buying an asset and buying a put
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the strategy of holding the asset and a put is sometimes called a protective put. B.Incorrect because the strategy of holding the asset and a put is sometimes called a protective put. C.Correct because the strategy of holding the asset and a put is sometimes called a protective put.

questions.stem: An investment portfolio consists of equal weights in two government bonds of different nations.What correlation level will most likely result in the lowest portfolio standard deviation?
questions.explanation: A.Correct because,all else being equal,the lower the correlation,the lower the portfolio risk(standard deviation). B.Incorrect because a 0%correlation portfolio will reduce the risks but not as much as the negative correlated portfolio. C.Incorrect because a 50%correlation portfolio will reduce the risks but not as much as the negative correlated portfolio.

questions.stem: If a floating-rate note is trading at a discount to par,this bond's required margin is:
questions.option_b: the same as the quoted margin
questions.option_c: greater than the quoted margin
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because if the required margin is less than the quoted margin,the note will trade at a premium to par. B.Incorrect because if the required margin is the same as the quoted margin,the note would trade at par value. C.Correct because if the required margin is greater than the quoted margin,the note will trade at a discount to par.For example on a floater with a margin of 50 bps,if the required margin goes up to 75 bps because of a downgrade in the issuer’s credit rating,a floater having a quoted margin of 50 bps now pays its investors a“deficient”interest payment.This FRN will be priced at a discount below par value.

questions.stem: The expected return calculated using the CAPM is least likely used for:
questions.option_b: determining the economic feasibility of projects
questions.option_c: forecasting the internal rate of return of a project
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because setting fair insurance premiums is a valid application of the CAPM-derived expected return.The CAPM is used for estimating expected return in many scenarios.Other examples include calculating the cost of capital for regulated companies by regulatory commissions and setting fair insurance premiums. B.Incorrect because determining the economic feasibility of projects is a valid application of the CAPM-derived expected return.The required rate of return from the CAPM is also used for capital budgeting and determining the economic feasibility of projects. C.Correct because the CAPM-derived expected return is not used for forecasting the internal rate of return of a project,but instead is used as a hurdle rate or cost of capital for discounting forecast cash flows to arrive at a valuation.Given an asset's systematic risk,the expected return can be calculated using the CAPM.Recall that the price of an asset is the sum of all future cash flows discounted at the required rate of return,where the discount rate or the required rate of return is commensurate with the asset's risk.On the other hand,the internal rate of return is the discount rate at which the sum of present values of the project's cash flows will equal zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following approaches to implementing ESG considerations in portfolio construction most likely selects investments specifically based on their environmental or social benefits?
questions.option_c: Engage/active ownership
questions.explanation: A.Correct because impact investing specifically selects investment opportunities based on their intention to create a positive environmental and social impact. B.Incorrect because negative screening entails excluding companies or sectors based on business activities or environmental or social concerns. C.Incorrect because under the engagement/active ownership approach,investors use shareholder power to influence corporate behavior to achieve targeted ESG objectives along with financial returns.

questions.stem: The no-arbitrage condition is violated at option expiry when the value of an in-the-money:
questions.option_a: put option is below its exercise price
questions.option_b: put option is below its exercise value
questions.option_c: call option is below the price of its underlying
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because a put option buyer will exercise only if the spot price,ST,is below X at maturity.The exercise price,X,therefore represents the upper bound on the put value.Therefore,the no-arbitrage condition is not violated when the value of put option is below its exercise price. B.Correct because an option buyer will exercise a call or put option at maturity only if it returns a positive payoff—that is:(X−S T )>0 for a put.[referred to as its exercise value].Also,examples of in-the-money(ITM)options include a put option with an underlying spot price below the exercise price.So,the value of an ITM put is equal to its exercise value at expiry.Also,an option which trades below its exercise value violates the no-arbitrage condition.Therefore,the no-arbitrage condition is violated when the value of ITM put option is below its exercise value. C.Incorrect because the call buyer will not pay more for the right to purchase an underlying than the price of that underlying,which is the upper bound.Therefore,the no-arbitrage condition is not violated when the value of a call option is below the price to its underlying.

questions.stem: In the binomial option model,when the volatility of the underlying increases,the value of a call option:
questions.option_c: increases
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because if volatility increases,the difference between S1 + and S1 − increases,which widens the range between c1 + and c1 − ,leading to a higher option value.So,the option value will increase,not decrease. B.Incorrect because if volatility increases,the difference between S1 + and S1 − increases,which widens the range between c1 + and c1 − ,leading to a higher option value.So,the option value will increase,not remain unchanged. C.Correct because if volatility increases,the difference between S1 + and S1 − increases,which widens the range between c1 + and c1 − ,leading to a higher option value.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about three mortgage loans: All else being equal,the mortgage loan most likely to be classified as prime is:
questions.option_c: Loan 3
questions.explanation: A.Correct because there are two types of mortgages based on the credit quality of the borrower:prime loans and subprime loans.Prime loans generally have borrowers of high credit quality with strong employment and credit histories,income sufficient to pay the loan obligation,and substantial equity in the underlying property.Subprime loans have borrowers with lower credit quality and/or are loans without a first lien on the property.In addition,the lower the LTV,the higher the borrower’s equity.Therefore,Loan#1,with Low LTV and a First Lien would most likely be considered a Prime loan. B.Incorrect because there are two types of mortgages based on the credit quality of the borrower:prime loans and subprime loans.Prime loans generally have borrowers of high credit quality with strong employment and credit histories,income sufficient to pay the loan obligation,and substantial equity in the underlying property.Subprime loans have borrowers with lower credit quality and/or are loans without a first lien on the property.In addition,the lower the LTV,the higher the borrower’s equity.Therefore,because Loan#2 has a second lien on the collateral,it would not likely be considered a Prime loan. C.Incorrect because there are two types of mortgages based on the credit quality of the borrower:prime loans and subprime loans.Prime loans generally have borrowers of high credit quality with strong employment and credit histories,income sufficient to pay the loan obligation,and substantial equity in the underlying property.Subprime loans have borrowers with lower credit quality and/or are loans without a first lien on the property.In addition,the lower the LTV,the higher the borrower’s equity.Therefore,because Loan#3 has a High LTV ratio,it would not likely be considered a Prime loan.

questions.stem: The value of a European call is inversely related to which of the following factors?
questions.option_c: Value of the underlying
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the value of a European call option is inversely related to the exercise price. B.Incorrect because the value of a European call option is directly related to the time to expiration. C.Incorrect because the value of a European call option is directly related to the value of the underlying.

B.Correct because the formula for calculating the standard deviation of a two stock portfolio,σp,is: σ p =[w 1 2 σ 1 2 +w 2 2 σ 2 2 +2w 1 w 2 ρ 12 σ 1 σ 2 ] 1/2 where: w=weight of each stock σ=standard deviation ρ 12 =the correlation of returns between Stock 1 and Stock 2 Plugging in the numbers,σp= [(0.25 2 ×0.12 2 )+(0.75 2 ×0.16 2 )+(2×0.25×0.75×0.12×0.16×0.75)] 0.5 ≈0.1439=14.39% C.Incorrect because it omits the correlation coefficient in calculating the standard deviation:[(0.25 2 ×0.12 2 )+(0.75 2 ×0.16 2 )+ (2×0.25×0.75×0.12×0.16)] 0.5 =0.15=15%,which is the weighted average standard deviation.

questions.stem: The process of representing ownership rights to physical assets on a distributed ledger best describes:
questions.option_c: a permissioned network
questions.explanation: A.Correct because tokenization is the process of representing ownership rights to physical assets on a blockchain or distributed ledger. B.Incorrect because blockchain is a type of digital ledger in which information,such as changes in ownership,is recorded sequentially within blocks that are then linked or“chained”together and secured using cryptographic methods.Each block contains a grouping of transactions(or entries)and a secure link(known as a hash)to the previous block.New transactions are inserted into the chain only after validation via a consensus mechanism in which authorized members agree on the transaction and the preceding order,or history,in which previous transactions have occurred. C.Incorrect because in permissioned networks,network members may be restricted from participating in certain network activities.Controls,or permissions,may be used to allow varying levels of access to the ledger,from adding transactions(e.g.,a participant)to viewing transactions only(e.g.,a regulator)to viewing selective details of the transactions but not the full record.

questions.stem: With respect to leveraged buyouts,the current management team will continue to manage the company in:
questions.option_c: both management buy-ins and management buyouts
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the leveraged buyout may also be of a specific type.In management buyouts(MBOs),the current management team is involved in the acquisition,and in management buy-ins(MBIs),the current management team is being replaced and the acquiring team will be involved in managing the company. B.Correct because the leveraged buyout may also be of a specific type.In management buyouts(MBOs),the current management team is involved in the acquisition,and in management buy-ins(MBIs),the current management team is being replaced and the acquiring team will be involved in managing the company. C.Incorrect because the leveraged buyout may also be of a specific type.In management buyouts(MBOs),the current management team is involved in the acquisition,and in management buy-ins(MBIs),the current management team is being replaced and the acquiring team will be involved in managing the company.

questions.stem: Compared to mutual funds,hedge funds most likely:
questions.option_b: have a longer notice period for redemptions than a mutual fund
questions.option_c: use a traditional index benchmark to gauge investment performance
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because with reduced operating constraints,hedge funds may invest in less liquid and unnoticed opportunities,the true valuation of which may at times be opaque. B.Correct because investors in modern hedge funds are subject to extended holding periods(known as lockup periods)and subsequent notice periods before an investment redemption is possible.Compared,for example,to many mutual funds allowing easier redemption and guaranteed liquidity on one day’s notice,such mandatory periods combine with a lighter regulatory compliance burden(in certain areas)to allow hedge funds more flexibility. C.Incorrect because a contemporary hedge fund generally has a goal to generate high returns,either in an absolute sense or on a risk-adjusted basis relative to its portfolio-level volatility.Gauging performance relative to a traditional index benchmark can be difficult,given that low correlation with traditional asset investing is frequently a selling point.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following cash flows(in$millions)for a private equity fund: If the terminal value is$180 million,an investor's multiple of invested capital(MOIC)is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because it reduces the liquidity event by the management fees and fund expenses(as opposed to reducing the invested capital by that amount).MOIC=(Realized value of investment+Unrealized value of investment)/Total amount of invested capital(which is paid-in capital less management fees and fund expenses). MOIC≠(180–12–8)/100=1.60x. B.Incorrect because it fails to subtract the management fees from the invested capital in the correct calculation.MOIC=(Realized value of investment+Unrealized value of investment)/Total amount of invested capital(which is paid-in capital less management fees and fund expenses).MOIC≠180/(100–8)=1.96x. C.Correct because MOIC=(Realized value of investment+Unrealized value of investment)/Total amount of invested capital(which is paid-in capital less management fees and fund expenses).Hence,MOIC=180/(100–12–8)=2.25x.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is most accurate about a strong-form efficient market?
questions.option_a: Fundamental analysis can generate abnormal returns
questions.option_b: Insiders can earn abnormal returns from trading on private information
questions.option_c: Passive portfolio management should outperform active portfolio management
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because fundamental analysis is the examination of publicly available information and the formulation of forecasts to estimate the intrinsic value of assets.However,in a strong-form efficient market,security prices fully reflect both public and private information.Therefore,fundamental analysis cannot generate abnormal return in a strong-form efficient market. B.Incorrect because in the case of a strong-form efficient market,insiders would not be able to earn abnormal returns from trading on the basis of private information.A strong-form efficient market also means that prices reflect all private information,which means that prices reflect everything that the management of a company knows about the financial condition of the company that has not been publicly released. C.Correct because if securities markets are weak-form and semi-strong-form efficient,the implication is that active trading,whether attempting to exploit price patterns or public information,is not likely to generate abnormal returns.In other words,passive portfolio management should outperform active portfolio management.If this applies to weak-form and semi-strong form efficient markets,it applies to a strong-form efficient market as well.

questions.stem: A bond issued by the International Monetary Fund is best classified as a：
questions.option_c: quasi-government bond
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because sovereign bonds are issued by national governments.National governments issue bonds primarily for fiscal reasons—to fund spending when tax revenues are insufficient to cover expenditures.Bonds issued by national governments,are often referred to as sovereign bond or sovereigns. B.Correct because supranational bonds are a form of often highly rated bonds issued by supranational agencies,also referred to as multilateral agencies.The most well-known supranational agencies are the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development(the World Bank),the International Monetary Fund(IMF). C.Incorrect because quasi-government bonds are issued by entities established by national governments to perform various functions.These organizations often have both public and private sector characteristics,but they are not actual governmental entities.

questions.stem: Challenges in constructing fixed-income indexes most likely include that:
questions.option_a: there is a small number of securities
questions.option_b: securities are relatively illiquid compared to equities
questions.option_c: fixed-income markets are predominantly order-driven markets
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the number of fixed-income securities is many times larger than the number of equity securities.To represent a specific fixed-income market or segment,indexes may include thousands of different securities.Over time,these fixed-income securities mature,and issuers offer new securities to meet their financing needs,leading to turnover in fixed-income indexes. B.Correct because in the fixed income market many securities do not trade frequently and,as a result,are relatively illiquid.As a result,index providers must contact dealers to obtain current prices on constituent securities to update the index or they must estimate the prices of constituent securities using the prices of traded fixed-income securities with similar characteristics. C.Incorrect because a challenge in index construction is that fixed-income markets are predominantly dealer markets.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about the limit order book for a stock: Based only on this information,which of the following orders to purchase 50 shares will be executed immediately at a price of$78.00?
questions.option_c: Both a market order and a limit order at$78.00
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because while a market order will execute,a limit order will also execute.A limit order seeks the best price immediately available,but in no event accept a price higher than a specified limit price when buying or accept a price lower than a specified limit price when selling.As the lowest offer price is$78.00 for 80 shares,the order will be executed immediately even if it is a limit order at$78.00 B.Incorrect because a limit order and a market order will execute.A market order instructs the broker or exchange to obtain the best price immediately available when filling the order.As the lowest offer price is$78.00 for 80 shares,the order will be executed immediately even if it is a market order. C.Correct because a market order instructs the broker or exchange to obtain the best price immediately available when filling the order.A limit order conveys almost the same instruction:obtain the best price immediately available,but in no event accept a price higher than a specified limit price when buying or accept a price lower than a specified limit price when selling.As the lowest offer price$78.00 for 80 shares,the order will be executed immediately if it is either a market order or a limit order at$78.00

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company's common stock and the market: If the growth rate of dividends is expected to be 2%,the stock's intrinsic value based on the Gordon growth model is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because D 0 is used instead of D 1 :V 0 =$10/(11.4%-2%)=$10/9.4%≈$106.38. B. Correct because the intrinsic value of a common stock is where:V 0 =Intrinsic value of the stock today;r=Required rate of return on the stock;and g=Dividend growth rate. The required rate of return on a common stock is the sum of the current expected risk-free rate plus a risk premium that equals the product of the stock's beta(a measure of non-diversifiable risk)and the market risk premium(the expected return of the market in excess of the risk-free return).Based on the information in the table and expressing the formula in alphanumeric format we have: r=r f +β×(r m –r f ).That is,r=3%+1.4×(9%-3%)=11.4%.Therefore:V 0 =$10×(1+2%)/(11.4%–2%)=10.2/9.4%≈$108.51. C.Incorrect because the candidate has applied the following formula to derive the stock's intrinsic value:V 0 =D 1 /(r m –g)=$10×(1+2%)/(9%–2%)=10.2/7%≈$145.71.

questions.stem: With respect to index weighting methods,constituent securities with both small market capitalizations and low prices are most likely overrepresented in a(n):
questions.option_c: market-capitalization-weighted index
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because in price weighting,the weight on each constituent security is determined by dividing its price by the sum of all the prices of the constituent securities.Therefore,securities with low prices are most likely a small part of a price-weighted index and as such are not likely overrepresented in a price-weighted index. B.Correct because securities that constitute a small fraction of the target market value are overrepresented.In this case,securities with small market caps and low prices constitute a small fraction of the target market value. C.Incorrect because in market-capitalization weighting,or value weighting,the weight on each constituent security is determined by dividing its market capitalization by the total market capitalization(the sum of the market capitalizations)of all securities in the index.Market capitalization or value is calculated by multiplying the number of shares outstanding by the market price per share.Therefore,securities with small market capitalizations are most likely a small part of a market-capitalization weighted index and as such are not likely overrepresented in such an index.

questions.stem: An index is made up of only two stocks.An analyst gathers the following information about those two stocks: Which of the following index weighting methods results in the largest weighting for Stock 2?
questions.option_c: Float-adjusted market-capitalization weighting
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because Stock 2 has a weight of 84.21%under a float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted index.This is greater compared to its weight under a price-weighted index(76.92%). In price weighting,the weight on each constituent security is determined by dividing its price by the sum of all the prices of the constituent securities. B.Incorrect because Stock 2 has a weight of 84.21%under a float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted index.This is greater compared to its weight under a market-capitalization-weighted index(75.91%). In market-capitalization weighting,or value weighting,the weight on each constituent security is determined by dividing its market capitalization by the total market capitalization(the sum of the market capitalization)of all the securities in the index.Market capitalization or value is calculated by multiplying the number of shares outstanding by the market price per share,where shares outstanding is the sum of the shares available to the public and the shares held by controlling shareholders. C.Correct because Stock 2 has a weight of 84.21%under a float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted index.This is greater compared to its weight under a price-weighted index(76.92%=100/(30+100))or a market-capitalization-weighted index(75.91%=690/(219+690)). In float-adjusted market-capitalization weighting,the weight on each constituent security is determined by adjusting its market capitalization for its market float.Typically,market float is the number of shares of the constituent security that are available to the investing public. Float-adjusted market cap=market float×BOP price. BOP weight=float-adjusted market cap/total float-adjusted market cap.

questions.stem: The yield-to-maturity of a 5-year,8%annual-pay bond priced at 108.42 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the yield-to-maturity is the discount rate,r,that equates the price of the bond to the present value of the coupon payments and par value:8/(1+r)+8/(1+r) 2 +8/(1+r) 3 +8/(1+r) 4 +108/(1+r) 5 =108.42,r=6.00%.N=5,PV=–108.42,PMT=8,FV=100,I/Y=6.00%. B.Incorrect because the yield-to-maturity is the discount rate,r,that equates the price of the bond to the present value of the coupon payments and par value.This answer computes the current yield instead of the yield to maturity.The current yield is the sum of the coupon payments received over the year divided by the flat price.8/108.42≈7.38%. C.Incorrect because the yield-to-maturity is the discount rate,r,that equates the price of the bond to the present value of the coupon payments and par value.This answer reverses the purchase price and the par value:8/(1+r)+8/(1+r) 2 +8/(1+r) 3 +8/(1+r) 4 +(108.42+8)/(1+r) 5 =100,r≈9.40%.N=5,PV=–100,PMT=8,FV=108.42,I/Y≈9.40%.

questions.stem: In the portfolio management process,the decision whether to use a nominal or real return objective is most likely part of the:
questions.option_c: execution step
questions.explanation: A.Correct because the planning step includes the preparation of an investment policy statement(IPS).One of the major components of an IPS is the return objective.Care should be taken that client and manager are in agreement on whether the return objective is nominal(which is more convenient for measurement purposes)or real(i.e.,inflation-adjusted,which usually relates better to the objective). B.Incorrect because determination of the return objective is included in the preparation of the IPS,which is part of the planning,not feedback,step.The feedback step includes:(1)Portfolio monitoring and rebalancing,and(2)Performance measurement and reporting. C.Incorrect because determination of the return objective is included in the preparation of the IPS,which is part of the planning,not execution,step.The execution step includes:(1)Asset allocation,(2)Security analysis,and(3)Portfolio construction.

questions.stem: The yields of a series of zero-coupon government bonds for a full range of maturities best define a:
questions.option_c: forward curve
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because in addition to the yield curve on coupon bonds and the spot curve on zero-coupon bonds,maturity structure can be assessed using a par curve.A par curve is a sequence of yields-to-maturity such that each bond is priced at par value. B.Correct because yields-to-maturity on a series of zero-coupon government bonds for a full range of maturities is the government bond spot curve,sometimes called the zero or“strip”curve. C.Incorrect because a forward market is for future delivery,beyond the usual settlement time period in the cash market.Agreement to the terms for the transaction is on the trade date,but delivery of the security and payment for it is deferred to a future date.A forward rate is the interest rate on a bond or money market instrument traded in a forward market.Thus a forward curve is composed of a series of forward rates.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about three well-diversified equity portfolios: Given a risk-free rate of 1.8%,the portfolio with the highest Treynor ratio is:
questions.option_c: Portfolio 3
questions.explanation: A.Incorrect because the Treynor ratio of Portfolio 1 ranks above Portfolio 3,but below Portfolio 2. TR 1 =(R 1 −R f )/β 1 =(9.2%−1.8%)/1.2 =0.0617 B.Correct because the Treynor Ratio of Portfolio 2 is the highest of the three portfolios. TR 2 =(R 2 −R f )/β 2 =(12.4%−1.8%)/1.4 =0.0757 The Treynor ratio is a simple extension of the Sharpe ratio and resolves the Sharpe ratio’s first limitation by substituting beta(systematic risk)for total risk.The portfolio with the highest Treynor ratio will be the best performing based on that measure. C.Incorrect because Portfolio 3 has the lowest Treynor ratio of the three portfolios. TR3=(R 3 −R f )/β 3 =(15.0%−1.8%)/2.3 =0.0574

questions.stem: Empirical duration:
questions.option_a: assumes that government bond yields and spreads are independent variables
questions.option_b: is higher than analytical duration for high-yield bonds under market stress scenarios
