B is incorrect because "[t]here are two types of waterfalls: deal-by-deal (or American) waterfalls and whole-of-fund (or European) waterfalls… In contrast to deal-by-deal waterfalls, whole-of-fund waterfalls occur at the aggregate fund level (i.e., after all investments have been exited) and are more advantageous to the LPs." C is incorrect because "[t]here are two types of waterfalls: deal-by-deal (or American) waterfalls and whole-of-fund (or European) waterfalls… In contrast to deal-by-deal waterfalls, whole-of-fund waterfalls occur at the aggregate fund level (i.e., after all investments have been exited) and are more advantageous to the LPs."

questions.stem: Assume management fees are calculated using end-of-period valuation. The investor’s net return given this fee structure is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct. Management fee: 1% of $112 million = $1.12 million Incentive fee: 10% of ($12 million – $ 1.12 million) = $1.088 million Fund value after fees: $112 million – $1.12 million – $1.088 million = $109.792 million Investor return: ($109.792 million/$100 million) – 1 = 9.79% A is incorrect. It neglects the incentive fee. Management fee: 1% of $112 million = $1.12 million Fund value after fees: $112 million – $1.12 million = $110.88 million Investor return: ($110.88 million/$100 million) – 1 = 10.88% C is incorrect. It ignores the fact that the incentive fee is calculated net of management fees. Management fee: 1% of $112 million = $1.12 million. Incentive fee: 10% of $12 million = $1.2 million. Fund value after fees: $112 million – $1.12 million – $1.2 million = $109.68 million Investor return: ($109.68 million / $100 million) - 1 = 9.68%

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely used by private equity funds?
questions.option_c: Convertible bond arbitrage strategies
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[t]he majority of private equity activity involves leveraged buyouts." "Leveraged buyouts (LBOs) or highly leveraged transactions arise when private equity firms establish buyout funds (or LBO funds) to acquire public companies or established private companies, with a significant percentage of the purchase price financed through debt." B is incorrect because "[m]erger arbitrage… [is a strategy] used by hedge funds." "HFR classifies hedge funds under four broad strategy categories: event-driven, relative value, macro, and equity hedge." "Event-driven strategies [used by hedge funds] seek to profit from defined catalyst events… Further subdivisions of this category by HFR include the following: Merger arbitrage." C is incorrect because convertible bond arbitrage are strategies used by hedge funds. "Examples of relative value strategies [used by hedge funds] include the following: Convertible bond arbitrage."

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about direct ownership of real estate is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Local real estate market expertise is important for success
questions.option_b: Investors have no control over the tenant selection process
questions.option_c: Investors cannot use non-cash property depreciation expenses to reduce taxable income
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[m]ajor disadvantages to investing directly include the extensive time required to manage the property, the importance of local real estate market expertise to success, and the large capital requirements." B is incorrect because "[t]here are several benefits to owning real estate directly. One is control. Only the owner decides when to buy or sell, when and how much to spend on capital projects (subject to lease terms and regulatory requirements), whom to select as tenants based on credit quality preference..." C is incorrect because "[p]roperty investors in the largest countries as ranked by the size of the institutional-quality real estate market can use non-cash property depreciation expenses and interest expense, with some limitations, to reduce taxable income and lower their income tax bills."

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered an economic infrastructure asset?
questions.option_c: Information and communication technology assets
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[e]conomic infrastructure assets support economic activity and include three broad types of assets: transportation assets, information and communication technology (ICT) assets, and utility and energy assets: ■ICT assets include infrastructure that stores, broadcasts, and transmits information or data, such as telecommunication towers and data centers." A is incorrect because health care assets are an example of social infrastructure assets. "Social infrastructure assets are directed toward human activities and include such assets as educational, health care, social housing, and correctional facilities, with the focus on providing, operating, and maintaining the asset infrastructure." B is incorrect because educational assets are an example of social infrastructure assets. "Social infrastructure assets are directed toward human activities and include such assets as educational, health care, social housing, and correctional facilities, with the focus on providing, operating, and maintaining the asset infrastructure."

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about commodities is most accurate？
questions.option_a: Commodities are effective hedges against inflation
questions.option_b: Commodity indexes are based on the prices of the underlying physical commodities
questions.option_c: Commodity returns historically demonstrated a high correlation with returns of diversified traditional asset portfolios
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[c]ommodity investing may be attractive to investors not only for the potential profits but also because of the following perceptions: (1) Commodities are effective hedges against inflation." B is incorrect because "[i]n order to be transparent, investable, and replicable, commodity indexes typically use the price of the futures contracts rather than the prices of the underlying commodities." C is incorrect because "[c]ommodity returns have historically had a low [and not high] correlation with other [traditional] investment returns".

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an event-driven hedge fund strategy?
questions.option_a: Buying the stock of a company that is spinning off a subsidiary
questions.option_b: Selling stock options to earn premiums and benefit from limited market movements
questions.option_c: Taking long positions in undervalued stocks and short positions in overvalued stocks
questions.explanation: A is correct because it describes a special situations investment strategy, a type of event-driven investing. "Event-driven strategies seek to profit from defined catalyst events, typically those that involve changes in corporate structure, such as an acquisition or restructuring… Special situations. These strategies focus on opportunities to get involved in the equity of companies that are engaged in restructuring activities other than mergers, acquisitions, or bankruptcy. These activities include security issuance or repurchase, special capital distributions, rescue finance, and asset sales/spin-offs." B is incorrect because it describes a relative value (short volatility) strategy. "Relative value funds seek to profit from a pricing discrepancy, an unusual short-term relationship, between related securities… Examples of relative value strategies include the following: … Volatility… a short-volatility strategy involves selling options to earn the premiums and benefit from calm markets but can experience significant losses during unexpected periods of market stress." C is incorrect because it describes an equity market neutral strategy. "Market neutral… strategies use quantitative (technical) and fundamental analysis to identify under- and overvalued equity securities. The hedge fund takes long positions in securities it has identified as undervalued and short positions in securities it has identified as overvalued."

questions.stem: A company issues a noncallable, nonconvertible perpetual preferred stock with the following terms: The cost of preferred stock is closest to:
questions.explanation: C is correct because the cost of preferrred stock is: r P = D P /P P Where P p = the current preferred stock price per share D P = the preferred stock dividend per share r P = the cost of preferred stock r P = 1.30/24.75 = 0.052525 ≈ 5.25%. A is incorrect because the tax rate is used in the calculation. "Unlike interest on debt, the dividend on preferred stock is not tax-deductible by the company; therefore, there is no adjustment to the cost for taxes." r P ≠ 1.30(1 – t)/24.75 = 1.17/24.75 = 0.047273 ≈ 4.73%. B is incorrect because par value is used instead of market value. r P ≠ 1.30/25.00 ;= 0.052000 ≈ 5.20%.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is most accurate? Private companies:
questions.option_a: are typically subject to registration requirements.
questions.option_b: may be restricted to issue securities only to accredited investors.
questions.option_c: have little ownership overlap between management and shareholders.
questions.explanation: B is correct "[b]ecause private securities are generally not registered with a regulatory authority, investors may be restricted to accredited investors, also termed 'eligible' or 'professional' investors depending on the jurisdiction. Accredited investors are those who are sophisticated enough to take greater risks and to have a reduced need for regulatory oversight and protection. To be considered accredited, an investor must have a certain level of income or net worth or possess a certain amount of professional experience or knowledge. Given the lower levels of disclosure required of private companies, regulators want to make sure that investors understand the associated risks and can afford the possibility of losing their entire investment." A is incorrect because "[p]rivately-held companies are not exchange listed nor usually subject to registration requirements" and "private securities are generally not registered with a regulatory authority". C is incorrect because this applies for public, not private companies. "Publicly-held companies are most often listed on exchanges and required to register shares. Their shares are typically liquid with minor ownership overlap between management and shareholders". Also, "[w]ith often smaller numbers of shareholders in private companies, investors have greater control over management and there may be greater chance of ownership overlaps between management and shareholders".

questions.stem: Which of the following best reflects good corporate governance?
questions.option_c: Diversity, experience, and independence of directors
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[m]ost corporate governance codes require that the board include a diverse mix of expertise, backgrounds, and competencies. Such qualifications may include specialized knowledge of the company’s industry as well as experience in certain functions, such as strategy, finance/audit, risk management, human resources, or legal. Moreover, many companies seek age, gender, and racial diversity in board composition...Non-executive (or external) directors provide objective decision making, monitoring, and performance assessment. Additionally, non-executive directors can serve an important role in challenging management and using past expertise in strategy and board issues. An independent director is a specific type of non-executive director that does not have a material relationship with the company with regard to employment, ownership, or remuneration." Also, "[k]ey analyst considerations in corporate governance and stakeholder management include economic ownership and voting control, board of directors representation, remuneration and company performance, investor composition, strength of shareholders' rights, and the management of long-term risks." A is incorrect because when "economic ownership becomes separated from control, investors can face significant potential risks...Critics of these structures believe they create conflicts of interest between the providers of capital and the management of the business. It is virtually impossible for outside investors to dismantle dual-class structures because of the inherent design of their unequal voting rights." B is incorrect because product brand reputation does not point to the quality of corporate governance. "A notable example is Toshiba Corp., beginning in 2015 when an investigation revealed that company managers had manufactured nearly $2 billion in profits since 2008. Poor internal controls allowed the fraudulent accounting to remain undetected for seven years." "Key analyst considerations in corporate governance and stakeholder management include economic ownership and voting control, board of directors representation, remuneration and company performance, investor composition, strength of shareholders' rights, and the management of long-term risks."

questions.stem: Investing in assets specifically related to an ESG factor, such as sustainable agriculture, best describes:
questions.option_c: engagement/active ownership.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[t]hematic investing is investment in themes or assets specifically related to ESG factors, such as clean energy, green technology, sustainable agriculture, gender diversity, or affordable housing." B is incorrect because "the positive screening approach focuses on investments that manage their material ESG risks well relative to industry peers. Positive screening, typically implemented through an ESG ranking or scoring approach, is the inclusion of certain sectors, companies, or practices in a fund or portfolio based on specific ESG criteria." C is incorrect because "[e]ngagement/active ownership is the use of shareholder or bondholder power to influence corporate behavior through direct corporate engagement (i.e., communicating with senior management and/or boards of companies), filing or co-filing shareholder proposals, and proxy voting that is directed by ESG guidelines."

questions.stem: The risk of a loss of market share or pricing power best describes:
questions.option_c: product market risk.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[c]ompetitive risk can be defined as the risk of a loss of market share or pricing power to competitors and often reflects a lack of competitive advantage." Also, "[w]hen market share and pricing power are low or declining, the level of competitive pressure and risk is generally high." A is incorrect because "[e]xecution risk arises from the possibility that management will be unable to do what is needed to deliver the expected results." C is incorrect because "[p]roduct market risk is the risk that the market for a new product or service will fall short of expectations."

questions.stem: For a capital investment, financing costs are most likely reflected in the:
questions.option_c: projected future cash flows.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[f]inancing costs are reflected in the required rate of return..." A is incorrect because "[f]inancing costs are reflected in the required rate of return and thus ignored in cash flows to avoid double-counting." C is incorrect because "[f]inancing costs are ignored. Financing costs are reflected in the required rate of return and thus ignored in cash flows to avoid double-counting."

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is the most accurate description concerning the internal rate of return (IRR) method? IRR:
questions.option_a: is the preferred method for evaluating mutually exclusive projects.
questions.option_b: assumes that all cash flows from a project will be reinvested at the computed IRR.
questions.option_c: is sensitive to changes in the firm’s weighted average cost of capital.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The internal rate of return method assumes that the cash flows from a project are reinvested at the project’s IRR; the net present value (NPV) method assumes that cash flows are reinvested at the cost of capital. A is incorrect. NPV is the preferred method both because NPV directly measures the gain or loss in wealth from the project and because the reinvestment assumption of the NPV method is the more economically realistic. C is incorrect. The IRR method is not sensitive to WACC but sensitive to the timing and pattern of the cash flows. In particular, when a project has a nonconventional cash flow pattern, there may be multiple IRRs or no IRR.

questions.stem: In capital investment decisions, an abandonment option is most likely a type of:
questions.option_c: flexibility option.
questions.explanation: A is correct because an abandonment option is a type of sizing option. "If after investing the company can abandon the investment if the financial results are disappointing, it has an abandonment option." B is incorrect because an abandonment option is a type of sizing option, not a type of timing option. A timing option means that "[i]nstead of investing now, the company can delay investing. Delaying an investment and basing the decision on hopefully improved information...could help improve the NPV of the projects selected." C is incorrect because an abandonment option is a type of sizing option, not a type of flexibility option. "Once an investment is made, operational flexibilities besides abandonment or expansion may be available...Management may be able to exercise a price-setting option [which is a flexibility option to benefit from excess demand]. There are also production flexibility options which offer the operational flexibility to alter production when demand varies from what is forecast."

questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary source of liquidity?
questions.option_c: Short-term investment portfolio
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[t]he main difference between primary and secondary sources of liquidity is that using a primary source is not likely to affect the normal operations of the company, whereas using a secondary source might result in a change in the company’s financial and operating positions. Secondary sources used by companies include negotiating debt contracts, such as relieving pressures from high interest payments or principal repayments, waiving debt covenants or suspending dividends". A is incorrect because "[p]rimary sources of liquidity represent the most readily accessible resources available to the company. These can be cash held or near-cash securities and include the following: Free cash flow, which is the firm’s after-tax operating cash flow less planned short- and long-term investments." C is incorrect because "[p]rimary sources of liquidity represent the most readily accessible resources available to the company. These can be cash held or near-cash securities and include the following:...Short-term funds, which can include items such as trade credit, bank lines of credit, and short-term investment portfolios of the firm."

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in € millions) about three companies: The company with the highest quick ratio is:
questions.option_c: Company 3.
questions.explanation: B is correct because the quick ratio = (cash + short term securities + A/R)/Current Liabilities Company 1 quick ratio = (50 + 30)/60 = 1.333 Company 2 quick ratio = (60 + 70)/90 = 1.444 Company 3 quick ratio = (90 + 40)/100 = 1.300 A is incorrect because Company 1 has the highest current ratio not quick ratio: Current ratio = (cash + short term securities + A/R + Inventories)/Current Liabilities Company 1 current ratio = (50 + 30 + 40)/60 = 2.000 Company 2 current ratio = (60 + 70 + 20)/90 = 1.667 Company 3 current ratio = (90 + 40 + 60)/100 = 1.900 C is incorrect because Company 3 has the highest cash ratio, not quick ratio: Cash ratio = (cash + short term securities)/Current Liabilities Company 1 cash ratio = 50/60 = 0.8333 Company 2 cash ratio = 60/90 = 0.6667 Company 3 cash ratio = 90/100 = 0.900

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company: Assuming a marginal tax rate of 20% and that interest expense is tax deductible, the company's WACC is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct because the WACC accounts for the tax deductibility of debt and incorporates the market value actual capital structure weightings. "Taking the sources of capital to be common stock, preferred stock, and debt and allowing for the fact that in some jurisdictions, interest expense may be tax deductible, the expression for WACC is WACC = w d r d (1 – t) + w p r p + w e r e (1)." WACC = [0.08 Χ (1 – 0.20) Χ (100 / 500)] + [0.12 Χ (400 / 500)] = 0.1088 A is incorrect because an equally-weighted capital structure based on book values instead of weights based on market values is used, in lieu of the market value implied capital structure. "The weights are the proportions of the various sources of capital that the company uses to support its investment program." WACC = [0.08 Χ (1 – 0.20) Χ 0.50] + [0.12 Χ 0.50] = 0.092 C is incorrect since the tax deductibility of debt is ignored. "Taking the sources of capital to be common stock, preferred stock, and debt and allowing for the fact that in some jurisdictions, interest expense may be tax deductible, the expression for WACC is WACC = w d r d (1 – t) + w p r p + w e r e (1)." WACC = [0.08 Χ (100 / 500)] + [0.12 Χ (400 / 500)] = 0.1120

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company's bond issue: If the company's marginal tax rate is 30%, the company's after-tax cost of debt is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[t]he before-tax required return on debt is typically estimated using the expected yield to maturity (YTM) of the company’s debt based on current market values." Using a financial calculator, PV = (1040), FV = 1000, N = 10 × 2 = 20, PMT = 1000 × 0.04/2 = 20 and solving for I/Y gives ≈ 1.76% × 2 = 3.52%. After tax, this is 3.52 × (1 – 0.30) ≈ 2.47%. A is incorrect because the yield to maturity calculation fails to annualize the semi-annual calculated yield. Using a financial calculator, PV = (1040), FV = 1000, N = 10 × 2 = 20, PMT = 1000 × 0.04/2 = 20 and solving for I/Y gives ≈ 1.76%. After tax, this is 1.76 × (1 – 0.30) ≈ 1.23%. Also, "[t]he before-tax required return on debt is typically estimated using the expected yield to maturity (YTM) of the company’s debt based on current market values." C is incorrect because it uses the coupon rather than YTM for the cost of debt. Calculated as 4% × (1 – 0.30) = 2.8%. Also, "[t]he before-tax required return on debt is typically estimated using the expected yield to maturity (YTM) of the company’s debt based on current market values."

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company and the market: The company's estimated cost of equity is:
questions.explanation: C is correct because the CAPM is the appropriate method to estimate the cost of equity given the inputs. E(R i ) = R F + β i × [E(R M ) – R F ] where: β i is the equity beta E(R M ) – R F is the expected market risk premium, MRP E(R M ) is the expected market return R F is the risk-free rate The risk-free rate can be found by MRP = E(R M ) – R F ; 8% = 9% – R F ; R F = 1%. Thus, the equity cost of capital = R F + β i × [E(R M ) – R F ] = 1% + 0.8 × 8% = 7.4%. A is incorrect because it omits the risk-free rate in the estimation. E(R i ) = β i × [E(R M ) – R F ] = 0.8 × 8% = 6.4%. B is incorrect because it omits the risk-free rate in the estimation and uses the market return instead of the market risk premium. E(R i ) = β i × E(R M ) = 0.8 × 9% = 7.2%.

questions.stem: Which method of calculating the firm’s cost of equity is most likely to incorporate the long-run return relationship between the firm’s stock and the market portfolio?
questions.option_c: Bond yield plus risk premium approach
questions.explanation: A is correct. The capital asset pricing model uses the firm’s equity beta, which is computed from a market model regression of the company’s stock returns against market returns. B is incorrect. Dividend discount model estimates the equity risk premium by adding the dividend yield and the growth rate in dividends. C is incorrect. Cost of equity under this method is the additional of cost of debt and risk premium (the additional yield on a company’s stock relative to its bonds).

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in £ millions) about competitors' capital structures to help estimate a target capital structure for a subject company: The estimated target weight of debt for the subject company is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct because it calculates the averages of the competitor's debt weight as the target weight. {100/(100 + 400) + 200/(200 + 300) + 250/(250 + 250)}/3 = (0.2 + 0.4 + 0.5)/3 = 1.1/3 = .36667 ≈ 0.37. "[T]arget capital structure, if not disclosed...[can be estimated] using one of several methods: Use averages of comparable companies' capital structures as the target capital structure." B is incorrect because it calculates the sum of the debt divided by the sum of the equity as follows: (100 + 200 + 250)/(400 + 300 + 250) = 550/950 = 0..5789 ≈ 0.58. C is incorrect because it calculates the average of the competitors' D/E ratios as follows: (100/400 + 200/300 + 250/250)/3 = (0.25 + 0.67 + .1)/3 = 1.92/3 = 0.64.

questions.stem: In which of the following companies would the return profile of debtholders most likely be closest to that of shareholders?
questions.option_a: A manufacturing company in financial distress
questions.option_b: A start-up airline with significant growth prospects
questions.option_c: A telecom company with stable earnings and a net-debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 1.5
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[w]hen leverage and financial risk are high, the perspective of debtholders becomes more like that of equityholders. Normally, debt has low default risk and is priced to provide a modest yield to maturity. Return, or upside, is limited, unless the general level of interest rates declines. A holder of debt to maturity will be very focused on minimizing downside risk. However, with higher-risk debt and particularly with distressed debt, the potential upside can be substantial if the company does not default or if recoveries in default are higher than expected. In these circumstances, the return profile (and thus the perspective) of the debtholder becomes closer to that of an equity investor." B is incorrect because "for a holder of debt to maturity, the return, or upside, remains the face value of the debt plus the coupon." So unless the company runs into financial distress, upside is limited. Although "debt capital is typically not available or available only at a high cost" for start-ups, a start-up with fungible assets can support debt. "Some businesses use high levels of leverage regardless of their development stage. For example, in real estate, utilities, shipping, airlines, and certain other highly capital-intensive businesses, the underlying assets can be bought and sold fairly easily, tend to retain their value regardless of who owns them, and can therefore support substantial debt secured by those assets." C is incorrect because "[f]or a given level of debt, firms with low revenue, earnings, and cash flow volatility are likely to have a lower probability of default and be able to access debt at lower cost than firms with high volatility in these streams." Furthermore, "[a] common leverage ratio used by analysts to assess a firm’s debt capacity is the ratio of total (or net) debt to EBITDA. This ratio provides an estimate of how many years it would take to pay off the company’s debt. In general, ratio values of 3 or less are considered acceptable." Although a mature company with low leverage can support more debt, "for a holder of debt to maturity, the return, or upside, remains the face value of the debt plus the coupon."

questions.stem: The degree of operating leverage (DOL) is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. B is incorrect because it is Revenues/(Variable operating costs + Fixed operating costs). C is incorrect because it is (Revenues – Variable operating costs)/Fixed operating costs.

questions.stem: The use of financial leverage by an unprofitable company most likely increases:
questions.option_a: the level of return on equity only.
questions.option_b: the variability of return on equity only.
questions.option_c: both the level and variability of return on equity.
questions.explanation: B is correct because for an unprofitable company, financial leverage is more likely to both decrease the return on equity while also increasing the variability of this measure. "Using financial leverage generally increases the variability of return on equity (net income divided by shareholders' equity). In addition, its use by a profitable company may increase the level of return on equity." A is incorrect because the variability of return on equity is increased, but the level is more likely to be decreased as the company is unprofitable. "Using financial leverage generally increases the variability of return on equity (net income divided by shareholders' equity). In addition, its use by a profitable company may increase the level of return on equity." C is incorrect because the variability of return on equity is increased, but the level is more likely to be decreased as the company is unprofitable. "Using financial leverage generally increases the variability of return on equity (net income divided by shareholders' equity). In addition, its use by a profitable company may increase the level of return on equity."

questions.stem: All else being equal, an increase in the per unit contribution margin will decrease:
questions.option_c: both the breakeven point and the operating breakeven point.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "QBE [the breakeven point] = (F + C) / (P – V)...and "QOBE [the operating breakeven point] = F / (P – V)" where F = fixed operating costs; C = fixed financial costs; P = price per unit; and V = variable cost per unit. Also, "[t]he per unit contribution margin is the amount that each unit sold contributes to covering fixed costs—that is, the difference between the price per unit and the variable cost per unit." Hence the per unit contribution margin = P – V. It follows that if the per unit contribution margin increases, both the breakeven point and the operating breakeven point will decrease. A is incorrect because an increase in the per unit contribution margin decreases both the breakeven point and the operating breakeven point. "The per unit contribution margin is the amount that each unit sold contributes to covering fixed costs—that is, the difference between the price per unit and the variable cost per unit." Hence the per unit contribution margin = P – V. It follows that if the per unit contribution margin increases, both the breakeven point (F + C) / (P – V) and the operating breakeven point F / (P – V) will decrease. B is incorrect because an increase in the per unit contribution margin decreases both the breakeven point and the operating breakeven point. "The per unit contribution margin is the amount that each unit sold contributes to covering fixed costs—that is, the difference between the price per unit and the variable cost per unit." Hence the per unit contribution margin = P – V. It follows that if the per unit contribution margin increases, both the breakeven point (F + C) / (P – V) and the operating breakeven point F / (P – V) will decrease.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about endowments and foundations is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Most endowments and foundations have relatively short time horizons.
questions.option_b: Endowments typically allocate a sizable portion of their assets in alternative investments.
questions.option_c: Foundations are funds of non-profit institutions that help the institutions provide designated services.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[e]ndowments and foundations typically allocate a sizable portion of their assets in alternative investments." A is incorrect because "[m]ost foundations and endowments are established with the intent of having perpetual lives." C is incorrect because "foundations are grant-making entities" whilst "[e]ndowments are funds of non-profit institutions that help the institutions provide designated services."

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about mutual funds is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Open-end funds tend to be fully invested without keeping cash.
questions.option_b: Closed-end funds can sell for a premium or discount to net asset value.
questions.option_c: Investors in a closed-end fund liquidate by selling their shares back to the fund itself.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "closed-end funds can sell for a premium or discount to net asset value depending on the demand for the shares." A is incorrect because "open-end funds tend not to be fully invested but rather keep some cash for redemptions not covered by new investments." C is incorrect because for a "closed-end fund … investors in the fund liquidate by selling their shares to other investors," and not to the fund itself.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a two-asset portfolio and a third asset that is not part of the current portfolio: If the asset is added to the portfolio, the portfolio standard deviation will most likely:
questions.option_c: increase.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[t]he correlation coefficient between two assets determines the effect on portfolio risk when the two assets are combined. ... Portfolio risk falls ... when the two assets are not perfectly correlated (r12 < +1)." Since the correlation of returns between the asset and the portfolio is 0.5, portfolio risk will decrease with the addition of the new asset. B is incorrect because, although the standard deviations for the asset and the portfolio are equal, the correlation of returns between the asset and the portfolio is 0.5. "The correlation coefficient between two assets determines the effect on portfolio risk when the two assets are combined. ... Portfolio risk falls ... when the two assets are not perfectly correlated (r12 < +1)." C is incorrect because "[t]he correlation coefficient between two assets determines the effect on portfolio risk when the two assets are combined. ... Portfolio risk falls ... when the two assets are not perfectly correlated (r12 < +1)." Since the correlation of returns between the asset and the portfolio is 0.5, portfolio risk will decrease, not increase, with the addition of the new asset.

questions.stem: A correlation matrix of the returns for securities A, B, and C is reported below: Assuming that the expected return and the standard deviation of each security are the same, a portfolio consisting of an equal allocation of which two securities will be most effective for portfolio diversification?
questions.option_c: Securities A and B
questions.explanation: B is correct. The negative correlation of –0.5 between investment securities B and C is the lowest and thus is the most effective for portfolio diversification. A is incorrect. The positive correlation of 0.5 between investment securities A and C means that these instruments have positive correlation with each other and are not effective for portfolio diversification. C is incorrect. The neutral correlation of 0.0 between investment securities A and B means that these instruments have no correlation with each other. While portfolio A and B is superior to portfolio A and C, it is not superior to the negative correlation of portfolio B and C.

questions.stem: If the expected return on the market portfolio is 6% and the risk-free rate is 2%, the expected return of a security with a beta of 1.25 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. The capital asset pricing model posits that the expected return of a security is E(R i ) = R f + β i [E(R m ) – R f ] where Rf is the risk-free rate, Rm is the return on the market portfolio, and β is the beta of the security: 2% + 1.25 × (6% – 2%) = 7.00%. B is incorrect. It fails to add the risk-free rate: 1.25 × (6% – 2%) = 5.00%. C is incorrect. It fails to subtract the risk-free rate from the market portfolio’s expected return: 2% + 1.25 × (6%) = 9.50%.

questions.stem: A portfolio manager generated a rate of return of 15.5% on a portfolio with beta of 1.2. If the risk-free rate of return is 2.5% and the market return is 11.8%, Jensen’s alpha for the portfolio is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. Jensen’s alpha = R p – [R f + β p (R m – R f )] = 0.155 – [0.025 + 1.2 × (0.118 – 0.025)] = 0.0184 B is incorrect. Alpha is calculated as 0.155 – [1.2 × (0.118 – 0.025)] = 0.0434. C is incorrect. Alpha is calculated as 0.155 – [0.025 + (0.118 – 0.025)] = 0.037.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the direct result of combining long-term capital market expectations with the objectives and constraints of a client's IPS?
questions.option_a: The risk budget for the client's portfolio
questions.option_b: The strategic asset allocation portfolio for the client
questions.option_c: A tactical asset allocation decision for the client's portfolio
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[a] strategic asset allocation results from combining the constraints and objectives articulated in the IPS and long-term capital market expectations regarding the asset classes. The strategic asset allocation or policy portfolio will subsequently be implemented into real portfolios. Exhibit 7 illustrates conceptually how investment objectives and constraints and long-term capital market expectations combine into a policy portfolio." A is incorrect because the strategic asset allocation is the direct result of combining long-term capital market expectations with the IPS objectives and constraints. The strategic asset allocation decision is separate from the risk budgeting process. "[R]isk budgeting is the process of deciding on the amount of risk to assume in a portfolio (the overall risk budget) and subdividing that risk over the sources of investment return (e.g., strategic asset allocation, tactical asset allocation, and security selection). Because the decision about the total amount of risk to be taken is made in constructing the IPS, at this stage we are concerned about the subdivision of that risk." C is incorrect because "[t]actical asset allocation is the decision to deliberately deviate from the policy exposures to systematic risk factors (i.e., the policy weights of asset classes) with the intent to add value based on forecasts of the near-term returns of those asset classes. For instance, an investor may decide to temporarily invest more of the portfolio in equities than the SAA prescribes if the investor anticipates that equities will deliver a higher return over the short term than other asset classes." Combining long-term capital market expectations with the objectives and constraints of an IPS directly results in the strategic asset allocation, which precludes the tactical asset allocation decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following behavioral biases most likely helps explain the momentum market anomaly?
questions.option_c: Anchoring and adjustment bias
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[m]omentum can be partly explained by availability, hindsight, and loss aversion biases. Studies have identified faulty learning models within traders, in which reasoning is based on their recent experience. Behaviorally, this is availability bias." A is incorrect because "[s]tatus quo bias is an emotional bias in which people choose to do nothing (i.e., maintain the 'status quo') instead of making a change, even when change is warranted." While this could be incorrectly interpreted as maintaining a trend in a price, it does not explain the momentum anomaly. "Momentum can be partly explained by availability, hindsight, and loss aversion biases." C is incorrect because "[a]nchoring and adjustment bias refers to relying on an initial piece of information to make subsequent estimates, judgments, and decisions." While the current market price may act as an anchor, it does not explain the observed momentum anomaly. "Momentum can be partly explained by availability, hindsight, and loss aversion biases."

questions.stem: Which of the following risk metrics is best used to estimate extreme losses?
questions.option_c: Conditional VaR
questions.explanation: C is correct because "VaR does not tell the maximum loss. The maximum loss is the entire equity of an organization or the entire value of a portfolio, but the statistics used to estimate VaR can be used to gauge average extreme losses. Conditional VaR or CVaR is a common tail loss measure, defined as the weighted average of all loss outcomes in the statistical distribution that exceed the VaR loss." A is incorrect because "[d]erivatives are also sensitive to changes in interest rates, which are reflected in a measure called rho. Most options have relatively low sensitivity to interest rates." B is incorrect because "[t]he sensitivity of the derivative price to a small change in the value of the underlying asset is called the delta. It is perhaps the most important measure of derivatives risk. Yet delta is limited to capturing only small changes in the value of the underlying."

questions.stem: According to technical analysis, after completing an inverse head and shoulders pattern, a stock price will most likely trend:
questions.option_c: downward.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[a]s the name implies, a reversal pattern signals the end of a trend, a change in direction for the financial instrument’s price. … Perhaps the most widely recognized reversal pattern is the head and shoulders pattern." "The head and shoulders pattern can also form upside down and act as a reversal pattern for a preceding downtrend." Since an inverse head and shoulders pattern indicates the previous price pattern was a downtrend, the stock price is expected to trend upward. B is incorrect because an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern acts as a reversal pattern for a preceding clearly defined downturn. The stock price is expected to move higher following an inverse head and shoulders pattern. C is incorrect because an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern acts as a reversal pattern for a preceding clearly defined downturn. The stock price is expected to move higher following an inverse head and shoulders pattern.

questions.stem: Which of the following inputs from a technical analyst is most likely assumed to add value for a portfolio manager? The technical analyst:
questions.option_a: making a decision on position sizing
questions.option_b: advising on the timing of the purchase or sale of a security
questions.option_c: conducting interviews with customers of a target company to assess demand for its products
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[a] technical analyst can serve a supporting role in a team of investors. ...the technical analyst goes through the opportunity set and provides trade and investment ideas to the portfolio/fund managers. The key value-added input would be in the form of timing of the purchase or sale of that security. " A is incorrect because "[t]he technical analyst will typically not be directly involved in position sizing decisions, such as how much of the portfolio to allocate to a certain idea or by what margin the fund should overweight or underweight the specific stock. However, the portfolio manager may well use high-conviction inputs from the technical analyst in weighting decisions." C is incorrect because although conducting interviews can add value to analysis of the company, this is not part of the technical analysis. "[T]echnicians are limited to studying market movements and do not use other predictive analytical methods, such as interviewing the customers of a subject company to determine future demand for a company’s products."

questions.stem: With respect to fintech applications, the instantaneous transfer of collateral in the event of default is an example of:
questions.option_c: high-frequency trading.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "DLT has the potential to accommodate 'smart contracts,' which are computer programs that self-execute on the basis of pre-specified terms and conditions agreed to by the parties to a contract. Examples of smart contract use are the automatic execution of contingent claims for derivatives and the instantaneous transfer of collateral in the event of default." A is incorrect because tokenization refers to "the process of representing ownership rights to physical assets on a blockchain or distributed ledger." C is incorrect because "[h]igh-frequency trading (HFT) is a form of algorithmic trading that makes use of vast quantities of granular financial data (tick data, for example) to automatically place trades when certain conditions are met."

questions.stem: Short sellers most likely:
questions.option_a: pay a short rebate to security lenders.
questions.option_b: receive cash collateral from security lenders.
questions.option_c: make payments-in-lieu of dividends to security lenders.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "the short sellers will pay the long sellers [security lenders] all dividends or interest that they otherwise would have received had they not lent their securities. These payments are called payments-in-lieu of dividends (or of interest)." A is incorrect because security lenders will pay a short rebate rate to short sellers. "They [security lenders] invest the collateral in short-term securities, and they rebate the interest to the short sellers at rates called short rebate rates." B is incorrect because short seller will deposit cash collateral to security lenders. "To secure the security loans, lenders require that the short seller leave the proceeds of the short sale on deposit with them as collateral [cash collateral] for the stock loan."

questions.stem: An investor buys a stock on margin and holds the position for one year. Assuming that the interest on the loan and the dividend are both paid at the end of the year, the price at which the investor sold the stock is closest to:
questions.explanation: C is correct. A is incorrect because it ignores the margin interest. B is incorrect because it ignores the dividend amount.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely associated with secondary capital markets?
questions.option_c: Book building
questions.explanation: A is correct. A secondary market is where investors continue to trade the securities among themselves. Continuous trading is typically associated with secondary capital markets. B is incorrect. Lead underwriter is associated with primary markets. C is incorrect. Book building is associated with primary markets.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements concerning financial regulatory bodies is least accurate? Financial regulatory bodies:
questions.option_a: act to level the playing field for market participants.
questions.option_b: define minimum standards of competence for agents.
questions.option_c: require that regulated firms maintain optimum levels of capital.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Financial regulators impose minimum levels of capital that apply across the board to all regulated firms—not the optimum level, which is firm specific. A is incorrect. Financial regulators act to level the playing field for market participants as in the case of regulation concerning insider trading. B is incorrect. Financial regulators help define minimum standards of competence for agents (e.g., the GIPS standards from CFA Institute).

questions.stem: The data for two stocks in an index are as follows: Assuming the beginning value of the float-adjusted market-capitalization-weighted equity index is 100, the ending value is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. In float-adjusted market-capitalization weighting, the weight on each constituent security is determined by adjusting its market capitalization for its market float. As the following computations show, the ending value of the index equals 102.06 (322,500/316,000). B is incorrect. It does make adjustment for the market float but makes the mistake of including dividends in the ending price of the stock. C is incorrect. It ignores the float and simply computes the index on the basis of market-capitalization weighting.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding rebalancing and reconstitution of an index is most accurate?
questions.option_b: Reconstitution can dramatically affect prices of both current and prospective constituents.
questions.option_c: Reconstitution is part of index management that reduces the need for rebalancing.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Reconstitution is the process in which index providers review whether securities are retained, removed, or added. Prior to the index’s reconstitution date, portfolio managers buy stocks they think will be added to an index and sell stocks they think will be deleted from the index, thus dramatically altering the prices of the affected stocks. A is incorrect because market-capitalization-weighted indexes largely rebalance themselves. An equal-weighted index is one that needs frequent rebalancing. C is incorrect because reconstitution and rebalancing are both part of index management and create turnover of an index. Besides, reconstitution is a part of the rebalancing cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding indexes for alternative investments is most accurate?
questions.option_a: Commodity index returns are based on changes in the prices of the underlying commodities.
questions.option_b: Commodity indexes consist of a market-weighted basket of one or more specific commodities.
questions.option_c: Hedge funds determine whether their results will be included in an index.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Hedge fund companies are not required to report their performance to any party other than their investors. As a result, rather than index providers determining the constituents, the constituents determine the index. A is incorrect. Commodity indexes are based upon futures contracts, not prices of the underlying commodities themselves. B is incorrect. Commodity indexes consist of futures contracts. There is no market weighting mechanism.

questions.stem: Which of the following situations will most likely indicate a reduction of market efficiency?
questions.option_a: An increase in rules and regulations that promote financial disclosure
questions.option_c: An increase in the number of market participants
questions.explanation: B is correct. Arbitrage is a set of transactions that produces riskless profits. Arbitrageurs are traders who engage in such trades to benefit from pricing discrepancies (inefficiencies) in markets. Such trading activity contributes to market efficiency. If arbitrage opportunities increase, it means that there are either more pricing discrepancies or fewer arbitrageurs (or both), than before indicating that there has been a reduction of market efficiency. A is incorrect. An increase of rules and regulations that promote financial disclosure will lead to an increase of market efficiency. C is incorrect. An increase of the number of market participants will lead to an increase market efficiency.

questions.stem: A consequence of preventing the exploitation of private information is that the market is not:
questions.option_c: strong-form efficient.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[s]ecurities markets are not strong-form efficient because securities laws are intended to prevent exploitation of private information." A is incorrect because "[i]n the weak-form efficient market hypothesis, security prices fully reflect all past market data, which refers to all historical price and trading volume information." Putting into place securities laws that are preventing the exploitation of private information does not affect the market's capability to reflect past market data. B is incorrect because in a "semi-strong-form efficient market, prices reflect all publicly known and available information". Putting into place securities laws that are preventing the exploitation of private information does not affect the market's capability to reflect public information.

questions.stem: An informed trader buys a company’s stock. His close friends, who lack information or expertise, imitate his action and buy the stock. Which of the following statements concerning this behavioral bias is most accurate?
questions.option_c: It is inconsistent with rational behavior.
questions.explanation: B is correct. This behavioral bias is an example of an information cascade wherein the transmission of information is from those participants who act first and whose decisions influence the decisions of others. The behavior of informed traders acting first and uninformed traders imitating the informed traders is consistent with rationality. The imitation trading by the uninformed traders helps the market incorporate relevant information and improves market efficiency. A is incorrect. Representativeness is a behavioral bias wherein investors assess probabilities of outcomes depending on how similar they are to the current state. C is incorrect. The behavior of informed traders acting first and uninformed traders imitating the informed traders is consistent with rationality.

questions.stem: Sponsored depository receipts most likely differ from unsponsored ones in terms of whether:
questions.option_c: their prices are affected by exchange rate movements.
questions.explanation: A is correct because a sponsored DR is when the foreign company whose shares are held by the depository has a direct involvement in the issuance of the receipts. Investors in sponsored DRs have the same rights as the direct owners of the common shares (e.g., the right to vote and the right to receive dividends). In contrast, with an unsponsored DR, the underlying foreign company has no involvement with the issuance of the receipts. Instead, the depository purchases the foreign company’s shares in its domestic market and then issues the receipts through brokerage firms in the depository’s local market. In this case, the depository bank, not the investors in the DR, retains the voting rights. B is incorrect because a depository receipt (DR) [sponsored or unsponsored] is a security that trades like an ordinary share on a local exchange and represents an economic interest in a foreign company. C is incorrect because a depository receipt (DR) [sponsored or unsponsored] is a security that trades like an ordinary share on a local exchange and represents an economic interest in a foreign company. The price of each DR will be affected by factors that affect the price of the underlying shares, such as company fundamentals, market conditions, analysts’ recommendations, and exchange rate movements.

questions.stem: The minimum rate of return required by investors to purchase an equity security is most likely approximated by the company's:
questions.option_c: weighted average cost of capital.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "the company’s cost of equity is often used as a proxy for the investors’ minimum required rate of return." B is incorrect because "[w]hen investors purchase the company’s equity securities, their minimum required rate of return is based on the future cash flows they expect to receive." Return on equity is a historical accounting measure which measures the total return on the firm's book value, therefore it may or may not approximate investors' minimum required rate of return. C is incorrect because "[t]he WACC represents the minimum required rate of return that the company must earn on its long-term investments to satisfy all providers of capital," i.e. both debt holders and equity investors not just equity investors.

questions.stem: Suppliers most likely have strong pricing power when:
questions.option_c: there are a few concentrated buyers of their output.
questions.explanation: A is correct because supplier bargaining power is affected by "switching costs of suppliers’ customers." If customers face high switching costs then suppliers can exercise more pricing power. B is incorrect because supplier power would be reduced by "the availability of (alternative) product categories that can satisfy customer needs." C is incorrect because if suppliers face only a few large customers, they are "able to force price reductions or better payment terms."

questions.stem: An industry characterized by rapidly increasing demand, improving profitability, and falling prices is most likely in which of the following stages of life cycle?
questions.option_c: Embryonic
questions.explanation: A is correct. A growth industry tends to be characterized by rapidly increasing demand, improving profitability, falling prices, and relativity low competition among companies in the industry. B is incorrect. During the maturity stage, industry growth tends to be limited to replacement demand and population expansion because the market at this stage is completely saturated. C is incorrect. During the embryonic stage, demand growth is slow because customers tend to be unfamiliar with the industry’s product and volumes are not yet sufficient to achieve meaningful economic of scale.

questions.stem: The oil services industry is most likely characterized by:
questions.option_c: market share stability.
questions.explanation: A is correct because the oil services industry is "fragmented." "Although only a small number of companies provide a full range of services, many smaller players compete effectively in specific areas. Service arms of national oil companies may control significant market share in their own countries, and some product lines are concentrated in the mature US market." B is incorrect because the barriers to entry is "medium" in the oil services industry. "Technological expertise is required, but a high level of innovation allows niche companies to enter the industry and compete in specific areas." C is incorrect because in the oil services industry "[m]arket shares may shift frequently depending on technology offerings and demand levels."

questions.stem: The first date a buyer of shares is not entitled to an announced dividend is the:
questions.option_c: holder-of-record date.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[b]ecause buyers of a company’s shares on the ex-dividend date are no longer eligible to receive the upcoming dividend, all else being equal, on that day the company’s share price immediately decreases by the amount of the foregone dividend." A is incorrect because "[f]irst is the declaration date, the day that the company issues a statement declaring a specific dividend. Next comes the ex-dividend date (or exdate), the first date that a share trades without (i.e., “ex”) the dividend." C is incorrect because "buyers of a company’s shares on the ex-dividend date are no longer eligible to receive the upcoming dividend, all else being equal, on that day the company’s share price immediately decreases by the amount of the foregone dividend.This is followed by "the holder-of-record date (also called the owner-of-record date, shareholder-of-record date, record date, date of record, or date of book closure), the date that a shareholder listed on the company’s books will be deemed to have ownership of the shares for purposes of receiving the upcoming dividend."

questions.stem: An investor gathers the following information about a company: If the investors’ required rate of return is 15%, the current estimate of the intrinsic value per share is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct. A is incorrect. It uses the historical growth rate and the constant growth model for estimating the intrinsic value. C is incorrect. It uses the historical growth rate rather than an analyst’s growth forecast.

questions.stem: The Gordon growth model is most appropriate for valuing the common stock of a dividend paying company that is:
questions.option_a: mature and relatively insensitive to economic fluctuations.
questions.option_b: young and just entering the growth phase.
questions.option_c: experiencing growth that is higher than the sustainable growth rate.
questions.explanation: A is correct. The Gordon growth model is most appropriate for valuing common stock of a dividend paying company that is mature and relatively insensitive to the business cycle or economic fluctuations. B is incorrect. A three-stage dividend discount model would be most appropriate for a fairly young company that is just entering the growth phase. C is incorrect. A two-stage dividend discount model would be appropriate for a company that is experiencing a higher than the sustainable growth rate.

questions.stem: Price multiples allow for:
questions.option_c: both time series and cross-sectional comparisons.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "the major advantage of using price multiples is that they allow for relative comparisons, both cross-sectional (versus the market or another comparable) and in time series." A is incorrect because "the major advantage of using price multiples is that they allow for relative comparisons, both cross-sectional (versus the market or another comparable) and in time series." B is incorrect because "the major advantage of using price multiples is that they allow for relative comparisons, both cross-sectional (versus the market or another comparable) and in time series."

questions.stem: Which of the following valuation models does not require the estimation of required rate of return on a share?
questions.option_c: A free-cash-flow-to-equity model
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[t]he term price multiple refers to a ratio that compares the share price with some sort of monetary flow or value to allow evaluation of the relative worth of a company’s stock." Discounting and the estimation of required rate of return are not needed in price multiple model. B is incorrect because the Gordon growth model requires the estimation of required rate of return (r) on equity. "Gordon growth model as presented: V o = D 1 / r – g." C is incorrect because the "[v]aluation obtained by using FCFE involves discounting expected future FCFE by the required rate of return on equity; the expression parallels Equation 1: V o = FCFE t /(1+r) t ."

questions.stem: Bonds issued in the Eurobond market are most likely:
questions.option_b: in the form of registered bonds.
questions.option_c: issued within the jurisdiction of the issuer's home country.
questions.explanation: B is correct because Eurobonds, domestic, and foreign bonds are now registered bonds for which ownership is recorded by either name or serial number. A is incorrect because bonds issued and traded on the Eurobond market are called Eurobonds, and they are named after the currency in which they are denominated. For example, Eurodollar and Euroyen bonds are denominated in US dollars and Japanese yens, respectively. Bonds that are denominated in euros are called euro-denominated Eurobonds. C is incorrect because Eurobonds are issued outside the jurisdiction of any single country, are usually unsecured, and may be denominated in any currency, including the issuer’s domestic currency.

questions.stem: Which of the following contingency provisions in a bond most likely benefits the issuer?
questions.option_c: Call provision
questions.explanation: C is correct. A call provision gives the issuer the right to redeem all or part of the bond before the specified maturity date to protect the issuer against a decline in interest rates. Therefore, it benefits the issuer and provides a lower future funding cost. A is incorrect because a put provision gives the bondholders (the borrower) the right to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-determined price on specified dates in the event of interest rates rise. B is incorrect because a conversion provision gives the bondholder (the borrower) the right to exchange the bond for a specified number of common shares in the issuing company in case of share price appreciation.

questions.stem: Which of the following US sovereign securities is a pure discount bond?
questions.option_c: Treasury bond
questions.explanation: A is correct because "T-bills are pure discount bonds; they are issued at a discount to par value and redeemed at par.” B is incorrect because Treasury bills are money market securities, while Treasury notes and Treasury bonds are capital market securities. …T-bills are pure discount bonds; they are issued at a discount to par value and redeemed at par. … In contrast, capital market securities are typically coupon (or coupon- bearing) bonds; these securities make regular coupon payments and repay the par value at maturity.” C is incorrect because Treasury bills are money market securities, while Treasury notes and Treasury bonds are capital market securities. … capital market securities are typically coupon (or coupon-bearing) bonds; these securities make regular coupon payments and repay the par value at maturity.”

questions.stem: Which of the following factors will most likely drive the repo margin lower?
questions.option_c: Lower credit quality of the counterparty
questions.explanation: B is correct. If the collateral is in short supply or if there is a high demand for it, repo margins are lower. Repo margin is the difference between the market value of the security used as collateral and the value of the loan. A is incorrect because the lower the quality of the collateral, the higher the repo margin. C is incorrect because the lower the creditworthiness of the counterparty, the higher the repo margin.

questions.stem: Given two otherwise identical bonds, when interest rates rise, the price of Bond A declines more than the price of Bond B. Compared with Bond B, Bond A most likely:
questions.option_c: has a lower coupon.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The lower the coupon rate, the more sensitive the bond’s price is to changes in interest rates. A is incorrect because the maturity would have to be longer for Bond A relative to Bond B. B is incorrect because when interest rates rise, the price of a callable bond will not fall as much as an otherwise option-free bond.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about spot rates: Given this information, the price of a three-year bond with a 4% coupon is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct because the "formula for calculating a bond price given the sequence of spot rates: PV= PMT/(1+Z 1 ) 1 + PMT/(1+Z 2 ) 2 + (PMT+FV)/(1+Z N ) N where Z 1 = spot rate...for Period 1, Z 2 = spot rate...for Period 2, Z N = spot rate...for Period N" Price = 4/(1.01) 1 + 4/(1.03) 2 + 104/(1.04) 3 = 3.96 + 3.77 + 92.46 ≈ 100.19 B is incorrect because the "formula for calculating a bond price given the sequence of spot rates: PV= PMT/(1+Z 1 ) 1 + PMT/(1+Z 2 ) 2 + (PMT-+FV)/(1+Z N ) N where Z 1 = spot rate...for Period 1, Z 2 = spot rate...for Period 2, Z N = spot rate...for Period N" This solution uses the sum of all payments as the numerator and the average spot rate in the denominator. Price = 112/(1.0267) 3 = 103.49 ≈ 103.5. C is incorrect because the "formula for calculating a bond price given the sequence of spot rates: PV= PMT/(1+Z 1 ) 1 + PMT/(1+Z 2 ) 2 + (PMT-+FV)/(1+Z N ) N where Z 1 = spot rate...for Period 1, Z 2 = spot rate...for Period 2, Z N = spot rate...for Period N" This solution fails to square and cube the denominator. Price = 4/(1.01) 1 + 4/(1.03) + 104/(1.04) = 3.96 + 3.88 + 100 ≈ 107.84 ≈ 107.8.

questions.stem: The sum of the coupon payments over a year divided by the flat price of a bond is best defined as:
questions.option_c: current yield.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[a]nother yield measure that is commonly quoted for fixed-income bonds is the current yield, also called the income or running yield. The current yield is the sum of the coupon payments received over the year divided by the flat price. A is incorrect because "[t]he true yield-to-maturity is the internal rate of return on the cash flows using the actual calendar of weekends and bank holidays." True yield incorporates a bond's premium and discount to maturity unlike current yield. B is incorrect because "the simple yield on a bond...is the sum of the coupon payments plus the straight-line amortized share of the gain or loss, divided by the flat price." The simple yield incorporates the premium and discount to maturity unlike current yield.

questions.stem: A 90-day commercial paper issue is quoted at a discount rate of 4.75% for a 360-day year. The bond equivalent yield for this instrument is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. The price of the commercial paper per 100 of par value is where PV and FV are the price and face value of the money market instrument, Days is the number of days between settlement and maturity, Year is number of days in the year, and DR is the discount rate stated as an annual percentage. The bond equivalent yield is B is incorrect because the price of the commercial paper is incorrectly computed as The bond equivalent yield is computed as C is incorrect because it is just the discount rate itself.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about US bonds: Assuming annual interest payments, the G-spread is closest to:
questions.option_c: 300 basis points.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[t]he yield spread in basis points over an actual or interpolated government bond is known as the G- spread." Using the data provided, the yield for the US Government Bond is found by 101 = 2 / (1 + r) + 102 / (1 + r) 2 . r = 1.49%. While the yield on the corporate bond is 103 = 5 / (1 + r) + 105 / (1 + r) 2 . r = 3.42%. G-spread = 3.42 - 1.49 = 1.93 or 193 basis points. A is incorrect because "[t]he yield spread in basis points over an actual or interpolated government bond is known as the G-spread." This answer is only the yield of the US government bond Corporate Bond.& 101 = 2 / (1 + r) + 102 / (1 + r) 2 . r = 1.498% or 149 basis points. C is incorrect because "[t]he yield spread in basis points over an actual or interpolated government bond is known as the G-spread." This answer incorrectly uses the difference between the coupon rates 5.00 – 2.00 = 3.00 or 300 basis points.

questions.stem: Key rate duration:
questions.option_a: requires the shape of the benchmark yield curve to stay constant.
questions.option_b: measures a bond's sensitivity to a change in the benchmark yield at a specific maturity.
questions.option_c: indicates the same interest rate sensitivity as effective duration for non-parallel shifts in the yield curve.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[a] key rate duration (or partial duration) is a measure of a bond’s sensitivity to a change in the benchmark yield at a specific maturity." A is incorrect because key rate duration assumes non-parallel shifts in the benchmark yield curve. “'Key rate' duration provides…insight into a bond’s sensitivity to non-parallel benchmark yield curve changes.” C is incorrect because effective and key rate durations indicate the same sensitivity to interest rate changes when all yields change by the same amount. "[E]ffective duration measures a bond’s sensitivity to changes in the benchmark yield curve if all yields change by the same amount. Key rate duration provides further insight into a bond’s sensitivity to non-parallel benchmark yield curve changes. Key rate duration (or partial duration) is a measure of a bond’s sensitivity to a change in the benchmark yield at a specific maturity... Key rate durations define a security’s price sensitivity over a set of maturities along the yield curve, with the sum of key rate durations being equal to the effective duration [when yields are shifted by the same amount]".

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information for a portfolio of annual pay bonds: The average (annual) modified duration of the portfolio is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. The average (annual) modified duration of the portfolio is 5.19. B is incorrect. It is the result of erroneously weighting the average modified duration using par, rather than market values. C is incorrect. It is the result of taking the weighted average of Macaulay Duration, rather than modified duration for the three bonds.

questions.stem: The option-free bonds issued by ALS Corp. are currently priced at 108.50. Based on a portfolio manager’s valuation model, a 1 bp increase in interest rates will result in the bond price falling to 108.40, whereas a 1 bp decrease in interest rates will result in the bond price rising to 108.59. The price value of a basis point (PVBP) for the bonds is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. The bond’s PVBP is computed using B is incorrect because the PVBP is calculated using the incorrect formula: C is incorrect because the PVBP is calculated by omitting the 2 in the denominator: 108.59 – 108.40 = 0.190

questions.stem: A bond has an annual modified duration of 2.741, an annual convexity of 22.638, and is currently yielding 5.0%. If the bond’s yield-to-maturity decreases to 4.2%, the expected percentage price change is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct because the expected price change is: %ΔPVFull ≈ (–AnnModDuration x ΔYield) + [1/2 x AnnConvexity x (ΔYield)2] = (–2.741 x –0.008) + [1/2 x 22.638 x (–0.008) 2 ] = 0.02265 ≈ 2.27%. A is incorrect because the expected price change is: %ΔPVFull ≈ (–AnnModDuration x ΔYield) + [1/2 x AnnConvexity x (-ΔYield) 2 ]. This answer fails to include a negative sign in front of the change in yield in the first term to reflect a decrease in yield: (–2.741 x 0.008) + [1/2 x 22.638 x (0.008) 2 ] = –0.021204 ≈ –2.12%. C is incorrect because the expected price change is: %ΔPVFull ≈ (–AnnModDuration x ΔYield) + [1/2 x AnnConvexity x (ΔYield) 2 ]. This answer fails to multiply the second term by 1/2: (–2.741 x –0.008) + [22.638 x (–0.008) 2 ] = 0.02338 ≈ = 2.34%.

questions.stem: The price of a fixed-rate corporate bond with an annual modified duration of 6.32 increases from 90 to 95 per 100 of par value. If the government benchmark yield declines by 5 bps, the estimated decline in the spread over the benchmark yield is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct because given that the price increases to 95 from 90, the percentage price increase is (95 – 90)/(90) ≈ 0.05556. Using %ΔPV Full ≈ –AnnModDur × ΔYield, the change in the yield-to-maturity can be calculated as 0.05556 = –6.32 × ΔYield ⇒ ΔYield = –0.05556/6.32 ≈ –0.00879, i.e. a decrease of 0.00879. Given that "the yield-to-maturity on a corporate bond is composed of a government benchmark yield and a spread over that benchmark," the decline in the government benchmark yield by 5 bps implies that the change in the spread over the benchmark yield is 0.00879 – 0.0005 = 0.00829, i.e. 82.9 bps, so that on a combined basis the decline in the yield-to-maturity is 0.0005 + 0.00829 = 0.00879. B is incorrect because it correctly calculates the decline in the yield-to-maturity of 0.00879 but omits to incorporate the effect of the government benchmark yield decrease, which means the decline in the spread over the benchmark yield is less than 87.9 bps, to have a total decrease in the yield-to-maturity of 87.9 bps. C is incorrect because it correctly calculates the decline in the yield-to-maturity of 0.00879 but instead of subtracting the decline in the benchmark yield to calculate the decline in the spread, it adds it back, i.e. 0.00879 + 0.0005 = 0.00929.

questions.stem: Compared to the support tranche of a collateralized mortgage obligation, the planned amortization class tranche most likely:
questions.option_b: offers a greater level of protection against prepayment risk.
questions.option_c: absorbs principal repayments in excess of the repayment schedule.
questions.explanation: B is correct because “[s]upport tranches expose investors to the highest level of prepayment risk.” A is incorrect because “there is much less variability for the average life of the PAC tranche compared with that of the support tranche.” C is incorrect because “the support tranches absorb any principal repayments in excess of the scheduled principal repayments.”

questions.stem: With respect to a collateralized debt obligation, any return in excess of what is paid out to the bond classes accrues to:
questions.option_b: the holders of the equity tranche only.
questions.option_c: both the collateral manager and the holders of the equity tranche.
questions.explanation: C is correct because “the CDO manager seeks to earn a rate of return higher than the aggregate cost of the bond classes. The return in excess of what is paid out to the bond classes accrues to the holders of the equity tranche and to the CDO manager.” A is incorrect because “the CDO manager seeks to earn a rate of return higher than the aggregate cost of the bond classes. The return in excess of what is paid out to the bond classes accrues to the holders of the equity tranche and to the CDO manager.” B is incorrect because “the CDO manager seeks to earn a rate of return higher than the aggregate cost of the bond classes. The return in excess of what is paid out to the bond classes accrues to the holders of the equity tranche and to the CDO manager.”

questions.stem: Credit ratings:
questions.option_b: reflect changes in creditworthiness before the markets do.
questions.option_c: have proved quite accurate as an absolute measure of default risk.
questions.explanation: A is correct because"Rating agencies incorporate ESG factors into their ratings of firms. Some have launched a set of ratings that aim to measure a company’s attitudes, practices, and advances related to ESG. They identify and track leaders and laggards in the space. Companies are evaluated according to their exposure to ESG risks and how well they manage those risks relative to peers." B is incorrect because "[c]redit ratings tend to lag the market’s pricing of credit risk. Bond prices and credit spreads frequently move more quickly because of changes in perceived creditworthiness than rating agencies change their ratings (or even outlooks) up or down." C is incorrect because rating agencies' "ratings have proved quite accurate as a relative measure of default risk," not an absolute measure of default risk.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company (in $ thousands): Based on the interest coverage ratio using EBITDA, the company's creditworthiness has:
questions.option_c: improved.
questions.explanation: C is correct because over the period the interest coverage ratio increased, which indicates that the company is better positioned to service its debt. "A higher ratio indicates higher credit quality." Interest coverage ratio is calculated as EBITDA/Interest expense and EBITDA = Operating income + Depreciation and amortization, hence the ratios are: Year 1: EBITDA: 255 + 432 = 687 ⇒ Interest coverage: 687/170 = 4.04 ≈ 4.0x; Year 2: EBITDA: 234 + 677 = 911 ⇒ Interest coverage: 911/156 = 5.84 ≈ 5.8x. A is incorrect because over the period the interest coverage ratio increased and "[a] higher ratio indicates higher [not lower] credit quality."
