questions.explanation: B is correct because according to Standard VII (B), Reference to The CFA Institute, The CFA Designation, and The CFA Program, "CFA Program candidates must never state or imply that they have a partial designation as a result of passing one or more levels or cite an expected completion date of any level of the CFA Program. Final award of the charter is subject to meeting the CFA Program requirements and approval by the CFA Institute Board of Governors." Therefore, she has violated the Standard by stating partial designation. A is incorrect because according to Standard VII (B), Reference to The CFA Institute, The CFA Designation, and The CFA Program, "CFA Program candidates must never state or imply that they have a partial designation as a result of passing one or more levels or cite an expected completion date of any level of the CFA Program. Final award of the charter is subject to meeting the CFA Program requirements and approval by the CFA Institute Board of Governors." Therefore, she has violated the Standard by stating partial designation. C is incorrect because according to Standard VII (B), Reference to The CFA Institute, The CFA Designation, and The CFA Program, this is not a violation. "If a candidate passes each level of the exam in consecutive years and wants to state that he or she did so, that is not a violation of Standard VII(B) because it is a statement of fact. If the candidate then goes on to claim or imply superior ability by obtaining the designation in only three years, however, he or she is in violation of Standard VII(B)."

questions.stem: Are both of the following statements consistent with the Standard relating to preservation of confidentiality?
questions.option_b: No, Statement 1 is not consistent with the Standard.
questions.option_c: No, Statement 2 is not consistent with the Standard.
questions.explanation: A is correct because according to Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality “[w]hen permissible under applicable law, members and candidates shall consider the PCP an extension of themselves when requested to provide information about a client in support of a PCP investigation into their own conduct. Members and candidates are encouraged to cooperate with investigations into the conduct of others.” So, Statement 1 is consistent with the Standard. Also, according to Standard III(E), "members and candidates must continue to maintain the confidentiality of client records even after the client relationship has ended.” So, Statement 2 is also consistent with the Standard. B is incorrect because according to Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality “[w]hen permissible under applicable law, members and candidates shall consider the PCP an extension of themselves when requested to provide information about a client in support of a PCP investigation into their own conduct. Members and candidates are encouraged to cooperate with investigations into the conduct of others.” So, Statement 1 is consistent with the Standard. C is incorrect because according to Standard III(E), Preservation of Confidentiality, "members and candidates must continue to maintain the confidentiality of client records even after the client relationship has ended.” So, Statement 2 is consistent with the Standard.

questions.stem: According to the Code and Standards regarding knowledge of laws and regulations, CFA Institute members and candidates must:
questions.option_a: understand the relevant regulations for all the countries where they trade securities.
questions.option_b: have detailed knowledge of all the laws that could potentially govern the member’s activities.
questions.option_c: spend a minimum of five hours per calendar year on continuing education activities related to applicable laws and regulations.
questions.explanation: A is correct because Standard I(A) requires members and candidates to understand applicable laws and regulations in those countries where they trade or conduct business. While an understanding of laws and regulations is required, members and candidates can rely on legal counsel and compliance to be subject matter experts in these areas. The Standards do not require a minimum of five hours of continuing education. B is incorrect because Standard I(A) does require members and candidates to become legal experts. While an understanding of laws and regulations is required, members and candidates can rely on legal counsel and compliance to be subject matter experts in these areas. C is incorrect because members and candidates do not have such a requirement.

questions.stem: Members should encourage their firms to establish which of the following procedures to avoid violations of Standard relating to independence and objectivity?
questions.option_c: Both Procedure 1 and Procedure 2
questions.explanation: C is correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard I(B), Independence and Objectivity, "[i]f the firm is unwilling to permit dissemination of adverse opinions about a corporate client, members and candidates should encourage the firm to remove the controversial company from the research universe and put it on a restricted list so that the firm disseminates only factual information about the company." Therefore, Procedure 1 is correct. In addition, according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard I(B), Independence and Objectivity, "[w]hen attending meetings at an issuer’s headquarters, members and candidates should pay for commercial transportation and hotel charges. No corporate issuer should reimburse members or candidates for air transportation." Employees should not receive reimbursement from issuers even the meetings are held at the issuer's headquarters. Therefore, Procedure 2 is correct. A is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard I(B), Independence and Objectivity, "[w]hen attending meetings at an issuer’s headquarters, members and candidates should pay for commercial transportation and hotel charges. No corporate issuer should reimburse members or candidates for air transportation." Employees should not receive reimbursement from issuers even the meetings are held at the issuer's headquarters. Therefore, Procedure 2 is also correct. B is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard I(B), Independence and Objectivity, "[i]f the firm is unwilling to permit dissemination of adverse opinions about a corporate client, members and candidates should encourage the firm to remove the controversial company from the research universe and put it on a restricted list so that the firm disseminates only factual information about the company." Therefore, Procedure 1 is also correct.

questions.stem: Diana Fairbanks, CFA, is married to an auditor who is employed at a large accounting firm. When her husband mentions that a computer firm he audits will receive a qualified opinion she thinks nothing of it. Later that week when she reviews a new client account she notices that there are substantial holdings of this computer firm. When she does a thorough internet search for news on the company, she does not find anything about its most recent audit or any other adverse information. Which of the following actions concerning the computer stock should Fairbanks most likely take to avoid violating the CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct?
questions.option_b: Complete a thorough and diligent analysis of the company and then sell the stock
questions.option_c: Sell the stock immediately as she has a reasonable basis for taking this investment action
questions.explanation: A is correct because the information concerning the qualified opinion is nonpublic and if it is material she would be in violation of Standard II(A) if she took investment action based on the information. She should also make reasonable efforts to achieve public dissemination of the information. B is incorrect because she should make reasonable efforts to achieve public dissemination of the information prior to selling the stock. C is incorrect because she should make reasonable efforts to achieve public dissemination of the information prior to selling the stock.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely sufficient to meet recommended or required procedures for compliance with CFA Institute Standard III(A): Loyalty, Prudence, and Care?
questions.option_a: Disclose any existing conflicts of interest.
questions.option_b: Establish a regular client meeting schedule.
questions.option_c: Seek best execution when trading on behalf of clients.
questions.explanation: A is correct. Disclosing any existing conflict of interest is least likely adequate to comply with the recommended or required procedure for compliance with CFA Institute Standard III(A): Loyalty, Prudence, and Care. The recommended procedure for compliance states that members and candidates must disclose all actual and potential conflicts of interest so that clients can evaluate those conflicts. B is incorrect. Establishing a regular client meeting schedule is a recommended or required procedure for compliance with Standard III(A): Loyalty, Prudence, and Care. Members and candidates should establish regularly scheduled client reviews to ensure the investments held adhere to the terms of the clients’ governing documents. C is incorrect. Seeking best execution when trading on behalf of clients, unless directed by the client to do otherwise, is a recommended or required procedure for compliance with Standard III(A): Loyalty, Prudence, and Care.

questions.stem: A member is developing allocation procedures for block trades and new issues. According to the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to fair dealing, the member's allocation procedures should involve:
questions.option_a: prohibiting consideration of advanced interest when allocating trades for new issues.
questions.option_b: bundling orders on a first-in, first-out basis for efficiency as appropriate for the asset class.
questions.option_c: giving client accounts participating in a block trade execution prices corresponding to order arrival time.
questions.explanation: B is correct because according to the recommendations for Standard III (B), Fair Dealing, procedures should include "processing and executing orders on a first-in, first-out basis with consideration of bundling orders for efficiency as appropriate for the asset class or the security." A is incorrect because according to the recommendations for Standard III (B), Fair Dealing, procedures should include "when allocating trades for new issues, obtaining advance indications of interest, allocating securities by client (rather than portfolio manager), and providing a method for calculating allocations." C is incorrect because according to the recommendations for Standard III (B), Fair Dealing, procedures should include "giving all client accounts participating in a block trade the same execution price and charging the same commission." So, the price should be the same, not based on order arrival time.

questions.stem: According to the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to additional compensation arrangements, a member should make an immediate written report specifying the proposed compensation arrangements:
questions.option_b: only to her supervisor and to her firm's compliance officer.
questions.option_c: to her supervisor, to her firm's compliance officer, and to her clients.
questions.explanation: B is correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(B), Additional Compensation Arrangements, “Members and candidates should make an immediate written report to their supervisor and compliance officer specifying any compensation they propose to receive for services...” A is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(B), Additional Compensation Arrangements, “Members... should make an immediate written report to their supervisor and compliance officer specifying any compensation they propose to receive for services...” C is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(B), Additional Compensation Arrangements, “Members... should make an immediate written report to their supervisor and compliance officer..." but not to their clients.

questions.stem: Which of the following is consistent with the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to referral fees?
questions.option_c: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2
questions.explanation: A is correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard VI (C), Referral Fees, “Employers should have investment professionals provide to the clients notification of approved referral fee programs…” B is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard VI (C), Referral Fees, “Employers should have investment professionals …provide the employer regular (at least quarterly) updates on the amount and nature of compensation received.” So, at least quarterly, not annual. C is incorrect because only Statement 1 is correct, as described in the response rationale for the correct answer.

questions.stem: Jan Loots, CFA, quit his job as a portfolio manager at an investment firm with which he had a non-solicitation agreement he signed several years ago. Loots received permission to take his investment performance history with him and also took a copy of the firm’s software-trading platform. Subsequently, Loots sent out messages on social media sites announcing he was looking for clients for his new investment management firm. Access to Loots’ social media sites is restricted to friends, family, and former clients. Loots least likelyviolated the CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct concerning his:
questions.option_c: investment performance history.
questions.explanation: C is correct because the portfolio manager received permission to use his investment performance history from his prior employer. The member violated his non-solicitation agreement by indicating his availability to new clients on several social media sites accessible by clients of his former employer. This is a violation of Standard IV(A)–Loyalty because he did not act for the benefit of his former employer. In this case, the member may cause harm to his former employer if his weekend messages result in clients moving to his new business from his former employer. The member also violated this standard by taking his employer’s property, trading software. A is incorrect because the portfolio manager took property of his former employer, proprietary trading software, and violated Standard IV(A)–Loyalty. Although the manager created the software himself, it was during a period of time when the large money manager employed him and the software is not his property to take. B is incorrect because the member violated Standard IV(A)–Loyalty as he did not act for the benefit of his former employer. In this case, the member may cause harm to his former employer if his weekend messages result in clients moving to his new business.

questions.stem: According to the recommended procedures for compliance with the Standard relating to responsibilities of supervisors, a member should encourage her employer to:
questions.option_a: integrate a code of ethics into compliance procedures.
questions.option_b: build incentive structures based on how much revenue is generated for the firm.
questions.option_c: write a code of ethics in plain language and without numerous detailed procedures.
questions.explanation: C is correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV (C), Responsibilities of Supervisors, “Stand-alone codes of ethics should be written in plain language and should address general fiduciary concepts. They should be unencumbered by numerous detailed procedures.” A is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV (C), Responsibilities of Supervisors, “Separating the code of ethics from compliance procedures will also reduce, if not eliminate, the legal terminology and “boilerplate” language that can make the underlying ethical principles incomprehensible to the average person.” B is incorrect because “Only when compensation and incentives are firmly tied to client interests and how outcomes are achieved, rather than how much is generated for the firm, will employees work to achieve a culture of integrity.”

questions.stem: A member has been asked by her supervisor to write a research report on a company. The member's firm owns options to buy the company's stock. The member's firm does not possess material nonpublic information on the company. According to the Standards, the member should:
questions.option_a: outsource the report to an approved third-party research provider.
questions.option_b: place the stock on a restricted list and provide only factual information about the company.
questions.option_c: disclose in the research report the amount and the expiration date of the options held by her firm in the covered company.
questions.explanation: C is correct because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard VI (A), Disclosure of Conflicts, "If a member, a candidate, or a member's or candidate's firm has outstanding agent options to buy stock as part of the compensation package for corporate financing activities, the amount and expiration date of these options should be disclosed as a footnote to any research report published by the member's or candidate's firm." Therefore, if the member's firm owns options to buy the company's stock as part of the compensation for offering corporate finance solutions, the member should disclose in the research report the amount and the expiration date of the options held by her firm in the covered company. A is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard VI (A), Disclosure of Conflicts, the member need not outsource the report to a third-party research provider. As described in the response rationale for the correct answer, the member should disclose in the research report the amount and the expiration date of the options held by her firm in the covered company. B is incorrect because according to the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard II (A), Material Nonpublic Information, "Firms should consider restrictions or prohibitions on personal trading by employees and should carefully monitor both proprietary trading and personal trading by employees. ... Securities should be placed on a restricted list when a firm has or may have material nonpublic information." The firm does not possess material nonpublic information about the covered company. Also, the stem does not relate to personal trading by employees. Therefore, the member need not place the stock on a restricted list and provide only factual information about the company. As described in the response rationale for the correct answer, Standard VI (A), Disclosure of Conflicts, recommends that the member disclose in the research report the amount and the expiration date of the options held by her firm in the covered company.

questions.stem: For a retail client's account to be included in a GIPS®-compliant firm’s composite, it will most likely be in a composite:
questions.option_c: with both fee-paying and non-fee-paying accounts.
questions.explanation: A is correct. A composite must include all actual, fee-paying, discretionary segregated accounts managed in accordance with the same investment mandate, objective, or strategy. B is incorrect. Institutional accounts may be included in a composite with retail accounts if they have a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy. C is incorrect. Non-fee-paying accounts are not required to be in a GIPS-compliant composite.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the GIPS standards is accurate?
questions.option_a: All fee-paying client portfolios must be included in at least one composite.
questions.option_b: All portfolios with the same investment mandate are aggregated into a composite.
questions.option_c: Aggregation of portfolios into composites is based on the actual performance of the portfolios every year.
questions.explanation: B is correct because according to the GIPS standards, "A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy." A is incorrect because according to the GIPS standards, "[a] claim of compliance requires that all fee-paying discretionary accounts managed by the firm be included in at least one composite...Non-discretionary portfolios must not be included in a firm’s composites." Fee-paying non-discretionary portfolios do not have to be included. C is incorrect because according to the GIPS standards, "[t]he determination of which portfolios to include in the Composite should be done according to pre-established criteria (i.e., on an ex-ante basis), not after the fact." Basing it on actual performance would require the aggregation to be done after the fact which is incorrect.

questions.stem: Which of the following should a GIPS®-compliant firm most likely provide to each prospective client?
questions.option_a: A list of composite descriptions upon request
questions.option_b: A copy of the GIPS standards
questions.option_c: A compliant presentation every six months
questions.explanation: A is correct. GIPS-compliant firms must provide a complete list of composite descriptions to any prospective client that makes such a request. The list must include terminated composites for a minimum of five years after the composite termination date. B is incorrect. A firm is not required to give a copy of the GIPS standards to prospective clients. C is incorrect. Firms must make every reasonable effort to provide a compliant presentation to all prospective clients. A firm meets this requirement if the firm gives the prospective client a compliant presentation every 12 months, not every 6 months.

questions.stem: According to the GIPS standards, which of the following statements is mostaccurate? Verification:
questions.option_a: ensures the accuracy of composite presentations.
questions.option_b: is required to maintain compliance with the GIPS standards.
questions.option_c: tests whether a firm has complied with composite construction requirements on a firm-wide basis.
questions.explanation: C is correct because according to GIPS standards, "One of the key concepts of the standards is the required use of composites. A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy. The requirement to create, use and maintain composites is designed to prevent firms from cherry-picking—using the best-performing accounts to represent the performance of an investment strategy." Further, "Veriﬁcation provides assurance on whether the ﬁrm’s policies and procedures related to composite and pooled fund maintenance, as well as the calculation, presentation, and distribution of performance, have been designed in compliance with the GIPS standards and have been implemented on a ﬁrm-wide basis.” A is incorrect because according to GIPS standards, “Verification does not ensure the accuracy of any specific composite presentation.” B is incorrect because according to GIPS standards, “Once a firm claims compliance with the Standards, they may voluntarily hire an independent third party to perform a verification in order to increase confidence in the firm's claim of compliance.” Therefore, verification is not mandatory; merely complying with the GIPS standards is enough for the firm to inform its clients and prospective clients that its performance presentation is in accordance with the GIPS standards.

questions.stem: If the effective annual rate is 6% with monthly compounding, the periodic rate is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct because the periodic rate is found using the equation EAR = (1 + periodic interest rate) m – 1 and solving for the periodic rate; 0.06 = (1 + periodic interest rate) 12 – 1; periodic interest rate = 1.06 (1/12) – 1 = 0.487%. Alternatively, the periodic rate is the stated annual rate of 5.841% divided by 12 periods or 0.487%; 0.06 = (1 + stated annual rate / 12) 12 – 1; stated annual rate = (1.06 (1/12) – 1) × 12 = 5.841%. Calculator solution: ICONV; EFF = 6%; C/Y = 12; compute NOM = 5.841%; 5.841%/12 = 0.487%. B is incorrect because it is the effective annual rate (rather than the stated annual rate) divided by 12; 6%/12 = 0.500%. C is incorrect because it incorrectly uses the effective annual rate (EAR) as the stated annual rate to calculate the periodic rate; [(1 + 0.06/12) 12 – 1]/12 = 6.168%/12 = 0.514%.

questions.stem: An investor gathers the following information: If a $1,000 deposit is made today, the future value in one year will be greatest for:
questions.option_c: Account 3.
questions.explanation: C is correct because the account with the highest effective annual rate (EAR) will have the greatest future value in one year. “The effective annual rate is calculated as follows: EAR = (1 + Periodic interest rate)m – 1. The periodic interest rate is the stated annual interest rate divided by m, where m is the number of compounding periods in one year.” (pp. 315-316) The EAR of Account 3 is (1 + 0.062/4)4 – 1 = 0.06346 = 6.35%, compared to (1 + 0.061/365)365 – 1 = 0.06289 = 6.29% for Account 1 and 6.30% for Account 2. The resulting future values are: $1,063.46 for Account 3, compared to $1,062.89 for Account 1 and $1,063.00 for Account 2. A is incorrect because Account 3 will have the greatest future value in one year. Despite Account 1's more frequent compounding, the lower stated annual interest rate results in a lower future value when compared to Account 3. B is incorrect because Account 3 will have the greatest future value in one year. Despite Account 2's higher stated annual interest rate, the less frequent compounding results in a lower future value when compared to Account 3.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following cumulative absolute frequency distribution of ratings for a bond portfolio: The relative frequency of BBB rated bonds is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct because “[t]he cumulative absolute frequency cumulates (meaning, adds up) the absolute frequencies as we move from the first bin to the last bin." The absolute frequency of BBB rated bonds is equal to the cumulative absolute frequency of BBB rated bonds minus the cumulative absolute frequency of the previous bin [A rated bonds]: 12 – 8 = 4. "For the last bin, the cumulative absolute frequency will equal the number observations in the dataset [24]." Hence, the relative frequency of BBB rated bonds "is calculated as the absolute frequency of each unique value of the variable divided by the total number of observations," which is 4/24 = 0.167 ≈ 17%. B is incorrect because it wrongly assumes the cumulative absolute frequency is the absolute frequency. Hence, the total number of observations becomes 3 + 8 + 12 + 24 = 47. The relative frequency of BBB rated bonds "is calculated as the absolute frequency of each unique value of the variable divided by the total number of observations," which is 12/47 = 0.255 ≈ 26%. C is incorrect because it wrongly calculates the absolute frequency as the cumulative absolute frequency of the next bin [BB rated bonds] minus the cumulative absolute frequency of BBB rated bonds: 24 – 12 = 12. "For the last bin, the cumulative absolute frequency will equal the number observations in the dataset [24]." Hence, the relative frequency of BBB rated bonds "is calculated as the absolute frequency of each unique value of the variable divided by the total number of observations," which is 12/24 = 0.50 = 50%. It is also the answer if the relative frequency is wrongly calculated as the cumulative absolute frequency of BBB rated bonds divided by the total number of observations: 12/24 = 0.50 = 50%.

questions.stem: Consider the following 20 items listed in ascending order: The median value of the items is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct. The median is the value of the middle item of a set of items that has been sorted into ascending or descending order. In an even-numbered sample, we define the median as the mean of the values of items occupying the n/2 and (n + 2)/2 positions (the two middle items). The n/2 item is the 10th item and the (n + 2)/2 item is the 11th item. The value of the 10th item is 3; the value of the 11th item is 5. The mean of 3 and 5 is 4. A is incorrect. It is the value of the 11th item. C is incorrect. It is the value of the 10th item and also the value of the mode.

questions.stem: If all paired observations of random variables X and Y satisfy the equation Y = –0.2 + 0.8X, the correlation between X and Y is:
questions.explanation: C is correct because if all data points lie exactly on the line Y = –0.2 + 0.8X, this indicates a perfect (positive) linear relationship, and "[a] correlation of 1 indicates a perfect linear relationship." Also, "[e]ven if the slope of the line were different (but positive), the correlation between the two variables would still be +1 as long as all the points lie on that straight line." A is incorrect because X and Y have a perfect linear relationship and "[a] correlation of 1 indicates a perfect linear relationship," not 0.6 (= –0.2 + 0.8). B is incorrect because X and Y have a perfect linear relationship and "[a] correlation of 1 indicates a perfect linear relationship," not 0.8.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about three events: The odds for Event 1 are 3 to 4. The odds against Event 2 are 6 to 8. The probability of Event 3 is 0.52. The event with the highest probability of occurring is:
questions.option_c: Event 3.
questions.explanation: B is correct because the probability of Event 2 occurring is 8/(6 + 8) = 8/14 = 0.57, since "[g]iven odds against E of 'a to b', the implied probability of E is b/(a + b)." This probability is higher than the probability of either Event 1 (0.43 = 3/(3 + 4) = 3/7) or Event 3 (0.52). The calculation can be simplified by noticing that the odds for Event 2 are 8 to 6, i.e. 4 to 3, which is the reciprocal of the odds for Event 1, so the probability of Event 2 occurring is 1 – 0.43 = 0.57. A is incorrect because the probability of Event 1 is 3/(3 + 4) = 3/7 = 0.43, since "[g]iven odds for E of 'a to b', the implied probability of E is a/(a + b)," and this is lower than the probability of Event 2 (0.57 = 8/(6 + 8) = 8/14). C is incorrect because the probability of Event 3 is 0.52, which is lower than that of Event 2 (0.57 = 8/(6 + 8) = 8/14).

questions.stem: For two random events A and B, the conditional probability of A occurring given that B has occurred is equal to:
questions.option_a: one, if A and B are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
questions.option_b: the unconditional probability of A, if A and B are independent.
questions.option_c: the joint probability of A and B multiplied by the probability of B.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[t]wo events A and B are independent if and only if P(A | B) = P(A)". A is incorrect because "[t]he conditional probability of A given that B has occurred is equal to the joint probability of A and B divided by the probability of B (assumed not to equal 0)". In the case of mutually exclusive events, where "only one event can occur at a time", the joint probability of A and B is zero, and the conditional probability is also zero. C is incorrect because "[t]he conditional probability of A given that B has occurred is equal to the joint probability of A and B divided by the probability of B (assumed not to equal 0)", not multiplied by the probability of B.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following probability distribution of a company's earnings: The standard deviation of the company's earnings is closest to:
questions.option_c: $375 million.
questions.explanation: A is correct because the expected value is calculated as E(X) = P(X 1 )X 1 + P(X 2 )X 2 + … + P(X n )X n = 0.25×100 + 0.70×300 + 0.05×600 = 25 + 210 + 30 = 265 and the variance is calculated as σ 2 (X) = E{[X − E(X)] 2 } = 0.25×(100 – 265) 2 + 0.70×(300 – 265) 2 + 0.05×(600 – 265) 2 = 6,806.25 + 857.50 + 5,611.25 = 13,275 and the "[s]tandard deviation is s the positive square root of variance", i.e. 13,275 1/2 ≈ $115.22 ≈ $115 million. B is incorrect because the candidate incorrectly calculates the expected value as the unweighted mean, i.e. E(X) ≠ (100 + 300 + 600)/3 ≈ 333.33. Then the variance is calculated as σ 2 (X) = E{[X − E(X)] 2 } = 0.25×(100 – 333.33) 2 + 0.70×(300 – 333.33) 2 + 0.05×(600 – 333.33) 2 ≈ 13,610.72 + 777.62 + 3,555.64 = 17,943.98 and the "[s]tandard deviation is s the positive square root of variance", i.e. 17,943.98 1/2 ≈ $133.96 ≈ $134 million. C is incorrect because the candidate omits the probabilities in the calculation of variance. The candidate calculates the expected value correctly as E(X) = P(X 1 )X 1 + P(X 2 )X 2 + … + P(X n )X n = 0.25×100 + 0.70×300 + 0.05×600 = 25 + 210 + 30 = 265. The candidate then incorrectly calculates the variance as σ 2 (X) = E{[X − E(X)] 2 } ≠ (100 – 265) 2 + (300 – 265) 2 + (600 – 265) 2 = 27,225 + 1,225 + 112,225 = 140,675 and the "[s]tandard deviation is s the positive square root of variance", i.e. 140,675 1/2 ≈ $375.07 ≈ $375 million.

questions.stem: A model to simulate stock price movement assumes that, in any one period, the price can move up, move down, or remain unchanged. In a 7-period model, the number of possible sequences which contain, in any order, a total of 2 "up" moves, 2 "down" moves, and 3 "unchanged" moves, is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct because, according to the multinomial formula, "[t]he number of ways that n objects [7 periods] can be labeled with k different labels [3 potential moves in each period], with n 1 [= 2] of the first type, n 2 [= 2] of the second type, and so on [n 3 = 3], with n 1 + n 2 + ... + n k = n, is given by n!/(n 1 !n 2 !...n k !)," and in this case the number of ways is 7!/(2!2!3!) = 5,040/(2 × 2 × 6) = 210. A is incorrect because the calculation used is 7 C 2 + 7 C 2 + 7 C 3 = 7!/(2!5!) + 7!/(2!5!) + 7!/(3!4!) = 21 + 21 + 35 = 77 instead of the multinomial formula. C is incorrect because the calculation used is 7!/[(2)(2)(3)] = 5,040/12 = 420 instead of 7!/(2!2!3!).

questions.stem: What is the probability that a uniform random variable with limits of a = 2 and b = 10 is less than or equal to 5?
questions.explanation: A is correct because "the middle line of the expression for the cdf [of the continuous uniform distribution] captures this relationship: 0 for x < a F(x) = x – a / b – a for a ≤ x ≤ b. 1 for x > b" For our problem, F(x) = 0 for x < 2, F(x) = (x – 2)/8 for 2 ≤ x ≤ 10, and F(x) = 1 for x > 10. Hence, F(5) = (5 – 2)/8 = 0.375. B is incorrect because it incorrectly computes the cdf F(x) = x/b and F(5) = 5/10 = 0.5 instead of F(x) = x – a / b – a, when evaluated at a point between limits a and b. C is incorrect because it incorrectly computes the cdf for the continuous uniform distribution as F(x) = x/(b – a) and F(5) = 5/8 = 0.625 instead of F(x) = x – a / b – a,when evaluated at a point between limits a and b.

questions.stem: A normal random variable, X, has a mean of 4.0 and a standard deviation of 2.0. A value X = 10.0 corresponds to a standardized value of:
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[i]f we have X ~ N(μ, σ 2 )..., we standardize it using the formula Z = (X − μ)/σ." In this case, Z = (X – μ)/σ = (10 – 4) /2 = 3. A is incorrect because it incorrectly computes the standardized value Z as (X – μ)/σ 2 = (10 –4) /4 = 1.5. B is incorrect because it incorrectly computes the standardized value Z as (X – σ)/μ = (10 – 2)/4 = 2.

questions.stem: The F-distribution is:
questions.option_a: defined by a single value of degrees of freedom.
questions.option_b: a family of asymmetric distributions whose outcomes span the entire real line.
questions.option_c: the basis for hypothesis tests concerning the equality of variances of two normally distributed populations.
questions.explanation: C is correct because the chi-square statistic is used to test the variance of a normally distributed population, while the F-statistic is used to test the equality of variances of two normally distributed populations from two independent random samples. A is incorrect because "[e]ach F-distribution is defined by two values of degrees of freedom, called the numerator and denominator degrees of freedom." B is incorrect because the probability density functions of the F-distributions can take only positive values. "Like the chi-square distribution, the F-distribution is a family of asymmetrical distributions bounded from below by 0."

questions.stem: Which of the following sampling methods involves selecting every kth member from a population until a desired sample size is obtained?
questions.option_c: Convenience sampling
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[w]ith systematic sampling, we select every kth member until we have a sample of the desired size. The sample that results from this procedure should be approximately random." A is incorrect because "[i]n this method, the population is divided into clusters, each of which is essentially a mini-representation of the entire populations Then certain clusters are chosen as a whole using simple random sampling." C is incorrect because "[i]n this method, an element is selected from the population based on whether or not it is accessible to a researcher or on how easy it is for a researcher to access the element. Because the samples are selected conveniently, they are not necessarily representative of the entire population, and hence the level of the sampling accuracy could be limited."

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a sample from a population with a lognormal distribution: The standard error of the sample mean is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct because when the standard deviation of the population is not known, the standard error of the sample mean sX̅ = s/(n) 0.5 , where s is the standard deviation and n is the sample size. Since the variance s 2 = Σ(Xi – X̅) 2 /(n – 1) = 12/(30 – 1) = 0.4138; s = 0.4138 0.5 = 0.6433, so that sX̅ = 0.6433/300.5 = 0.1174 ≈ 0.12. B is incorrect because it is the variance, not the standard error of the sample mean. s 2 = Σ(Xi – X̅) 2 /(n – 1) = 12/(30 – 1) = 0.4138 ≈ 0.41. This answer is also closest if the standard error of the sample mean is calculated as X̅/(n) 0.5 = 2.27/(30) 0.5 = 0.4144 ≈ 0.41. C is incorrect because it is the standard deviation, not the standard error of the sample mean. s 2 = Σ(Xi – X̅) 2 /(n – 1) = 12/(30 – 1) = 0.4138; s = 0.41380.5 = 0.6433 ≈ 0.64.

questions.stem: The practice of determining a model by extensively searching a dataset for statistically significant patterns best describes:
questions.option_c: sample selection bias.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "[d]ata snooping is the practice of determining a model by extensive searching through a dataset for statistically significant patterns (that is, repeatedly “drilling” in the same data until finding something that appears to work)." To "investigate the presence of data snooping bias[,] ... we can split the data into three separate datasets: the training dataset, the validation dataset, and the test dataset. ... The test dataset is to provide an out-of-sample test to evaluate the final model fit. If a variable or investment strategy is the result of data snooping, it should generally not be significant in out-of-sample tests." A is incorrect because "[a] test design is subject to look-ahead bias if it uses information that was not available on the test date." C is incorrect because sample selection bias refers to "certain assets being excluded from the analysis."

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the p-value is most accurate?
questions.option_a: The smaller the p-value, the smaller the chance of a false positive.
questions.option_b: The p-value is a calculated test statistic used in hypothesis testing.
questions.option_c: The smaller the p-value, the stronger the evidence against the alternative hypothesis.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[t]he smaller the p-value, the smaller the chance of making a Type I error," and "[a] Type I error is a false positive." B is incorrect because "[t]he p-value is the area in the probability distribution outside the calculated test statistic; ... the p-value is the area under the curve (so, the probability) associated with the calculated test statistic," and not the test statistic itself. C is incorrect because "[t]he smaller the p-value, the stronger the evidence against the null hypothesis," and not the alternative hypothesis.

questions.stem: An analyst builds a contingency table of stocks with two classifications: market capitalization (small, medium, large) and beta (high, medium, low). To test the relationship between size and beta using a test of independence, the number of degrees of freedom for the chi-square test statistic is:
questions.explanation: A is correct because for "a contingency table ... [the independence] test statistic has (r − 1)(c − 1) degrees of freedom, where r is the number of rows and c is the number of columns." For the contingency table in the stem, there are 3 rows and 3 columns as each classification has 3 groups. Hence, the number of degrees of freedom is equal to (r − 1)(c − 1) = (3 − 1)(3 − 1) = 4. B is incorrect because it wrongly assumes the number of degrees of freedom for the test of independence equals the sum of the number of groups in each classification: 3 + 3 = 6. C is incorrect because it wrongly assumes the number of degrees of freedom for the test of independence equals the product of the number of groups in each classification (= rc). For the contingency table in the stem, there are 3 rows and 3 columns as each classification has 3 groups. Hence, the number of degrees of freedom is incorrectly calculated as rc = 3 × 3 = 9.

questions.stem: An analyst runs a simple linear regression using 35 months of data to assess a country's short-term interest rate as a function of its inflation rate, with the following results: The value of the standard error of the estimate is closest to:
questions.explanation: B is correct because the standard error of the estimate in a linear regression is the square root of the mean square error, thus 0.61300.5 = 0.7829 ≈ 0.78. A is incorrect because it incorrectly considers the standard error of the estimate as the square root of the coefficient of determination, which is calculated as the sum of square regression/sum of squares total: = 17.3009/37.5308 = 0.461. Then 0.4610.5 = 0.6789 ≈ 0.68. C is incorrect because it is the sample standard deviation of the dependent variable, computed as the square root of the total variation of the dependent variable divided by the number of observations minus one: (37.5308/34)0.5 = 1.0506 ≈ 1.05.

questions.stem: If the price of one good purchased by a consumer increases while the price of all other goods remains the same, the consumer's real income:
questions.option_c: increases.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "the rise in the price of beef [a good] results in a decrease in the consumer’s real income because now she [the consumer] can buy less goods with the same amount of money income." B is incorrect because "the rise in the price of beef [a good] results in a decrease in the consumer’s real income because now she [the consumer] can buy less goods with the same amount of money income." C is incorrect because "the rise in the price of beef [a good] results in a decrease in the consumer’s real income because now she [the consumer] can buy less goods with the same amount of money income."

questions.stem: In the short run, a firm operating in a perfectly competitive market will most likelyavoid shutdown if it is able to earn sufficient revenue to cover which of the following costs?
questions.option_c: Variable
questions.explanation: C is correct. Shutdown is defined as a situation in which the firm stops production but still confronts the payment of fixed costs in the short run. In the short run, a business can operate at a loss as long as it covers its variable costs even though it is not earning sufficient revenue to cover fixed costs. If variable costs cannot be covered in the short run (P < AVC), the firm will shut down operations and simply absorb the unavoidable fixed costs. A is incorrect. In the short run, a business can operate at a loss as long as it covers variable costs even though it is not earning sufficient revenue to cover fixed costs. B is incorrect. Marginal cost is the incremental cost of producing one more unit and can be calculated as either (Δ total cost/Δ quantity) or (Δ total variable cost/Δ quantity).

questions.stem: The following data apply to a firm operating in perfect competition. The firm’s profit maximizing output (in units) is most likely:
questions.explanation: A is correct. Under perfect competition, economic profits are maximized when marginal revenue equals marginal cost—in this case, marginal cost crosses $10 per unit. Profits are maximized at 23 units of production because marginal cost is in excess of marginal revenue at 24 units. B is incorrect. At and beyond 24 units, marginal costs exceed marginal revenue. C is incorrect. It represents the minimum total cost point for the given data, not the profit maximizing point.

questions.stem: Customers are segregated by demographic traits in the case of:
questions.option_c: third-degree price discrimination.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[t]hird-degree price discrimination happens when customers are segregated by demographic or other traits." A is incorrect because "[t]hird-degree price discrimination happens when customers are segregated by demographic or other traits." In contrast, in first-degree price discrimination "a monopolist can charge each customer the highest price the customer is willing to pay." B is incorrect because "[t]hird-degree price discrimination happens when customers are segregated by demographic or other traits." In contrast, in "second-degree price discrimination the monopolist offers a menu of quantity-based pricing options designed to induce customers to self-select based on how highly they value the product."

questions.stem: All else being equal, a reduction in a government's fiscal deficit is most likelyaccompanied by a decrease in the value of:
questions.option_c: domestic private sector saving.
questions.explanation: C is correct because the fundamental relationship between saving (S), investment (I), the fiscal balance (G ‒ T) and the trade balance (X ‒ M) is S = I + (G ‒ T) + (X ‒ M), where G is government expenditure, T is net taxes, X is exports and M is imports. This can be rearranged to (G ‒ T) = (S ‒ I) ‒ (X ‒ M); a fiscal deficit occurs when (G ‒ T) > 0. All else being equal, a reduction in the fiscal deficit (G ‒ T) is accompanied by a decrease in domestic private sector saving (S), for example due to increased private sector consumption. A is incorrect because the fundamental relationship between saving (S), investment (I), the fiscal balance (G ‒ T) and the trade balance (X ‒ M) is S = I + (G ‒ T) + (X ‒ M), which can be rearranged to (G ‒ T) = (S ‒ I) ‒ (X ‒ M). All else being equal, a decrease in exports (X) reduces the trade balance (X ‒ M) and goes along with an increase in the fiscal deficit instead of a reduction. B is incorrect because “[h]ouseholds allocate disposable income between consumption of goods and services (C) and household saving (SH).” (p. 133) The fundamental relationship between saving (S), investment (I), the fiscal balance (G ‒ T) and the trade balance (X ‒ M) is S = I + (G ‒ T) + (X ‒ M), which can be rearranged to (G ‒ T) = (S ‒ I) ‒ (X ‒ M), where G is government expenditure, T is net taxes, X is exports and M is imports. All else being equal, a decrease in consumer spending (C) increases domestic private saving (S) which goes along with an increase in the fiscal deficit instead of a decrease.

questions.stem: Economic expansion most likely occurs as a result of a:
questions.option_b: leftward shift in the aggregate demand curve.
questions.option_c: rightward shift in the aggregate demand curve.
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[i]ncreases in AD [rightward shift] lead to economic expansions as real GDP and employment increase." A is incorrect because over the long run the aggregate supply curve is assumed to be vertical, and it is from "fluctuations arising from shifts in the AD and SRAS curves, [that] the economy rarely operates at potential GDP." The supply curve staying vertical will not result in an economic expansion. B is incorrect because "a leftward shift in the AD curve results in lower [not higher] GDP."

questions.stem: Which of the following changes most likely leads to a decrease in GDP and an uncertain impact on the price level?
questions.option_a: A decrease in both aggregate demand and aggregate supply.
questions.option_b: A decrease in aggregate demand and an increase in aggregate supply.
questions.option_c: An increase in aggregate demand and a decrease in aggregate supply.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[i]f both AD and AS decrease, real GDP and employment will decline but the effect on the price level is unclear unless we know the magnitude of the changes, because a decrease in AD decreases the price level, whereas a decrease in AS increases the price level. If AD decreases more than AS, the price level will fall. If AS decreases more than AD, the price level will rise." B is incorrect because "[i]f AD decreases and AS increases, the price level will decline but the effect on real GDP is unclear unless we know the magnitudes of the changes, because a decrease in AD decreases real GDP, whereas an increase in AS increases real GDP. If AD decreases more than AS increases, real GDP will fall. If AS increases more than AD declines, real GDP will rise." C is incorrect because "[i]f AD increases and AS declines, the price level will rise but the effect on real GDP is unclear unless we know the magnitude of the changes, because an increase in AD increases real GDP, whereas a decrease in AS decreases real GDP. If AD increases more than AS declines, GDP will rise. If AS decreases more than AD increases, real GDP will fall."

questions.stem: Which of the following theories of the business cycle focuses more on the role of money?
questions.option_c: The Austrian School
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[t]he so-called Austrian school, another “non-intervention” theory, shares many views of the neoclassical economists. In contrast to the neoclassical school, however, it focuses on the role of money, which they believe does more than facilitate the exchange of goods and services." A is incorrect because "[k]eynesian economists advocate government intervention in the form of fiscal policy." "...the Keynesian model does not recognize the supreme importance of the money supply." B is incorrect because "[n]eoclassical economists, but in particular the so-called Real Business Cycle (RBC) advocates, stress the importance of movements in the supply curve."

questions.stem: A member of the labor force quit her job last week and will begin a new job next week. During this interim period, for the purposes of calculating unemployment statistics, this person is most likely classified as:
questions.option_c: voluntarily unemployed.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Frictional unemployment is short term and transitory in nature; it includes people who are “between jobs,” as in this case, and those who are not working because they are taking time to search for a job that better matches their skills, interests, and other preferences. A is incorrect. The hidden unemployed encompass discouraged workers and underemployed people. Discouraged workers are those who have stopped looking for a job, and the underemployed are those who have a job but have qualifications to work at significantly higher paying jobs. C is incorrect. Although this person likely left their old job voluntarily, frictionally unemployed is a better answer here because they do have a job waiting for them. The voluntarily unemployed are persons outside the labor force who might refuse an available vacancy if the pay rate is below their reservation wage or those who might have retired early.

questions.stem: A central bank increases its purchases of bonds from commercial banks intending to decrease interest rates, boost confidence, increase asset prices, and ultimately raise the general level of employment, production, and prices in the economy. This is most likely an example of:
questions.option_c: the monetary transmission mechanism.
questions.explanation: C is correct. The implementation of monetary policy may work through the economy via four interrelated channels: lending rates, asset prices, agents’ expectations, and exchange rates. A is incorrect. If money neutrality holds, only prices would rise whereas employment and output would not change. B is incorrect. Expansionary fiscal policy is implemented by reducing taxes and/or raising government spending.

questions.stem: Quantitative easing addresses the monetary policy challenges most likely caused by:
questions.option_c: inflationary demand shocks or supply shocks.
questions.explanation: A is correct. In a deflationary environment, reducing rates below zero may become ineffective and result in a liquidity trap. The next step to deter deflation is quantitative easing. B is incorrect. Bond market vigilantes act on long-term rates when they determine that the central bank lacks credibility or is ineffective in its policy implementation. C is incorrect. Demand shocks and supply shocks that cause increases in inflation would not be addressed by quantitative easing. Such an action would exacerbate inflation.

questions.stem: For similar amounts, which of the following actions will have the largest effect on GDP? An increase in:
questions.option_c: social transfers to the poorest citizens.
questions.explanation: A is correct because '[g]overnment spending increases have a much bigger effect (six times bigger) on GDP than similar size social transfers because the latter are not considered permanent." B is incorrect because "[g]overnment spending increases have a much bigger effect (six times bigger) on GDP than similar size social transfers."… C is incorrect because "[g]overnment spending increases have a much bigger effect (six times bigger) on GDP than similar size social transfers…"

questions.stem: A country seeking nationalism but willing to cooperate with other countries is best classified as:
questions.option_c: hegemonic.
questions.explanation: B is correct because bilateralism describes a country seeking both nationalism and cooperation. "Bilateralism is the conduct of political, economic, financial, or cultural cooperation between two countries." A is incorrect because "[a]utarky describes countries seeking political self-sufficiency with little or no external trade or finance." Autarky describes a country seeking both anti-globalization and non-cooperation. C is incorrect because hegemony describes a country seeking both globalization and non-cooperation. "A hegemonic system can provide valuable benefits both to hegemonic countries themselves and to the international system. For the country itself, economic and political dominance may provide important influence on global affairs."

questions.stem: The production capabilities of two countries for computers and phones is as follows: Country X is best described as having a comparative advantage over Country Y for producing:
questions.option_c: phones and computers.
questions.explanation: A is correct. A country has a comparative advantage if its opportunity cost for producing a product is less than its trading partners: the cost of a computer in units of phones is lowest for Country X. Country X has an absolute advantage over country Y in producing both computers and phones. B is incorrect because Country Y has the higher opportunity cost in making phones. C is incorrect because Country Y has a comparative advantage in making phones.

questions.stem: All else being equal, a government's budget deficit is most likely reduced after the introduction of:
questions.option_c: both tariffs and export subsidies.
questions.explanation: A is correct because “[t]ariffs are taxes that a government levies on imported goods.” Therefore, all else being equal, the imposition of a tariff will increase government revenue and thereby reduce a government budget deficit. “An export subsidy is paid by the government to the firm when it exports a unit of a good that is being subsidized.” Therefore, all else being equal, a new export subsidy will increase, not decrease, a government's budget deficit. B is incorrect because “[a]n export subsidy is a payment by the government to a firm for each unit of a good that is exported.” Furthermore, “[a]n export subsidy is paid by the government to the firm when it exports a unit of a good that is being subsidized.” All else being equal, a new export subsidy will increase a government's budget deficit. C is incorrect because an export subsidy will increase a government's budget deficit, not reduce it.

questions.stem: A country’s international transactions accounts data for last year are presented in its domestic currency: The current account balance is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. B is incorrect. It is simply Exports – Imports: 10,000 – 14,216 = –4,216. C is incorrect. It mixes up the direction of flow for the income payments and receipts and the unilateral transfers Exports + Income payments made + Unilateral transfers paid = 10,000 + 1,107 + 2,519 + 1,107 = 13,626 Imports + Income payments received + Unilateral transfers received = 14,216 + 3,409 + 346 = 17,971 13,626 – 17,971 = –4,345

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about foreign exchange spot prices: The percentage appreciation of the EUR/CAD is closest to:
questions.explanation: C is correct because the EUR / CAD spot price increased from 0.6602 to 0.7036, which is an increase of 6.58%. First, find the CAD / EUR cross quotes; S 0 = 1.4025 × 1.0800 = 1.5147; S 1 = 1.3600 × 1.0450 = 1.4212. Second, convert CAD to the base currency; S 0 = 1 / 1.5147 = 0.6602; S 1 = 1 / 1.4212 = 0.7036. Third, find the percentage change; (0.7036 / 0.6602) – 1 = 0.0658, or 6.58%. An alternative solution is to take (S 0 / S 1 ) − 1 from the original cross quote, which is essentially the same as converting CAD to the base currency and using (S 1 / S 0 ) – 1; (1.5147 / 1.4212) −1 = 0.0658, or 6.58%. A is incorrect because it assumes the percentage decline in the EUR is the percentage gain in the CAD; −[(1.4212 / 1.5147) – 1] = 0.0617, or 6.17%. B is incorrect because it fails to account for compounding and simply adds the percentage gain in USD against the EUR to the percentage gain in CAD against the USD; (1.4025 / 1.3600) – 1 = 0.03125; (1.0800 / 1.0450) – 1 = 0.03349; 0.03125 + 0.03349 = 0.0647, or 6.47%.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information: The CAD/EUR 12-month forward points are closest to:
questions.explanation: C is correct because the 12-month forward rate is first calculated, then followed by the forward points. The 12-month forward rate is (CAD/EUR) x ((1 + CAD interest rate) / (1 + EUR interest rate)) = 1.4356 x ((1 + 0.02)/(1 + 0.005)) ≈ 1.4570. The forward points is the difference between the forward rate and the spot rate, and scaled up by 10,000 = (1.4570 – 1.4356) x 10,000 = 214. A is incorrect because the 12-month forward rate is wrongly calculated. The 12-month forward rate is wrongly calculated as the domestic interest rate is used as numerator and the foreign interest rate is used as denominator. (CAD/EUR) x ((1 + EUR interest rate) / (1 + CAD interest rate)) = 1.4356 x ((1 + 0.005)/(1 + 0.02)) ≈ 1.4145. The forward points is the difference between the forward rate and the spot rate, and scaled up by 10,000 = (1.4145 – 1.4356) x 10000 = – 211. B is incorrect because the forward points are wrongly multiplied by 1,000, instead of 10,000. The 12-month forward rate is (CAD/EUR) x ((1 + interest rate of Canada) / (1 + interest rate of Europe)) = 1.4356 x ((1 + 0.02)/(1 + 0.005)) ≈ 1.4570. The forward points is the difference between forward rate and the spot rate, and scaled up wrongly by 1,000 = (1.4570 – 1.4356) x 1,000 ≈ 21.

questions.stem: Which of the following most likely presents information on the financial performance of a company's business activities over a period of time? The statement of:
questions.option_c: changes in equity
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[t]he income statement presents information on the financial performance of a company’s business activities over a period of time. It communicates how much revenue and other income the company generated during a period and the expenses it incurred to generate that revenue and other income. ... The income statement is sometimes referred to as a statement of operations or profit and loss (P&L) statement." B is incorrect because "[t]he balance sheet (also called the statement of financial position or statement of financial condition) presents a company’s financial position by disclosing the resources the company controls (assets) and its obligations to lenders and other creditors (liabilities) at a specific point in time." C is incorrect because "[t]he statement of changes in equity, sometimes called the “statement of changes in owners’ equity” or “statement of changes in shareholders’ equity,” primarily serves to report changes in the owners’ investment in the business over time. The basic components of owners’ equity are paid-in capital and retained earnings. Retained earnings include the cumulative amount of the company’s profits that have been retained in the company. In addition, non-controlling or minority interests and reserves that represent accumulated OCI items are included in equity. The latter items may be shown separately or included in retained earnings."

questions.stem: Which of the following most likely enforces financial reporting requirements?
questions.option_c: Accounting standards boards
questions.explanation: A is correct because "[a] distinction must be made between standard-setting bodies and regulatory authorities. Standard-setting bodies, such as the IASB and FASB, are typically private sector, self-regulated organizations with board members who are experienced accountants, auditors, users of financial statements, and academics. The requirement to prepare financial reports in accordance with specified accounting standards is the responsibility of regulatory authorities. Regulatory authorities, such as the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority in Singapore, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in the United States, and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Brazil have the legal authority to enforce financial reporting requirements and exert other controls over entities that participate in the capital markets within their jurisdiction. In other words, generally, standard-setting bodies set the standards and regulatory authorities recognize and enforce the standards." B is incorrect because "[t]he requirement to prepare financial reports in accordance with specified accounting standards is the responsibility of regulatory authorities... In other words, generally, standard-setting bodies set the standards and regulatory authorities recognize and enforce the standards." C is incorrect because the accounting standards boards are the standard setters: "[t]hese boards are typically independent, private, not-for-profit organizations. There are certain attributes that are typically common to these standard setters" while "[t]he requirement to prepare financial reports in accordance with specified accounting standards is the responsibility of regulatory authorities."

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a 2-year construction contract: Work performed provides an appropriate measure of progress towards completing the contract and the performance obligations are satisfied over time. Assuming it is highly probable that revenue will not be subsequently reversed, revenue recognized in Year 1 is:
questions.explanation: C is correct because "[t]he standard states that for performance obligations satisfied over time (e.g., where there is a long-term contract), revenue is recognized over time by measuring progress toward satisfying the obligation." In this case, works performed provide an appropriate measure of progress towards completing the contract. The construction company has performed 30% of the total works and will thus recognize €300,000 (30% × €1,000,000) in revenue for the first year. A is incorrect because in this case the construction company recognizes %Works performed in Year 1 × Estimated total costs [instead of the Contract price] = 30% × €800,000 = €240,000 in revenue for the first year. B is incorrect because this is the cash received which is not relevant for the purpose of determining the recognized revenue while "[t]he standard states that for performance obligations satisfied over time (e.g., where there is a long-term contract), revenue is recognized over time by measuring progress toward satisfying the obligation."

questions.stem: At year end, a company has non-convertible debt, ordinary shares, and employee stock options outstanding. The company’s capital structure is considered to be:
questions.option_a: complex, because the company has both debt and equity.
questions.option_b: complex, because the options are convertible into ordinary shares.
questions.option_c: simple, if the options are antidilutive.
questions.explanation: B is correct. When a company has issued any financial instruments that are potentially convertible into common stock, it is said to have a complex capital structure. Potentially convertible financial instruments include convertible bonds, convertible preferred stock, employee stock options, and warrants. Any antidilutive effect of a convertible security relates to the calculation of EPS and is not part of the distinction of simple vs. complex capital structure. A is incorrect because the existence of debt does not make the capital structure complex. The structure is complex because the employee stock options are convertible into ordinary shares. C is incorrect because a capital structure is considered complex if the company has issued any financial instruments that are potentially convertible into common stock, such as employee stock options. It does not matter if these instruments are antidilutive.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information (in € millions) about a company: Based only on this information, total comprehensive income (in € millions) is:
questions.explanation: C is correct because “Under IFRS, total comprehensive income is ''the change in equity during a period resulting from transaction and other events, other than those changes resulting from transactions with owners in their capacity as owners''. […] comprehensive income includes both net income and other revenue and expense items that are excluded from the net income calculation (other comprehensive income).” Other comprehensive income (OCI) = ending shareholder's equity – beginning shareholder's equity – net income + dividend declared and paid = 180 – 140 – 30 + 10 = 20. Total comprehensive income is net income + OCI = 30 + 20 = 50. A is incorrect because additional to ignoring net income and only using other comprehensive income (OCI) as total comprehensive income, it also ignores the dividends in the OCI calculation. The calculation becomes other comprehensive income = ending shareholders' equity – beginning shareholders' equity – net income = 180 – 140 – 30 = 10. B is incorrect because it ignores net income and only uses other comprehensive income as total comprehensive income. Other comprehensive income = ending shareholder's equity – beginning shareholder's equity – net income + dividend declared and paid = 180 – 140 – 30 + 10 = 20.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding balance sheets is correct?
questions.option_a: Equity stated on the balance sheet fairly represents a company’s intrinsic value as of the reporting date.
questions.option_b: Important aspects of a company’s ability to generate future cash flows are absent from its balance sheet.
questions.option_c: On the reporting date, shareholders’ equity is adjusted to account for changes in expectations about future market conditions.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Important aspects of a company’s ability to generate future cash flows—for example, its reputation and management skills—are not included in its balance sheet. A is incorrect because the balance sheet amount of equity should not be viewed as a measure of either the market value or the intrinsic value of a company’s equity for a variety of reasons. The balance sheet amount of equity will differ from the market value of equity because some assets and liabilities are measured at historical cost and others are measured at current value. Furthermore, the value of a company is a function of many factors, including future cash flows expected to be generated by the company and current market conditions. C is incorrect because owners’ equity is determined simply by subtracting the liabilities from the assets of a company.

questions.stem: Based on the presented information about a company’s trade receivables, the bad debt expense (in £ millions) for Year 2 is closest to:
questions.explanation: C is correct. The allowance for doubtful accounts increases by the bad debt expense recognized for the year and decreases by the amounts written off during the year. Solve for bad debt expense = £120 million. A is incorrect. It is just write offs, which is not the same as the expense. B is incorrect. It is just the increase in the allowance for the year (92 – 56 = 36) and ignores the write-offs that reduce the account.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the link between the cash flow statement and the balance sheet?
questions.option_a: The statement’s investing activities section reconciles the changes in current assets on the balance sheet.
questions.option_b: The cash flow statement reconciles the beginning and ending balances of cash reported on the balance sheet.
questions.option_c: The cash flow statement reconciles changes in all accounts on the balance sheet.
questions.explanation: B is correct. The statement of cash flows ultimately shows the change in cash during an accounting period. The company’s balance sheet shows the beginning and ending cash balances for the previous and current years, and the bottom of the cash flow statement reconciles beginning cash with ending cash. Non-cash changes in accounts may appear on the balance sheet; therefore, not all changes in the balance sheet are reconciled on the cash flow statement. A is incorrect. The changes in current assets are in the operating section of the CFS not the investing section. C is incorrect. There could be non-cash changes in accounts on the balance sheet therefore not all changes in the balance sheet are reconciled on the CFS.

questions.stem: A firm reports sales of €50,000 for the year ended 31 December 20X2. Its accounts receivable balances were €6,000 at 1 January 20X2 and €7,500 at 31 December 20X2. The company’s cash collections from sales for 20X2 is closest to:
questions.explanation: A is correct. Cash collections from sales equals beginning receivables plus sales less ending receivables: €6,000 + €50,000 – €7,500 = €48,500 B is incorrect. It is sales plus the change in receivables: €50,000 + (€7,500 – €6,000) = €51,500. C is incorrect. It is sales less the end receivables: €50,000 – €7,500 = €42,000.

questions.stem: The most appropriate statement about financial ratio analysis is that it has limited use as an analytical tool for:
questions.option_a: providing insights into microeconomic relationships within a company that help analysts project earnings.
questions.option_c: comparing companies that use different accounting methods.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Financial ratio analysis is limited by the use of alternative accounting methods. Accounting methods play an important role in the interpretation of financial ratios. The lack of consistency across companies makes comparability difficult to analyze and limits the usefulness of ratio analysis. A is incorrect. Financial ratios provide insights into microeconomic relationships within a company that help analysts project earnings and free cash flow. B is incorrect. Financial ratios are useful in providing evaluation of management.

questions.stem: Working capital turnover is most likely a(n):
questions.option_c: operating efficiency ratio.
questions.explanation: C is correct because the working capital turnover ratio is an activity ratio. “Activity ratios are also known as asset utilization ratios or operating efficiency ratios.” “Working capital turnover indicates how efficiently the company generates revenue with its working capital. ... A high working capital turnover ratio indicates greater efficiency (i.e., the company is generating a high level of revenues relative to working capital).” A is incorrect because the working capital turnover ratio is an activity ratio. “Activity ratios are also known as asset utilization ratios or operating efficiency ratios.” “Liquidity ratios measure a company's ability to meet its short-term obligations.” B is incorrect because the working capital turnover ratio is an activity ratio. “Activity ratios are also known as asset utilization ratios or operating efficiency ratios.” “Solvency ratios measure a company's ability to meet long-term obligations.”

questions.stem: An inventory system that reduces average inventory without affecting sales will most likely reduce the:
questions.option_c: cash conversion cycle.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A reduction in inventory will increase the inventory turnover (Cost of goods sold/Average inventory), which means that the days in inventory will be reduced (365/Inventory turnover). This will lead to a reduction in the cash conversion cycle (also called net operating cycle). Cash conversion cycle consists of number of days of inventory and number of days of receivables minus number of days of payables. A is incorrect. Quick ratio will increase as the result of efficient inventory system. B is incorrect. Inventory turnover will increase as the result of efficient inventory system.

questions.stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a company: Based only on this information, from Year 1 to Year 2, the company's ROE:
questions.option_c: increased.
questions.explanation: B is correct because "ROE = Net profit margin × Total asset turnover × Leverage" Accordingly, Year 1 ROE = 2.5% × 1.5 × 1.2 = 4.5%, and Year 2 ROE = 3.6% × 1.0 × 1.25 = 4.5%. Therefore, ROE remained the same from Year 1 to Year 2. A is incorrect because ROE remained the same from Year 1 to Year 2 instead of decreased. One possible way to calculate a decrease is to calculate ROE = (Net profit margin × Total asset turnover) / Leverage. Consequently, Year 1 ROE = (2.5% × 1.5) / 1.2 = 3.125%, and Year 2 ROE = (3.6% × 1.0) / 1.25 = 2.88%. C is incorrect because ROE remained the same from Year 1 to Year 2 instead of increased. One possible way to calculate an increase is to calculate ROE = (Net profit margin × Leverage) / Total asset turnover. Consequently, Year 1 ROE = (2.5% × 1.2) / 1.5 = 2.0%, and Year 2 ROE = (3.6% × 1.25) / 1.0 = 4.5%.

questions.stem: Which of the following inventory valuation methods best matches the actual historical cost of the inventory items sold to their physical flow?
questions.option_c: Specific identification
questions.explanation: C is correct. Specific identification best matches the physical flow of the inventory items because it tracks the actual units that are sold. A is incorrect. LIFO is based on cost flow assumptions but does not necessarily match the actual physical movement of the goods. B is incorrect. FIFO is based on cost flow assumptions but does not necessarily match the actual physical movement of the goods.

questions.stem: The following information for a company was taken from its financial statements and the accompanying notes: After adjusting for the LIFO liquidation in 20X4, the change in gross profit margin compared with 20X3 is most likely:
questions.option_c: lower by 2.3%.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Gross profit margin = (Sales – COGS)/Sales × 100 Gross profit under LIFO in 20X4 ($ thousands) = 11,159 – 9,898 = 1,261 This figure arose in part from the LIFO liquidation, which decreased COGS by $263,000 and hence increased gross profit. Adjusting the gross profit downward by this amount gives adjusted gross profit ($ thousands) of 1,261 – 263 = 998. Adjusted gross profit margin in 20X4 = (998/11,159) × 100 = 8.9% Gross profit margin in 20X3 = (8,895 – 7,901)/8,895 = 11.2% After adjusting for the LIFO liquidation, gross profit margin is lower by (11.2% – 8.9%) = 2.3%. A is incorrect. It makes no adjustment for the LIFO liquidation effect: 1,261/11,159 = 11.3%, which is 11.3% – 11.2% = 0.1% higher, unchanged as rounded. B is incorrect. It adds the decrease in COGS: (1,261 + 263)/11,159 = 13.7%, which is 13.7% – 11.2% = 2.5% higher.

questions.stem: A retailer that prepares its financial statements in accordance with IFRS has 100 office chairs in its inventory with a suggested retail price of $240 each, for which it paid a supplier an average of $200 a chair. Demand for the chairs has been low for quite a while, and in response the supplier has lowered its selling price to $160 each. However, the retailer estimates it can sell the chairs for $180 each if it offers free shipping to its customers. Shipping costs to the retailer are estimated to be $10 per chair, on average. The total carrying amount of these 100 office chairs on the retailer’s balance sheet is closest to:
questions.explanation: C is correct. IFRS measures inventory at lower of cost and net realizable value. Net realizable value under IFRS is defined as the estimated selling price less the estimated costs necessary to get the inventory ready for sale and make the sale: Selling price: $180 Costs to get ready to sell: $10 (Free shipping is required in order to sell these chairs at $180) Net realizable value per chair: $170 For 100 chairs: $17,000 A is incorrect. It uses the $160 replacement cost. B is incorrect. Costs (free shipping) to make a sale must be taken into consideration when determining net realizable value (not $180).

questions.stem: The entire cost of an intangible asset is most likely expensed when incurred if the asset is:
questions.option_c: purchased in a transaction other than a business combination.
questions.explanation: A is correct because "the costs to internally develop intangible assets are generally expensed when incurred.
